THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA by TOYOTA GROUP Reopens with New Exhibition Featuring Monet and Japanese Ukiyo-e
News Release
Events
			Download all images
	Early bird ticket sales begin today ahead of the October 24, 2026, reopening of THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA, featuring the new exhibition The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet.
	Toyota City, Japan, September 24, 2026―Last December, the Toyota Group, inspired by Yokohama's history and the city's vision for a "City of Cultural and Artistic Creation," opened THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA by TOYOTA GROUP ("THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA")*1 at Yamashita Pier as a venue offering "MOVE" through both movement and emotion. Visitors enjoyed an immersive experience combining stunning visuals and music in a vast space.
With this reopening, THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA will launch a new program, The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. This program focuses on the innovative artistic expressions created by ukiyo-e artists, including Katsushika Hokusai, and explores their influence on the Impressionist painter Claude Monet.
	In addition, Toyota's e-Palette*2 will provide transportation from the Yamashita Pier entrance to the venue at Shed No. 4. Building on the mobility experience that was well received by many visitors last time, automated driving trials are also planned for this reopening.
	In addition to immersive art exhibitions, THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA will offer art activities and workshops, and introduce the Toyota Group's cultural activities. By creating a space for cultural exchange open to the local community, Toyota aims to broaden opportunities for cultural experiences and generate synergies throughout the Yokohama area.The Toyota Group aims to go beyond simply providing transportation to deliver "MOVE" that touches people's hearts, thereby creating new opportunities for inspiration and learning through culture. We hope visitors will look forward to the new emotional "MOVE" experience that THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA has to offer.
Please see the official website (https://global.toyota/info/themoveum/) for more details and ticket information.

	About the Program
The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet
One of the key sources of inspiration that broadened the world of Monet's art was ukiyo-e prints from Japan. The unique compositions, views of nature, and aesthetics created by Hokusai, Hiroshige, Utamaro, and others offered Monet new perspectives in his ongoing exploration of changes in light and nature, enriching the breadth of expression in Impressionism. This exhibition allows visitors to experience art unbound, presenting the dialogue between Monet's works and Japanese art. It takes Impressionist paintings outside their frames to fill the entire space in a fusion of imagery, music, architecture, and sound. Rather than merely looking at the art, visitors can experience a new viewpoint born from the encounter between Japanese and European art as they wander through this world.
	Monet's dining room: the ukiyo-e space that entranced Monet
Monet lived in his house at Giverny from 1883 until the end of his life. The dining room, a space that grew to symbolize that house, was decorated with prints by Hokusai, Hiroshige, and Utamaro that Monet treasured. The venue showcases a space inspired by that room.
						* Image is for illustrative purposes only
	Ukiyo-e Gallery: Monet, Ukiyo-e, and the spaces between
Japanese ukiyo-e entranced Monet. This exhibit focuses on the bold compositions and richness of expression found in ukiyo-e, as well as the skills of the craftsmen who created these works. Through ukiyo-e depicting the lifestyles and cultures of the people of Edo, visitors can discover the depth of Japanese art that so fascinated Western artists when they first encountered it.
	Learning events for families (scheduled)
Family-oriented workshops and study programs are planned with the goal of fostering children's creativity through encounters with art and culture. Opportunities to combine cultural experiences with learning will be provided.
	LISTEN. ―WHITE NIGHT
LISTEN.―a sound time capsule woven for the future―has spent the past 10 years traveling the world to explore musical cultures and capturing these treasures of "sound" on film. In WHITE NIGHT, the latest installment in the ONE MOMENT series―which blends immersive art with music―we embark on a journey through the sounds of the North, which hold the secrets to survival.
"Let's "Encounter the Earth". Sing, play music, dance, laugh, and cultivate a brighter tomorrow."
―LISTEN. producer Tomoko Yamaguchi
	Profile of Tomoko Yamaguchi, LISTEN. producer
Tomoko Yamaguchi launched LISTEN., a 10-year project to explore music cultures around the world and compile them into a video library, in 2010. She has since produced short films and feature-length films. (https://www.the-listen-project.com)
In 2025, she held a LISTEN. exhibition at the "HOUSE OF MUSIC HUNGARY" in Budapest.
She published the book LISTEN. (Ikinobiru Books), which allows readers to "experience" music videos by scanning QR codes.
On her YouTube channel, Tomoko Yamaguchi KazeAna!?, she is currently sharing her journey of rediscovering the world. (https://www.youtube.com/@tomoko_yamaguchi)
	Special exhibition and video of winners of the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest
THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA is exhibiting winning works from the 19th Japan Contest of the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest. Visitors can see dream-filled works created from the free-spirited imaginations of children. At STUDIO, a special video is screened in which these award-winning works come to life as immersive imagery. We hope visitors will enjoy the worlds where children's imaginations soar.
	About the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest
With "Your Dream Car" as its theme, this art contest, held by Toyota Motor Corporation, invites children to use their imaginations to create their visions of future mobility.https://www.toyota-dreamcarart.com/

Toyota Signs TEAM JAPAN Partnership Agreement with JOC and JPC as a Gold Partner, Directly Supporting Athletes Competing on the World Stage
News Release
Management
	Toyota City, Japan, September 18, 2026―Toyota Motor Corporation (Toyota) signed a TEAM JAPAN Partnership Agreement with the Japanese Olympic Committee (JOC) and the Japanese Paralympic Committee (JPC) as a Gold Partner. Toyota will help create an environment in which Japanese athletes competing on the world stage can focus on their sport and perform at their best.
	Toyota's Commitment to Sports
Toyota's strong commitment to sports can be traced back to its early days.Ever since founder Kiichiro Toyoda established a sports club alongside the company's automotive operations, sports have gone hand in hand with Toyota's corporate activities.
   Never Give Up, Challenge, Teamwork, Respect
Never giving up until the end and continuing to take on challenges. Fighting for your teammates and respecting your opponents. Toyota has long associated these sporting values with its identity and cherished them.
Today, Toyota supports athletes from Toyota Motor Corporation's sports clubs and Group companies, as well as athletes competing around the world as Global Team Toyota Athletes (GTTA).
Underlying this support is a desire to help athletes as they strive toward their goals and continue taking on challenges, rather than focusing solely on wins, losses, and medals.
	What This Partnership Aims to Achieve
Toyota's priority in this partnership is ensuring that support truly reaches athletes. Working closely with JOC and JPC, Toyota will listen first to athletes and individual sports federations. It will also consider areas where support is less readily available and work to create an environment in which each athlete can continue taking on challenges. This includes providing sports federations with support for athlete development and reducing the burden of travel for international competitions and training camps.
	Looking Ahead
Athletes' challenges do not begin and end with competition periods. Toyota aims to remain by their side throughout the long journey toward the world stage as they train each day, travel to competitions, and overcome various difficulties.
Toyota will use this year's 20th Asian Games and 5th Asian Para Games as an opportunity to broaden the circle of support for athletes and continue supporting Japanese athletes who take on the world as TEAM JAPAN.
The sight of athletes taking on challenges brings hope and motivation to society and inspires the next generation to take a step forward.
Together with JOC and JPC, Toyota will support the future of sports and athletes.

Jun. 01, 2026
Toyota Announces New Exhibition at the Toyota Kaikan Museum"TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking" presents Toyota's pursuit of ever-better cars guided by the founding principle of "for the benefit of others"
Interest
Related Facilities
			Download all images
	Toyota City, Japan―June 1, 2026―Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC) has added a new exhibition space to the Toyota Kaikan Museum,* a corporate exhibition hall located in Toyota City. Titled "TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking," the new section will open to the public on Friday, June 5. The immersive exhibits feature real vehicles and visual displays that guide visitors through each stage of Toyota's long-established carmaking process, from vehicle planning and development to procurement, production, and customer delivery.
            *
            The Toyota Kaikan Museum was established in 1977 to commemorate TMC's 40th anniversary. The museum showcases Toyota's corporate philosophy and latest automotive technologies. It has received over 17 million visitors, including those who visited Toyota Hall, its predecessor, which opened in 1960.
	The Japanese automotive industry is widely known for its creative manufacturing processes, including kaizen activities that drive continuous improvement on the production line. To pass this manufacturing philosophy and these processes on to future generations, TMC introduced the Toyota Virtual Plant Tour on its website in 2023 as a comprehensive guide to the car manufacturing process. The new exhibition space builds on this initiative. After introducing the origin of Toyota's passion for manufacturing, the exhibition takes a close look at the entire carmaking process―from vehicle planning and development to production and logistics. The exhibition is divided into three zones, each presenting a multifaceted perspective through real vehicles and dynamic visuals.
	Zone 1: The Inspiration for TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking
Toyota's approach to creative carmaking was inspired by Sakichi Toyoda, the founder of the Toyota Group and the father of Kiichiro Toyoda, who founded TMC. As a young boy, Sakichi wanted to ease his mother's work burden. His commitment to "for the benefit of others" continues to inspire TMC employees today, as does the slogan "Let's Make Ever-Better Cars," introduced in 2009 by Akio Toyoda, the current TMC chairman. United by these enduring visions, TMC employees pursue creative carmaking every day.
Kiichiro Toyoda aimed to establish the automobile industry as the foundation of Japan's economic development. "With Japanese ideas and skills, we must create an automobile industry for Japan," he declared before successfully completing the Toyoda Model AA, Toyota's first passenger car. Zone 1 features a concept video on the origins of Toyota's carmaking philosophy, together with a one-eighth scale model of the Toyoda Model AA.
	Zone 2: Let's Make Ever-Better Cars (Vehicle Development)
One of Toyota's distinctive approaches to carmaking is its organizational style, which grants chief engineers extensive responsibility over their respective models, covering planning, development, production, and sales. This exhibit zone uses graphics, videos, and figures, and special lighting effects to show how teams unite under the chief engineer's leadership. The exhibition uses the fifth-generation Prius released in 2023 as a case study. Through real vehicles and life-size video presentations, the exhibition presents behind-the-scenes development episodes and demonstrates how engineering, production, and sales personnel worked closely together throughout the development process.
	Zone 3: Experience the Wonder and Craftsmanship of Toyota's Manufacturing Plants (Production)
This exhibit zone uses graphics to illustrate the basic production flow, including stamping, welding, painting, assembly, inspection, and logistics. Real disassembled parts and welding robots complement the displays. In addition, visitors can experience dynamic plant operations in an immersive theater, together with large-screen production line footage from the workers' perspective.
	Through this exhibition, we hope to convey the appeal of automobiles and the spirit of carmaking and monozukuri that underpin them to people of all ages, and to contribute to promoting automobiles as part of Japanese culture.

        Broadcom Introduces VMware HyperArmor, Expanding Hypervisor Security and Protections for VMware Cloud Foundation
  PDF Version
                    VMware HyperArmor offers unique, proactive zero day protection to VMware Cloud Foundation environments with no downtime, software upgrades, or in-guest agentsPALO ALTO, Calif., Oct.  13, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO), a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, today introduced VMware HyperArmor, a new software solution to help further protect the VMware ESX hypervisor component of VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) against the exponential increase in cyber attack sophistication by closing exposure windows without disrupting the workloads that depend on the host.  "Frontier AI has changed the three V's of cybersecurity threats - the volume, velocity, and variety. When attacks come at machine speed, reactive detection and patching are no longer enough," said Paul Turner, chief product officer, VMware Cloud Foundation Division, Broadcom. "VMware HyperArmor takes a different approach by allowing only what is 'known good' to run on the host. With VMware vDefend already delivering virtual patching capabilities for the network layer of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware HyperArmor now expands that protection around the hypervisor component itself."   As AI-accelerated threats grow in scale and sophistication, the threat surface now extends across every layer of the infrastructure stack including the hypervisor. Two problems account for most hypervisor attacks: stolen root credentials and unpatched vulnerabilities. VMware HyperArmor addresses both problems, with support for VMware ESX 8.x and later releases, as follows:  Virtual patching for VCF’s ESX Component Host Environment. HyperArmor delivers host-layer virtual patching to shield ESX by detecting and blocking attempted malicious actions within the host nodes before any vulnerabilities can be exploited. These host-level virtual patching capabilities complement the network-layer virtual patching available for VCF via VMware vDefend. Because virtual patching of ESX does not require host reboots or software upgrades to mitigate vulnerabilities, security teams will benefit from dramatically reduced risk windows and IT teams gain more operational flexibility to test and apply official patches on the schedule they prefer.Positive Host Security Guardrails. HyperArmor protects the host at the infrastructure layer, with no agents inside guest virtual machines (VMs). An ESX host runs a small, fixed set of processes. HyperArmor establishes a positive security baseline and automatically blocks any unauthorized executable or script. HyperArmor takes an inventory of scripts already on the host and allows them automatically, and administrators can approve new ones. The result is continuous monitoring and compliance enforcement with minimal performance overhead.Hypervisor-level multi-factor authentication (MFA). HyperArmor integrates MFA functionality directly into the ESX SSH login path. Logging in requires two steps: standard SSH credentials, followed by a secondary time-based one-time password challenge tied to a separately defined identity. Even if an attacker obtains the root password through phishing or credential leaks, they cannot reach the command line without that second factor.  “Attackers are using automation and AI to exploit infrastructure weaknesses faster than most organizations can patch, which means layered defense must extend all the way to the hypervisor as the foundation of the private cloud,” said Stephen Elliot, Group Vice President, Software Development and IT Operations, IDC. “Technology leaders should prioritize preventive controls that help shrink exposure windows without disrupting production, and approaches that harden the virtualization layer natively rather than relying on external agents or post-incident detection.”   Defense in Depth Across VMware Cloud Foundation  VMware HyperArmor works alongside the broader security capabilities in VMware Cloud Foundation to deliver an integrated and multi-layered approach. VMware Cloud Foundation is hardened out of the box with key capabilities that include centralized identity management, data-at-rest and data-in-transit encryption, and VMware vSphere live patching, which applies critical updates to the hypervisor without taking workloads down or placing hosts into full maintenance mode. VMware HyperArmor adds a proactive layer of protection for the hypervisor by blocking process execution exploits and credential theft. VMware vDefend delivers strong lateral security with micro-segmentation and advanced threat detection and prevention for VCF workloads, which uses deep traffic inspection to block emerging exploits and to deliver network-level virtual patching. VMware Avi Load Balancer provides web application and API protection (WAAP) for securing web and API traffic. Together, these layers give customers defense in depth across the infrastructure, network, and hypervisor.                     Company to Highlight OCP Rack-Based Innovations Enabling Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across Networks Across AI ClustersPALO ALTO, Calif., Oct.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO), a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, today announced it is set to present its latest innovations in scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across AI networking at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit. Running from October 12–15 in San Jose, Broadcom will feature Ethernet switches, NICs, PCIe components and integrated optics to power Open Rack Version 3 (ORV3) solutions for scaling AI infrastructure.  Featured innovations include Tomahawk® 6, Tomahawk Ultra, and Jericho 4 Ethernet switches, the Thor Ultra 800G and Thor 2 400G AI Ethernet NICs, and Broadcom's third-generation TH6-Davisson Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) — a portfolio built to meet the exponential bandwidth demands of frontier AI models as they grow in scale and complexity.  "Together, the OCP Community and Broadcom have a long history of driving computing at massive scale, and this year’s event theme—'Scaling Innovation for the AI Era'—underscores the growing importance of open collaboration. AI infrastructure demands are scaling faster than anything our industry has seen, and Ethernet is the foundation that makes that growth sustainable. With our industry-leading portfolio of networking solutions and new breakthroughs in integrated optics, Broadcom is giving AI labs, hyperscalers and cloud providers the bandwidth and power efficiency they need to scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across next-generation AI clusters,” said Charlie Kawwas, Ph. D., president, Semiconductor Solutions Group, Broadcom.  “The current pace of AI data center infrastructure development depends on an open ecosystem that can support rapid innovation. The OCP Foundation with its unique collaborative model, Chip-to-Grid vision, and large collaborative community is the perfect place to nurture open ecosystems for the rapidly evolving AI data center industry. Broadcom has been a longstanding contributor to OCP, and we appreciate the technologies and contributions they're bringing to this year's Summit that leverage the open collaborations of the OCP Community, from ORV3 rack-based designs to advances in ORW (wide) racks and new wide co-packaged optics, that reflect exactly the kind of collaboration our Community needs to solve the bandwidth and efficiency challenges facing AI data centers at scale,” said George Tchaparian, CEO, Open Compute Project Foundation. Khamisy will also address challenges in building switch hardware for AI networks and share innovations that deliver greater bandwidth, reliability, and efficiency for distributed AI computing.         AST Completes Singapore's First High-End FC-BGA Substrate Facility to Meet Growing AI Chip Demand
  PDF Version
                    First Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FC-BGA) substrate production facility in SingaporeAddresses one of the most critical supply chain capacity constraints of the semiconductor industry Diversifies Singapore’s semiconductor ecosystem beyond current wafer fab, IC design and assembly operations. 29 September 2026, SINGAPORE – Advanced Substrate Technologies (AST) today announced the official opening of its new manufacturing facility in Singapore, the first in the country capable of producing high-end Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FC-BGA) substrates, and the TOPPAN Group’s first such facility outside Japan. The milestone comes as demand for advanced substrate capacity, a persistent bottleneck for AI, networking, and next-generation computing chips, continues to outpace global supply. AST is a joint venture between TOPPAN Holdings Inc. and Broadcom Inc. A delegation of AST executives, including key partners from the TOPPAN Group and Broadcom  welcomed Mr Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade), alongside other partners and guests to the opening ceremony. “AST’s ability to deliver large-body, high-layer-count substrates at TOPPAN's exacting standard is helping meet a real bottleneck in AI and networking chip production,” said Yoshiyuki Iida, CEO, AST. “We are grateful for the longstanding support and partnership of the Singapore government in this venture. This investment reflects both TOPPAN and Broadcom’s long-term commitment to Singapore as a critical hub in our global manufacturing network and strengthens the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain.”The approximately 95,000-square-metre facility is designed to meet the growing demand for generative AI and data centres in the region featuring sustainability elements such as solar panels and advanced water recycling technologies. The Singapore production base also complements TOPPAN’s main production hub in Niigata, Japan, and will manufacture large-body, high-layer-count substrates for advanced semiconductor products, including AI compute and networking devices. Since breaking ground in March 2024, AST has already hired more than 200 high-tech engineers and skilled technicians, in addition to operational personnel in Singapore. The facility also houses R&D capabilities to meet future performance demands, alongside close collaborations with technology institutions in Singapore. “Singapore continues to be an attractive destination and gateway to the global semiconductor industry for us, especially with a strong ecosystem of innovation, capabilities and resources,” said Satoshi Oya, President & COO, TOPPAN Holdings. “TOPPAN looks forward to continuing to drive advanced semiconductor packaging forward as artificial intelligence accelerates across the board.” The project is supported by Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) and JTC Corporation, which have played a key role in enabling the facility's establishment. “AST’s facility will boost Singapore’s capabilities in advanced substrates, which is a critical enabler for advanced packaging, and strengthen our position in the global semiconductor value chain,” said Png Cheong Boon, Chairman, Singapore Economic Development Board. “Singapore has served as an important base for Broadcom and TOPPAN. We are glad that both companies are growing their manufacturing and R&D presence here through AST. EDB will continue to work with both companies and AST to build new capabilities to support global demand for semiconductors, and create new jobs and opportunities here.” JTC Ms Jacqueline Poh, Chief Executive of JTC Corporation, said: “Advanced substrates are increasingly critical to the semiconductor value chain as AI and high-performance computing drive demand. JTC is pleased to support Broadcom and TOPPAN in establishing this new facility in Jurong and will continue to work with industry partners to provide the infrastructure needed for next generation semiconductor manufacturing in Singapore.”  As TOPPAN's largest customer for FC-BGA substrates, Broadcom has closely supported the facility's development, reflecting the strategic importance of additional large-body, high-layer-count substrate capacity to its next-generation AI compute and networking product roadmap. “AST's FC-BGA substrate capacity in Singapore gives us meaningful flexibility and differentiation as demand for AI and networking silicon continues to climb. This facility, brought online three months early, strengthens our supply chain resilience by delivering vital relief while the industry is constrained by substrate shortages,” said Charlie Kawwas, Ph.D., president, Semiconductor Solutions Group, Broadcom. “Thanks to the exceptional execution by TOPPAN and AST, alongside the continued partnership of the Singapore EDB, this facility will deliver the next generation of large-body, high-layer-count substrates that Broadcom requires to further scale global AI infrastructure.”Located in the Jurong Lake District, AST’s facility is targeting the start of high-value manufacturing by late-2026, with ongoing recruitment across engineering and technical roles. The company will work closely with TOPPAN and Broadcom to scale the output as demand for advanced substrates grows across AI, networking, and next-generation computing applications.ABOUT ADVANCED SUBSTRATE TECHNOLOGIES (AST)Advanced Substrate Technologies Pte. Ltd. (AST) is a Singapore-based joint venture between TOPPAN Holdings Inc. and Broadcom Inc., specialising in the design and manufacturing of advanced Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FC-BGA) substrates. Based near Jurong Lake District, AST is at the forefront of developing high-quality substrates for cutting-edge semiconductor applications, including network switches and AI/ML devices. For more information, please see: https://ast-sg.com/  ABOUT the TOPPAN GroupEstablished in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading global provider of integrated solutions spanning printing, communications, security, packaging, and electronics. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals. In Singapore, the TOPPAN Group has maintained a critical strategic hub for regional growth and high-tech innovation  for many years. Through its Singapore-based subsidiaries, including Advanced Substrate Technologies (AST), the TOPPAN Group is launching the country’s first flip chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrate manufacturing facility to directly anchor advanced semiconductor packaging, artificial intelligence (AI), and next-generation data centre supply chains across the Asia-Pacific region. For more information, visit https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en. ABOUT BROADCOM Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO) is a technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductors and infrastructure software for global organizations’ complex, mission-critical needs. Broadcom combines long-term R&D investment with superb execution to deliver the best technology, at scale. Broadcom is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, CA. For more information, visit www.broadcom.com.

Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
        Oct 13, 2026 at 12:45 PM EDT
  PDF Version
  Company expects strong multi-year growth as global AI infrastructure buildout fuels demand for leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging – areas where Applied has built market leadership
  Expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow faster through 2030 than over the past decade; targets more than 2 percentage points of WFE share gain from calendar 2025 to 2030
  Targets higher profitability through 2030 with non-GAAP gross margin target of approximately 54 percent and non-GAAP operating margin target of approximately 40 percent
  Committed to distribute 80 to 100 percent of free cash flow to shareholders over time
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct.  13, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- At its 2026 SEMICON West Investor Breakfast Presentation held today, Applied Materials, Inc. presented its longer-term growth expectations and outlined how its leadership in materials engineering positions the company to outperform the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market over the coming years.
“The global buildout of AI infrastructure is driving a new era of growth for wafer fab equipment,” said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Applied Materials has built leadership in the fastest growing areas of the market that have the greatest impact on AI computing performance, power efficiency and cost, and our advanced services offerings enable chipmakers to increase yield and fab output. Our industry-leading capabilities position Applied for continued growth and outperformance in the years ahead.”
The race for AI computing leadership requires tremendous technology innovation and capacity expansion to support infrastructure scaling, which is fueling sustained WFE investments – bigger than any of the industry’s past growth drivers. The growth and diversity of AI applications from generative to agentic and physical AI require increasing amounts of silicon. Applied expects leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to drive around 75 percent of WFE growth from 2025-2030. Applied has strong number-one process equipment positions in all three areas and is targeting to gain more than 2 percentage points of WFE market share from calendar 2025 to 2030.
To support the industry’s capacity expansion, Applied is utilizing its unique eBeam technology and advanced service solutions to help chipmakers accelerate the ramp of new process nodes and optimize yield, output and cost in high-volume manufacturing. With the industry’s highest resolution and fastest imaging capabilities, Applied’s eBeam equipment portfolio is expected to generate $2 billion in revenue in calendar year 2026. The company is expecting service revenue to grow more than 20 percent this calendar year and to exceed $12 billion in revenue by calendar year 2030, representing a mid-teens compound annual growth rate.
“For the past 10 years, Applied Materials has been making strategic investments to build the industry’s most enabling portfolio for AI computing,” said Brice Hill, Senior Vice President and CFO. “As AI drives wafer fab equipment growth, we are focused on further increasing profitability and operating leverage while investing in R&D programs that will fuel our outperformance into the future.”
Based on the company’s expectations for semiconductor industry growth, Applied is investing to more than double its R&D lab and manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2030. The company yesterday unveiled its new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Silicon Valley, the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. To date, Applied has announced 15 EPIC Center partnerships with leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and universities. Applied has also recently expanded its manufacturing infrastructure in Austin, Texas, Singapore and Treviso, Italy.

Management uses non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate the company’s operating and financial performance and for planning purposes, and as performance measures in its executive compensation program. Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era
        Oct 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
  PDF Version
                $5 billion investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facilityPurpose-built to accelerate the path from breakthrough innovation to high-volume manufacturing of next-generation chipmaking technologiesLeading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC SUNNYVALE, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc., the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a $5 billion capital investment* to build the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. Inside the EPIC Center, leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and university researchers will work side by side with Applied’s scientists and engineers to accelerate the pace of chip innovation for the AI era.“As AI infrastructure scales, the demands of high-performance computing are driving unprecedented complexity across the chipmaking roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials. “To win the race for AI leadership, our industry must rethink and re-engineer how we collaborate to develop and commercialize the next generation of semiconductor technologies. At EPIC, the world’s leading chipmakers, system designers, equipment partners and researchers will work side by side with our teams to accelerate the path from breakthrough materials innovation to high-volume manufacturing faster than ever before.”Purpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and CommercializationUnveiled today at Applied’s Sunnyvale, California, campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two Eiffel Towers. Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.EPIC is designed to reinvent the R&D model the industry has relied on for decades. In the traditional model, foundational materials research happens in one environment, equipment and process development in another, and process integration and pilot production in a third, with a careful handoff at every phase. The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization.EPIC is founded on a simple conviction: the technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone. The EPIC Center opens with a founding roster that spans the AI technology stack. Founding partners TSMC, Intel, SK hynix, Micron and Samsung Electronics are joined by innovation partners Broadcom, Advantest, SCREEN, KIOXIA, and Besi; and by research partners Arizona State University, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UCLA Samueli School of Engineering. Each partner brings its own roadmap challenges and engineers into the facility, working in tight, secure learning cycles alongside Applied teams. Over time, additional companies and organizations are expected to join the EPIC ecosystem.Leaders from many of the EPIC Center partner companies attended the unveiling event, getting a first glimpse inside the facility. The day started with a summit hosted by Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials, where R&D leaders from top semiconductor design, manufacturing and equipment companies discussed key challenges facing growth and progress in the global chip industry.“Materials innovation has outgrown serial development – at today’s atomic-scale dimensions, many materials and materials interfaces behave in entirely new ways, and making them work at industry scale demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” said Dr. Prabu Raja. “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies. Because our customers’ own engineers help optimize the technology before it ever reaches their factory, what leaves EPIC arrives at the fab ready to ramp to high performance and high yield sooner.”Applied expects the EPIC operating model to deliver returns on both sides of the partnerships. Chipmakers gain earliest access to next-generation materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. Applied gains visibility across several generations of emerging technology challenges, informing where the company directs its R&D investments to create value for customers and have its systems and services designed in.Supporting Quotes from Industry and Academic Leaders“For three decades, TSMC and Applied Materials have grown together – pushing the boundaries of semiconductor technology through every major transition. Thirty years ago, the leading-edge production node was 350 nanometers. Today, it is 2 nanometers. Working hand-in-hand with the industry, we have shrunk features 175-fold. As chipmaking complexity grows exponentially, our partnership is more vital than ever. Beyond 2nm, collaborating with Applied gives us early access to the disruptive equipment technologies that define the future. This fast-tracks the leap from R&D to high-volume manufacturing for the energy-efficient AI architectures of tomorrow – including new architecture, low-resistance wiring, and advanced packaging. We are proud to be a founding partner of EPIC, accelerating the innovations that will power AI from the data center to the edge.” – Dr. C.C. Wei, Chairman and CEO of TSMC“AI is creating a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity for the semiconductor industry. To capture it, we need continued innovation in transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging. At Intel, we see a path to more than a trillion transistors in a package by 2030. As architectures become more complex and R&D costs continue to rise, we need to move faster and work more closely with our equipment partners. EPIC gives our teams the opportunity to work side by side with Applied on materials and process innovation – helping us accelerate development, improve R&D efficiency and bring new technologies to market faster.” – Lip-Bu Tan, CEO, Intel“Data-intensive AI workloads are driving massive demand for high-performance memory and storage, and innovation in materials and process technology is a critical enabler of next-generation memory. As a founding partner of EPIC, Micron will work side by side with Applied Materials to accelerate innovation and bring next-generation memory technologies from research to high-volume manufacturing at scale.” – Sanjay Mehrotra, Chairman and CEO, Micron Technology“The defining challenge of AI computing is moving data fast enough to keep increasingly powerful processors fully utilized, and meeting that challenge requires memory with far greater bandwidth, speed and capacity. At EPIC, SK hynix and Applied will bring together our leadership in advanced memory with Applied’s leadership in materials engineering and semiconductor manufacturing technology to address major inflections across HBM, DRAM and NAND, and accelerate memory innovation for the AI era.” – Nohjung Kwak, President and CEO of SK hynix“Samsung takes an end-to-end view of AI-era computing – across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. Applied Materials brings uniquely broad process equipment leadership across all three domains, and at EPIC together we will develop, iterate and deploy breakthrough technologies faster than ever, at the pace AI scaling demands.” – Jaihyuk Song, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Device Solutions Division, Samsung Electronics“The next frontier of AI will be defined by how seamlessly the industry can integrate vast amounts of compute, memory and connectivity into high-performance systems, and that depends on breakthrough advances in advanced packaging. As an innovation partner at EPIC, Broadcom can engage earlier with Applied’s foundational technologies and manufacturing capabilities, connecting future system requirements to the packaging innovations needed to realize them and accelerating the path from concept to commercialization.” – Charlie Kawwas, Ph.D., President of Semiconductor Solutions Group, Broadcom“Future performance improvements will depend on advanced 3D architectures and heterogeneous integration. As these technologies converge, it becomes increasingly important to connect insights from front-end process development with those from back-end test and measurement. EPIC breaks down these traditional barriers by bringing together Applied Materials’ leadership in materials engineering and process control with Advantest's leadership in semiconductor test and measurement, including capabilities enabled through the Advantest Innovation Center. Together, we are helping the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers improve yield, accelerate production ramps, and bring next-generation AI systems to market faster.” – Doug Lefever, Representative Director and Group CEO, Advantest Corporation“At EPIC, we have a unique opportunity to co-optimize the critical wet and dry processes behind next-generation chip architectures. We can together accelerate the innovations required to master increasingly complex 3D devices and advanced packaging structures. By driving tighter process integration with materials engineering, we can help chipmakers unlock higher yields, faster production ramps, and the manufacturing scale required for the AI future.” – Masato Goto, President and CEO, SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd.“AI is making the world increasingly data-driven, and future breakthroughs will depend on memory, logic, and interconnect technologies working seamlessly within integrated systems. We believe the EPIC Center provides a powerful platform for collaboration across technology domains. By working closely with Applied Materials engineers and other partners, we can accelerate the development of next-generation memory technologies.” – Hideshi Miyajima, Ph.D., Managing Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer, KIOXIA Corporation“The future of AI depends not only on more powerful chips, but on the chip-to-chip interconnects that drive performance, bandwidth and power efficiency. Besi and Applied recognized early that hybrid bonding would be foundational to next-generation AI systems, and by combining Besi’s leadership in precision die-to-wafer bonding with Applied’s leadership in front-end processing, we are advancing hybrid bonding technology to enable future high-performance 3D integrated devices. EPIC extends that model of high-velocity co-innovation across the ecosystem, accelerating the technologies that will shape future AI systems.” – Richard Blickman, President and CEO, BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi)“ASU has developed a very strong working relationship with Applied Materials through the Materials-to-Fab Center at ASU Research Park, and we are excited to dig deeper into this partnership at the EPIC Center, where researchers, engineers and manufacturers converge to accelerate bold ideas from the lab to breakthroughs in the fab. EPIC will also serve as a cornerstone for the semiconductor talent pipeline and by working alongside Applied’s scientists and engineers, our students will gain the systems-level perspective needed to drive the future of AI innovation.” – Michael Crow, President, Arizona State University“UC Berkeley has helped shape microelectronics from its earliest days, advancing the research and talent that continue to propel the semiconductor industry, and our collaboration with Applied Materials is a great example of how academia and industry must work together to meet the scale and opportunity of what’s ahead. The EPIC platform gives our researchers access to the same cutting-edge capabilities used by the world’s leading chipmakers, within a manufacturing-relevant environment, so ideas can be tested, refined and transformed much faster into the semiconductor breakthroughs that will advance the frontier of AI.” – Rich Lyons, Chancellor, UC Berkeley“Many of the technologies powering today’s AI revolution began in university labs years, often decades, before they transformed the world. As computing demand increases, we must accelerate the pace at which new semiconductor materials, devices and integration technologies move from discovery to deployment. As an inaugural research partner at the EPIC Center, RPI’s students and researchers gain access to world-class experts and a direct pathway to test and validate academic advances in real-world production environments – a powerful blueprint for high-velocity industry-academia collaboration in the AI era.” – Martin Schmidt, President of RPI“The explosive growth of AI is pushing semiconductor technology researchers to find new ways to increase energy efficiency of semiconductor chips. Opportunities abound in discovering new materials and inventing new devices. Experimentation demands faster cycles of innovation and closer collaboration across the ecosystem. Beyond the existing broad research engagement between Stanford faculty and Applied Materials, the EPIC Center presents an additional opportunity that enables our students and researchers to engage directly with industry-scale tools and experts, accelerating discovery while gaining the industry-relevant experience needed to lead future advances in semiconductor manufacturing.” – H.S. Philip Wong, Willard R. and Inez Kerr Bell Professor in the School of Engineering, Stanford University“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before. UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and our collaboration with Applied Materials at the EPIC Center builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.” – Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and Valerie Sugar Dean of UCLA Samueli*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence.Forward-Looking StatementsThis press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding Applied’s investment and growth strategies, the development of new materials and technologies, industry outlook and technology requirements, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, and other statements that are not historical facts. Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
        Oct 8, 2026 at 4:05 PM EDT
  PDF Version
  R&D programs to focus on speeding up the commercialization pipeline so chip technology moves from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing faster
  Collaborative work at the state-of-the-art facility in Silicon Valley pairs UCLA’s semiconductor research strength with Applied’s cutting-edge chipmaking equipment and process integration expertise
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --  Applied Materials, Inc. today announced that the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering will join the company’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley as a research partner. Together with Applied’s scientists and engineers, UCLA researchers will work to solve semiconductor materials and integration challenges with a focus on shortening the time it takes to bring breakthrough research to commercialization.
“As the industry races to bring new AI chip technologies to market, the EPIC Center will play a pivotal role by convening the industry’s top innovators in a collaborative environment designed to accelerate the path from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “UCLA has a long history of semiconductor technology innovation and Applied looks forward to welcoming their researchers to the EPIC Center where together we will work to solve the industry’s toughest challenges.”
The EPIC Center aims to accelerate chip R&D by bridging the gap between traditional academic innovation and industrial-scale development. UCLA researchers will have access to advanced chipmaking tools so that new ideas can be validated and tested in a commercial fab environment, thereby shortening the path from concept to production.
UCLA Samueli brings extensive expertise across semiconductor devices, materials, electronics and computing. In 1991, Henry Samueli co-founded Broadcom Corporation while teaching at UCLA. The school is also home to the Center for Heterogeneous Integration and Performance Scaling (CHIPS) Lab, which brings together researchers across disciplines to advance semiconductor technologies and address challenges in chip design, manufacturing and integration.
By collaborating at the EPIC Center, Applied Materials and UCLA will focus R&D programs on the semiconductor industry’s most critical challenges in areas including 3D chip scaling, advanced packaging and the discovery of new materials for improving energy-efficient AI compute performance. The work will complement and extend the efforts of UCLA’s Semiconductor Hub, which Applied joined as a co-founding member earlier this year. Applied’s ongoing commitment to strengthen the ties between industry and academia is aimed at empowering the next generation of engineers and researchers to bring semiconductor breakthroughs to market faster.
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before,” said Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and Valerie Sugar Dean of UCLA Samueli. “UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and this collaboration builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S. investment in advanced semiconductor equipment R&D. The center is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. The facility is on track to become operational in 2026. Visit the EPIC Center website to learn more.

Press Release
Oracle Extends Fusion Agentic Applications with Introduction of Fusion Claw
New governed agentic execution runtime enables Oracle Fusion Agentic Applications to complete highly complex work more autonomously at scale
25 Claw-powered Fusion Agentic Applications are now available to help organizations drive business outcomes with built-in, enterprise-grade governance and security controls
Austin, Texas—Sep 29, 2026
Oracle today announced Oracle Fusion Claw, a governed agentic execution runtime for Oracle Fusion Agentic Applications that combines AI reasoning with deterministic enterprise computation to enable highly complex work to be economically completed at scale. Oracle Fusion Applications customers can take advantage of Fusion Claw through 25 new Claw-powered agentic applications that can reason, compute, adapt, and execute specialist-grade work including deep research, computation, simulation, modeling, and continuous re-planning. The new Claw-powered Agentic Applications are the latest additions to the growing portfolio of 75 Agentic Applications that can coordinate and execute end-to-end business processes.
“Every organization is looking at AI and asking the same question: how can we use it to create measurable value for our business?” said Mike Sicilia, CEO, Oracle. “Fusion Claw helps answer that question by moving from AI assistance to execution, enabling customers to automate increasingly complex work across their most important business processes, with enterprise-grade governance. By letting AI take on more of the work, while people set the objectives and guardrails, organizations can unlock tremendous capacity for their teams to focus more on driving growth, innovation, and serving customers.”
Agentic Applications represent a new class of outcome-based applications that provide Fusion Applications customers with a system of outcomes, where people define the objectives, authority, and accountability and the Agentic Applications coordinate the process to get to an outcome. Fusion Claw enables Agentic Applications to take on more complex, specialist-grade work by providing a new execution runtime that supports larger scale and longer-running work, continuous replanning, deterministic execution, and increased governed autonomy. Each Claw Outcome begins with a frontier model that reasons, plans, learns, and adapts. Fusion Claw then uses deterministic enterprise computation to execute precisely and at scale. This separation provides Fusion Applications customers with a potential economic advantage by applying AI reasoning only where intelligence is needed and using efficient deterministic computation for high-volume execution.
To govern autonomous enterprise execution, Fusion Claw applies an Enterprise Operating Envelope, which includes an organization’s objectives, standard operating procedures, policies, constraints, permissions, risk thresholds, decision rights, approval requirements, and escalation boundaries. The operating envelope is enforced across all outcomes through an Outcome Trust Harness that applies specific governing authority and controls to each outcome run, including identity, capabilities, data, and actions. When the outcome is complete, an Outcome Receipt provides an auditable record of exactly what happened, including the authority applied, evidence used, decisions made, actions and transactions executed, and the result. In addition, Fusion Applications customers can decide what level of automation they want a process to have, ranging from quick assistance to governed full auto execution within explicitly delegated authority.
Running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and powered by industry-leading frontier models including Gemini and OpenAI, with support for additional frontier models planned over time, new Claw-powered Agentic Applications extend the broader Agentic Applications portfolio. There are 25 new Claw-powered, full auto-capable Agentic Applications available today, including:
Ledger: Helps finance leaders improve close readiness and resolve accounting exceptions faster by working across large volumes of accounting entries to reconcile information, investigate exceptions and anomalies, and apply deterministic computation to complex financial analysis and execution.
Workforce Staffing: Helps HR leaders create executable staffing plans that meet coverage and service requirements while balancing constraints, including skills and accreditations, availability, schedules, labor rules, costs, coverage, and service requirements, with the ability to evaluate alternatives and continuously re-plan as conditions change.
Shipping Consolidation: Helps supply chain leaders reduce shipping costs while addressing service requirements and customer commitments by modelling consolidation alternatives across timing, capacity, service commitments, cost, and other constraints, and then carrying the best supported plan into governed execution when authorized.
Account Territory Growth Plan: Helps sales leaders achieve better coverage and opportunity allocation by modelling and comparing scenarios across different territory configurations, evaluating tradeoffs, and optimizing against capacity and business constraints before taking governed action.
The new Claw-powered Agentic Applications are part of a broader Fusion AI ecosystem anchored by Oracle AI Agent Studio for Fusion Applications. With the Agentic Applications Builder and AI Studio Skill no-code and pro-code capabilities in Oracle AI Agent Studio, organizations can create and manage agentic applications using reusable Oracle, partner, and external agents. In addition, built-in observability, ROI measurement, and safety controls enable agents to deliver measurable value and operate responsibly at scale.
Fusion Claw Partner and Analyst Quotes
“Agentic AI is reinventing how work gets done across the enterprise,” said Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO, Accenture. “Oracle Fusion Claw enables organizations to apply AI to more complex, outcome-driven work while always keeping humans in the lead. Combined with Accenture’s industry and transformation expertise, this new capability can help our clients redesign processes for better business outcomes and create new sources of value.”
“Together with Oracle, we’re helping organizations move from isolated AI pilots to scaled adoption by connecting technology with the operating models, governance, and change capabilities needed to realize value,” said Joe Ucuzoglu, Global CEO, Deloitte. “We look forward to advancing that journey alongside Oracle, supporting more complex, outcome-oriented work while keeping accountability and control at the center.”
“The next phase of enterprise AI will require models that can reason through complex problems while working within the systems businesses use every day,” said Kevin Ichhpurani, president, Global Partner Ecosystem, Google Cloud. “By bringing Gemini models to Oracle Fusion Claw, Oracle is combining frontier AI with the context, controls, and execution capabilities of its market-leading enterprise applications. This creates an important foundation for AI that can take on more sophisticated work while operating within the boundaries organizations define.”
“Fusion Claw is an important and logical next step in the evolution of enterprise agentic AI,” said Aly Pinder, research vice president, Aftermarket Services Strategies, IDC. "Oracle is moving the conversation from agents that assist with individual tasks to a next generation of applications that can take on increasingly complex work around a business outcome. With an execution architecture that can combine AI reasoning with precise enterprise computation and governed action, Oracle Fusion Applications customers can gain significant value from enterprise AI.”
“Organizations want to move quickly with agentic AI, but greater autonomy is often only possible when built upon a solid foundation of trust, accountability and proper controls,” said Rob Fisher, Global Head of Advisory, KPMG International. “Oracle Fusion Claw is designed to bring these requirements together and give organizations the confidence they need to use agentic AI for high value processes. This is another example of how Oracle’s investments in AI and agentic capabilities are redefining the solutions and value KPMG firms and Oracle can jointly bring to clients.”
“The clients leading on AI are reinventing customer experiences, products and services, and back-office processes through agentic AI,” said Dan Priest, US Chief AI Officer, PwC. “Capabilities like Oracle Fusion Claw make it possible to apply AI to more complex business processes, with the autonomy and governed execution those processes demand. Combining Oracle’s technology with PwC’s industry and transformation experience, we can help clients turn that into new ways of working and measurable business outcomes.”

About Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications
Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications are a complete suite of cloud applications that form the enterprise system of record, spanning finance, HR, supply chain, manufacturing, sales, service, and marketing. The suite includes Oracle Fusion Cloud Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Oracle Fusion Cloud Human Capital Management (HCM), Oracle Fusion Cloud Supply Chain & Manufacturing (SCM), and Oracle Fusion Cloud Customer Experience (CX).
Fusion Agentic Applications extend that foundation into a system of outcomes. They can coordinate and execute end-to-end work toward business objectives, and are designed to operate within the policies, controls, and authority each organization defines. Press Release
Oracle Health Advances Revenue Cycle Management with AI
Native AI capabilities will help connect and simplify revenue cycle workflows to help healthcare organizations optimize financial performance and enhance patient financial experiences
Oracle Health and Life Sciences Summit, Orlando, Florida—Sep 23, 2026
Oracle Health today announced new AI capabilities across its revenue cycle management portfolio that are planned to be released in the coming months to help healthcare organizations in the US limit reimbursement problems early in the patient and payment journey. Revenue cycle teams often spend significant time correcting downstream issues, including denials, missing information, authorization problems, inaccurate charges, and delayed payments. Oracle Health is bringing AI upstream—across scheduling, financial clearance, clinical documentation, charge capture, billing, and payment—to identify risks early, streamline routine actions, and connect clinical, financial, payer, and operational information before issues lead to payment delays and revenue loss.
“AI gives us an opportunity to prevent revenue cycle problems before they lead to denials and delayed payments,” said Seema Verma, executive vice president and general manager, Oracle Health and Life Sciences. “Oracle Health is delivering a comprehensive revenue cycle solution that brings AI across the front, middle, and back office, connecting clinical and financial workflows from the first patient interaction through payment. This can help healthcare organizations reduce administrative work and revenue leakage, get paid faster, and strengthen their financial stability so they can stay focused on delivering excellent patient care.”
Clinical, financial, payer, provider, and operational activities all influence reimbursement and financial performance, yet many organizations continue to manage these activities across fragmented systems and manual workflows that create inefficiencies, reimbursement delays, and administrative burden. Oracle Health revenue cycle management solutions connect workflows across patient access, clinical documentation, patient accounting, contract intelligence, payment operations, enterprise analytics, and financial management.
Organizations can leverage native AI embedded across existing Oracle Health revenue cycle solutions while modernizing at their own pace.
The new embedded AI capabilities1 include:
Prior authorization: Checks coverage, retrieves documentation requirements and pre-fills the information, attaches evidence, coordinates authorization activities, and supports payer interactions to help limit authorization-related delays and denials
Clinical document quality integrity: Reviews reimbursement-related documentation, identifies documentation gaps, and surfaces contextual recommendations to help enhance documentation and coding quality
Charge capture and integrity: Analyzes clinical and reimbursement context, modifiers, and service details within charge review workflows to help limit revenue leakage, limit denials, and optimize reimbursement outcomes
Medical coding for professional fees: Analyzes clinical documentation and patient context to surface coding recommendations within existing workflows to support reimbursable claim readiness
Appeal Management: Analyzes the remittance received, identifies payment variances, and automates the creation of appeal packets when a decision to appeal is made to help limit turnaround times
As part of its planned product direction, Oracle Health intends to further connect reimbursement workflows with enterprise financial operations, including financial reconciliation, revenue accounting, treasury management, and analytics through solutions such as Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications. This can help health systems connect reimbursement activity, financial operations, and enterprise analytics to support informed operational and financial decision-making.
To learn more, join the live action today at the Oracle Health and Life Sciences Summit by visiting https://www.oracle.com/health/health-life-sciences-summit/.

Press Release
Oracle to Advance Cancer Care with New Oncology EHR
Is expected to empower care teams with AI-driven workflows, insights, and connected patient information to help enable more effective, personalized treatment
Oracle Health and Life Sciences Summit, Orlando, Florida—Sep 23, 2026
Oracle today announced its Oracle Health Oncology EHR. Building on the capabilities of Oracle’s modern, AI-powered ambulatory EHR, the new solution is purpose-built for the distinct demands of cancer care, bringing together oncology-specific workflows, AI-fueled clinical intelligence derived from multiple data sources, and connected information to support patient care from diagnosis through treatment and follow-up.
“A cancer diagnosis changes everything for patients and their families. Care teams should not be slowed down by fragmented information, lack of clinical insights, and antiquated technology that forces the patient to search for and recount their history repeatedly, risking critical missed details,” said Seema Verma, executive vice president and general manager, Oracle Health and Life Sciences. “Oracle Health Oncology EHR is designed to bring the patient’s story together and provide personalized treatment recommendations, helping clinicians focus their time and expertise where they matter most: caring for the person in front of them.”
Putting the needs of patients and oncology teams at the center of care
Cancer care is among the most complex forms of medicine. The multidisciplinary nature of treatment requires oncologists and their teams to coordinate rapidly changing treatment plans, chemotherapy regimens, laboratory and imaging results, medications, referrals, and insurance requirements across multiple care settings. When that information is fragmented, clinicians lose valuable time assembling the context needed to make decisions, while patients face a disconnected care experience during an already difficult time.
With embedded AI agents and clinical decision support built in, the context-aware EHR is expected to help care teams navigate the complexity of cancer care by delivering an intuitive and responsive experience across inpatient and outpatient settings.
Oracle Health’s AI-powered assistant for oncologists is expected to connect results, decision support, and action across the cancer care journey. From patient snapshots and pre-visit summaries that surface what has changed, to specialized assistants for Tumor Board preparation and guideline-grounded treatment planning, the assistant can help clinicians make sense of complex information and carry their decisions into workflows such as orders, referrals, documentation, and coding. Oracle’s broader vision is a connected ecosystem of role-based AI assistants supporting nurses, patients, care coordinators, researchers, and the wider multidisciplinary cancer care team, helping people work together with shared context throughout the patient journey.
Planned capabilities are intended to help users benefit from:
Unified cancer-care timelines: enabling access to a clear, chronological view of cancer-related diagnoses and treatments to support continuity of care and informed decision-making.
Connected worklists for nurse navigators: to support care coordination from clinician diagnosis through treatment and survivorship, helping navigators maintain holistic, connected care plans.
Intelligent precision oncology insights: that unify genomic, radiology, pathology, laboratory, pharmacy, and social determinants of health data to support diagnoses and evidence-based treatment decisions, with a foundation for future capabilities such as pathway guidance, predictive analytics, trial matching, cost comparisons, and industry content.
Streamlined regimen planning workflows: which simplify chemotherapy and immunotherapy ordering with lifetime cumulative-dose calculations, mobile ordering, response-to-treatment documentation, and simplified regimen maintenance, helping care teams manage treatment changes and support consistent, evidence-based care.
To learn more, join the live action today at the Oracle Health and Life Sciences Summit by visiting https://www.oracle.com/health/health-life-sciences-summit/.

						LG Electronics Expands WashTower Lineup With New 25-Inch Model
    Latest Premium Laundry Solution Combines Large Washing and
 Drying Capacities With a Seamless, Space-Efficient Design
    News Summary
LG Electronics begins the global rollout of the new 25-inch LG WashTower, which joins the 24- and 27-inch models to form a complete lineup of premium laundry solutions, giving customers greater choice.The new WashTower combines a compact 25-inch form factor with the ability to simultaneously wash and dry separate loads of up to 20 kilograms each.Equipped with LG’s core laundry technologies and AI-powered features, including AI Wash 2.0, AI Dry and AI Time Sensing, the new WashTower offers fast washing and drying, intuitive control and a refined flat design.
SEOUL, Oct. 15, 2026 — LG Electronics (LG) is commencing the global rollout of the 25-inch LG WashTower™, a unified vertical laundry solution designed to balance large-capacity performance with space efficiency. Featuring an independently operated dual-drum design, the WashTower allows users to wash and dry separate loads simultaneously. The new appliance joins the existing 24- and 27-inch WashTowers to form a complete lineup, enabling customers to select the model best suited to their living space, laundry needs and lifestyle.
Balancing Capacity and Space Efficiency
 LG WashTower integrates a separate washer and dryer that can operate simultaneously into a unified form factor, allowing users to manage more loads in less time. With LG’s optimized drum structure and a compact footprint, the new 25-inch model combines installation flexibility with ample laundry capacity.
A Refined, Integrated Design for Modern Living Spaces
 The new WashTower adopts LG’s Flat design to deliver a refined, built-in-inspired aesthetic that complements a range of interiors. The integration of the Hidden Hinge Door and Push Detergent Box results in a sleek exterior that allows the appliance to blend in seamlessly with most modern living spaces. Equipped with a wide 6.8-inch touch LCD display, the WashTower’s signature Center Control™ panel lets users adjust settings and check washing and drying status from a single, centrally positioned interface.
Advanced Core Technologies and AI Capabilities
Employing LG’s advanced core technologies, the 25-inch WashTower delivers a fast and convenient wash-to-dry experience. TurboWash™ uses powerful water jets and rapid drum movements to help reduce washing time,1 DUAL Inverter HeatPump™ technology helps deliver drying performance while improving energy efficiency and Turbo Dry helps shorten drying time.
For additional convenience, the WashTower’s Prepare to Dry feature makes it possible to wash and dry a three-kilogram load of laundry within 120 minutes.2 Meanwhile, AI Wash™ 2.0, which is powered by LG’s Artificial Intelligence Direct Drive™ (AI DD™), analyzes load weight, fabric characteristics and soil level to tailor the washing and rinsing process for enhanced cleaning and gentle fabric care.
The new WashTower further streamlines the task of laundry with its advanced smart features. AI Dry assesses fabric type, load size and humidity changes to help determine the appropriate drying time. For loads under five kilograms consisting of similar fabric types, it can also help deliver more even drying.3 By continuously updating usage data over time, AI Time Sensing can detect load characteristics to supply a more precise cycle-length estimate.4 After each cycle, the AI Laundry Report provides a summary of key information – including estimated load size, detergent usage and energy consumption – on the Center Control display. By connecting the appliance to the LG ThinQ™ app for compatible mobile devices, users can check related notifications and laundry status from almost anywhere.5
LG will commence the rollout of its new WashTower in Asia, the Middle East and Latin America later this year, with availability to follow in additional markets starting from 2027.
“With the addition of the 25-inch model, our complete WashTower lineup gives customers greater flexibility – allowing them to choose the premium laundry solution that best suits their space, needs and lifestyle,” said Baek Seung-tae, president of the LG Home Appliance Solution Company. “The new WashTower shows that customers can enjoy both capacity and space efficiency. Our premium laundry solution delivers performance and convenience in a size designed to fit more homes.”
# # #

Based on a 3 kilograms real-use load, a complete wash and dry cycle was finished within 120 minutes using the Cotton wash cycle with Prepare to dry option and Cotton dry cycle (Washer: F0W5DBPKZH, Dryer: RH18W5ZVKWP). Results may vary depending on usage conditions and other factors.
3 Tested by Intertek in April 2026. Compared to the Cotton cycle, reduced drying time was observed with a 3 kilograms load of soft fabrics, while more even drying performance was confirmed for cotton-based laundry (RH18W5ZVKWP). Results may vary depending on load weight, fabric type and other conditions. AI sensing is activated for loads under 5 kilograms. AI Dry should only be used with similar fabric types, as not all fabrics are detected.
4 Time estimates vary depending on load condition and selected cycle settings.
5 Displayed on the Center Control panel upon completion of the cycle. When the appliance is connected to the ThinQ™ app, users can also check notifications on their mobile device.
