documents.title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• NVIDIA and Meta will expand their partnership on Muse and the Muse family of models, reflecting popular demand for AI agents.

• The companies are also considering other technological collaborations, including NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture to strengthen agency security and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring, structured, unstructured and graph data processing.

• Meta to expand NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment to boost performance and scale workloads with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4.

NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents.

Meta’s Muse models and agents, which leverage NVIDIA’s infrastructure, have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Meta and NVIDIA intend to further deepen their collaboration by partnering on optimizations across workflows to maximize performance and improve total cost of ownership. Meta and NVIDIA will also consider additional collaboration opportunities with NVIDIA on its NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, including NVIDIA OpenShell™ for safe deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior.

This announcement reinforces Meta and NVIDIA’s strong long-term partnership to support Meta’s AI infrastructure ambitions. Meta intends to expand the deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs for next-generation AI agents to deliver maximum performance per watt. Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ Ethernet networking and BlueField-4® to support network efficiency and throughput.

In addition, NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering.

“AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents. NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions.”

“Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We’re excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people,” said Mark Zuckerberg, founder and CEO of Meta.

documents.title: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years.

• Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028.

• KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA.

• SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform.

Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain.

“We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.”

Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway.

Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity.

NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028.

Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms.

Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore.

NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027.

In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027.

Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.

documents.title: NVIDIA Advances Isaac Platform for General-Purpose Robotics With New Reference Humanoid, Frameworks, Simulation Pipelines and Data
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• Agile Robots announces Agile ONE SN, a humanoid reference platform built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and NVIDIA Jetson Thor with planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack, giving developers and researchers a complete platform for frontier humanoid development and validation.

• NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning and open source reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos on NVIDIA DGX Station to accelerate robot data generation, training and evaluation.

• Europe’s robotics ecosystem, including leaders like ABB Robotics, Flexion, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Sereact and Universal Robots, is building on NVIDIA’s open robotics platform to advance autonomous robotic systems.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform, adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework.

Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster.

“General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Isaac, our full-stack open robotics platform, we are giving developers the models, data, simulation tools and computing systems to bring physical AI to the world’s largest industries.”

Agile ONE SN — A Frontier Humanoid Reference Platform for Research Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor™ edge AI platform.

Robotics researchers and developers often struggle to integrate the separate simulation, training and deployment tools needed to take robot skills from development to the physical world. Agile ONE SN unifies these tools and workflows on a single platform, cutting setup time from weeks to days.

Agile ONE SN features:

• Agile ONE S humanoid body, standing 1.40 meters (4.59 feet tall) and weighing 40 kilograms (88 pounds), with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3-kilogram payload per arm.

• Dual WUJI Hand 2 five-finger hands, each offering 20 degrees of freedom, 1kHz force control and tactile sensing for dexterous manipulation

• NVIDIA Jetson Thor onboard compute, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control.

• Multimodal sensing, including head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors and inertial measurement units to help the robot perceive and interact with its surroundings.

• NVIDIA Isaac GR00T platform, which comprises the GR00T foundation model, a full workflow from data capture to deployment and whole-body control for coordinated movement.

• Safety capabilities, with planned integration of on-robot safety protocols with the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system for robotics.

“The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale: one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people,” said Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots. “Today, Agile Robots introduced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack, open reference humanoid built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, powered by Jetson Thor, giving developers a ready system to create, train and validate the capabilities needed to put humanoids to work.”

Scheduled to be available in early 2027, Agile ONE SN is designed to advance frontier humanoid research and development, with interest from leading institutions such as Stanford University and ETH Zurich.

New NVIDIA Technology Accelerate Robot Learning — From Data to Deployment New NVIDIA technologies help developers generate training data, scale robot learning, build simulation environments and deploy robot applications, reducing time to solution.

• SimReady Central Library offers more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, while the Human 1M Dataset includes diverse human activities, synchronized three-view video and 3D hand tracking. Both are available on Hugging Face, with the full Human 1M Dataset accessible to Cosmos Coalition partners.

• NVIDIA Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available, providing an open source, agent-ready learning framework training and refining robot policies from desktop to data center using multi-GPU workflows and physics engines including Newton and NVIDIA PhysX™.

• NVIDIA Isaac OS, an open source runtime framework built on NVIDIA Holoscan, connects AI, sensors, controls and robot hardware for deterministic, real-time performance from simulation to physical robots.

• NVIDIA is releasing three open source reference workflows for NVIDIA DGX Station™ that help developers refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills in NVIDIA Isaac Lab and post-train NVIDIA Cosmos™ world models for synthetic data generation using ChatGPT Astra.

• NVIDIA Halos provides a full-stack safety platform built on NVIDIA IGX Thor™ to help move autonomous vehicles and robots from development to safer real-world deployment at scale.

SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face includes simulation-ready assets from Comau, FANUC, ForgeCAD, Franka Robotics, LG Electronics, Palatial, Robotiq, Standard Bots, Universal Robots and Vertiv.

NVIDIA’s open source robot learning reference workflows running on DGX Station will be supported by solutions from 1X, Agile Robots, Humanoid, Maven Robotics, Mentee, MicroAGI, Rhoda, Sereact and Skild AI.

Robotics partners are integrating NVIDIA Halos within their safety architectures, including Agile Robots, Agility, Dexory, FORT Robotics and KION for warehouse robot safety. SICK is evaluating Halos to advance dynamic safety for industrial robots, helping them respond to changing conditions beyond fixed zones.

Advantech and NexCOBOT are developing NVIDIA IGX-based industrial computing platforms, while Reynolds & Moore, Accenture and TÜV SÜD are accelerating the certification process for the safe deployment of industrial physical AI.

European Robotics Leaders Build on NVIDIA Open Technologies ABB Robotics is integrating NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to simulate and virtually commission robotic systems before installation across a wide range of industries. KUKA Group is using Omniverse libraries in its Visual Components FactoryLens to add real-time rendering for factory simulation workflows. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T with Cosmos Transfer to train and post-train its Cortex platform for goods handling, running on Universal Robots industrial robot arms.

Using Jetson Thor, Holoscan Sensor Bridge, Halos and NVIDIA Isaac OS, Humanoid is developing and validating robot behaviors before industrial pilots, Hexagon Robotics is building AEON perception capabilities including teleoperation video, localization, mapping and object pose detection, and Bear Robotics is accelerating KR1 perception and model execution while post-training Isaac GR00T through Kino-2 for warehouse, returns and industrial workflows.

Toyota Material Handling Europe and SoftServe use Omniverse and the NVIDIA Isaac Sim™ framework to develop autonomous material-handling solutions, reducing deployment time by up to 50%. Idealworks is using NVIDIA open models and Jetson to develop memory capabilities for autonomous mobile robots in factories. Analog Devices Inc. (ADI) is using NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin™ and the cuVSLAM library to build autonomous mobile robots.

Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics are using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim and Newton to build Microduck, a small, open source robot designed to help developers and students train, modify and share new physical behaviors. Franka Robotics is using NVIDIA NIM™ microservices and Isaac Sim to turn natural-language requests into actions on its Franka FR3 Duo robot system. Bellboy is using Jetson and GR00T to power Billie, its first robot teammate built on Bellboy’s physical AI infrastructure, already deployed at hotels operated by Marriott, Hilton, IHG and OYO.

Flexion is using Isaac Lab and Newton to scale learning for Reflect, its unified robot intelligence model combining reasoning and whole-body movement for complex manipulation across robot bodies. Schaeffler is contributing its actuator technology as an exclusive foundational component for Newton, helping accelerate humanoid robot development with NVIDIA Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim.

NEURA Robotics is using Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to generate synthetic training data and train robot skills in simulation for Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model.

documents.title: European Mobility Leaders Build Safe Vehicles and Robotaxi Fleets on NVIDIA Hyperion
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets, with Volvo Cars adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for safe automated driving.

• NVIDIA introduces Halos SAFE, a new framework within the NVIDIA Halos safety system, which combines simulation and physical testing to help developers generate measurable, traceable AV safety evidence.

• NVIDIA announces Alpamayo 2 Edge, Alpamayo Agentic Factory and new Cosmos 3 Nano model variants to help developers build, customize and evaluate autonomous-driving for diverse vehicles, operating conditions and regions.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced that leading automakers in Europe and mobility providers, including Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride, are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.

In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale.

Autonomous transportation represents a multitrillion-dollar opportunity, with robotaxis leading the move to commercial level 4 deployment. NVIDIA Hyperion and the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system give automakers and mobility providers the computing performance, safety foundation and long-term support to bring AVs and robotaxi fleets to market at scale.

“Robotaxis are the first mass-market application of robotics and physical AI, reinventing how people and goods move,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “NVIDIA Hyperion, together with our Halos safety operating system, gives our partners a full-stack robotaxi platform designed to achieve full autonomy and the highest levels of safety, bringing us closer to a future where everything that moves is autonomous.”

Mobility Leaders in Europe Build on NVIDIA Hyperion Automakers and mobility providers in Europe are pursuing various paths to autonomy, from passenger vehicles and robotaxi fleets to autonomous freight trucks. NVIDIA Hyperion’s modular architecture supports all of these programs, compatible with NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack autonomous driving software as well as partners’ own driving software.

Bolt has selected NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for its European robotaxi program, beginning with future Lucid vehicles built on Hyperion. Bolt and NVIDIA will adapt the software for European roads and integrate it into vehicles from multiple manufacturers, combining NVIDIA’s driving and safety technologies with Bolt’s fleet-management systems, operations and local market expertise.

Bolt plans to begin gathering real-world driving data to support the development and validation of the autonomous driving technology — subject to regulatory approval — in Madrid in 2027, with Germany being a priority for future deployment as part of a planned European rollout of at least 25,000 level 4-capable future Lucid vehicles built on NVIDIA Hyperion.

At GTC Berlin, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is presenting its autonomous ID. Buzz AD vehicle platform with Hyperion to support multiple autonomous-driving systems. Hyperion provides a common computing and sensor architecture designed to simplify integration and validation, helping developers and mobility operators bring robotaxi and commercial transport services to market.

Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with Hyperion, Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door.

Mercedes-Benz is extending its partnership with NVIDIA on Hyperion and Alpamayo Stack to support the development of the automaker’s L3 and L4 capabilities. The company also announced that MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, will soon get approval for urban point-to-point urban driver assistance in Germany, helping drivers navigate journeys through complex city traffic.

Beyond passenger vehicles and robotaxis, Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using Halos, Alpamayo and NVIDIA Cosmos™ open world models to develop and validate its driving system, while TIER IV and the Technical University of Munich plan to integrate Hyperion to develop and validate systems for autonomous public transportation in Germany.

NVIDIA technology and manufacturing partners are also helping expand the AV ecosystem, with Aptiv, Valeo and Schaeffler building Hyperion-based computing platforms that can be integrated by vehicle manufacturers for L4 AVs and robotaxis.

Scaling Safe Autonomy With NVIDIA Halos Halos provides the safety foundation for NVIDIA’s AV platform, bringing together AI computing, safety software and validation from development through deployment.

To give developers repeatable ways to evaluate driving behavior and simulation accuracy, NVIDIA today introduced Halos SAFE — the Safety Assurance Framework for Evaluation — with dSPACE, IVEX and TÜV Rheinland collaborating on evaluation workflows. Halos SAFE connects simulation, software- and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, on-road testing and fleet monitoring through defined scenarios, tests and measurable performance criteria to generate traceable safety evidence that supports deployment.

The Halos SAFE ecosystem also includes JLR, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo Cars, 51Sim, aiMotive, AVL, Deepen AI, Foretellix and Synopsys.

Accelerating AV Development Developing AVs means teaching AI to handle the diversity of real-world driving, then bringing that intelligence into the vehicle. NVIDIA’s latest models, tools and blueprints help developers prepare driving data, improve models and evaluate performance:

• Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-billion-parameter reasoning model built on NVIDIA Cosmos, is optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor™ platform and designed to run at 10Hz for in-vehicle scene understanding and motion planning.

• AlpaJudge, a human-calibrated evaluation and reward model, scores driving explanations to assess reasoning quality, filter weak annotations and reduce manual review of training data.

• Foundation4D labels multicamera video without lidar input, supporting perception-model training and NVIDIA Omniverse™ NuRec scene reconstruction.

• New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants expand synthetic data generation and closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving through synchronized multiview, multi-camera and lidar generation across diverse driving scenarios.

• Cosmos Data Factory’s AV dataset-generation blueprint turns driving video and vehicle signals into curated, searchable, labeled data, using synthetic data to expand scenario coverage.

• Alpamayo Agentic Factory, an open blueprint expected to become available in early 2027, uses AI agents to connect data preparation, model post-training and simulation evaluation, reducing integration work.

• NVIDIA NIM™ microservices for Alpamayo 1.5 and NuRec Harmonizer deliver both models as optimized inference containers, giving AV reasoning and scene harmonization a simplified deployment path.

Uber and NVIDIA are developing a data factory powered by Cosmos to curate and process data for AV development. The effort is part of a broader partnership spanning AI development infrastructure, Hyperion-based vehicles and Uber’s global ride-hailing network.

Porsche is leading the development of a data flywheel workflow across Volkswagen Group brands through Voxel51, using NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory and Omniverse NuRec on Microsoft Azure to turn fleet data into datasets and simulations for evaluating autonomous-driving models. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle duration by up to 85%.

This compares to revenue of $6.72 billion, gross margin of $3.48 billion, or 51.7% of revenue, operating expenses of $965.3 million, operating margin of 37.4%, and net income of $2.28 billion, or $1.81 per diluted share, for the quarter ended June 28, 2026 (the "June 2026 quarter").Non-GAAP Financial ResultsFor the September 2026 quarter, non-GAAP gross margin was $4.31 billion, or 52.4% of revenue, non-GAAP operating expenses were $1.00 billion, non-GAAP operating margin was 40.2%, and non-GAAP net income was $2.77 billion, or $2.20 per diluted share. FREMONT, Calif., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) today announced that Michael ("Mike") R. Cannon and Sohail U. Ahmed have informed the company of their respective decisions to retire from Lam's Board of Directors, effective November 2, 2026, following years of leadership.
"Mike's deep expertise in executive leadership and his passion for innovation have been invaluable in guiding Lam through strategic geographic growth and expanding its technology leadership in deposition, etch and advanced packaging," said Abhi Talwalkar, chair of the board at Lam Research. "Sohail's deep industry experience and understanding of silicon logic and semiconductor processing equipment technologies have been assets to our board. We thank Mike and Sohail for their dedication and many significant contributions and wish them well in their retirements."Joining the Lam Board of Directors in 2011, Cannon retires after a career spanning more than 40 years of transformational leadership and innovation in several technology industries.Most recently, Cannon held senior advisory and board roles providing guidance to technology companies on global strategy, business transformation, and operational excellence. At Seagate Technology Holdings, plc, he served on the board for fifteen years including five years as the lead independent director and five years as the board Chairman. Seagate recently announced that he will retire from the board later this year. He has also served on the boards of Dialog Semiconductor plc from 2013 until its sale to Renesas Electronics in 2021, and previously was on the board of Adobe Systems for 13 years.Previously, Cannon held CEO and other executive leadership positions at top technology companies, most recently as the President of Global Operations at Dell Technologies leading the worldwide transformation of operations, supply chain and logistics functions. Prior to Dell, he was president and CEO of Solectron, a global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider, where he led the company through a major transformation, including a comprehensive restructuring plan resulting in an increased focus on design services. Previously he was CEO of Maxtor Corporation, a disk drive technology leader, for seven years including a successful IPO in 1998 and the company's acquisition by Seagate in 2006. Cannon also held several senior leadership positions at IBM, including Vice President of the Personal Storage Systems Division, with P&L responsibility for disk drive and storage solutions products. Earlier in his career, he worked as a mechanical engineer in the R&D organization of Boeing and was named an Inventor of the Year in 1983.Joining the Lam Board of Directors in 2019, Ahmed was formerly senior vice president and general manager of the Technology and Manufacturing Group at Intel Corporation, a leading producer of microchips, computing and communications products, where he was responsible for overseeing the research, development and deployment of next-generation silicon logic technologies for the production of future Intel microprocessors. He held that position from 2015 to 2018. Immediately prior to that, he was corporate vice president and general manager, Logic Technology Department, at Intel from 2004 to January 2015. Ahmed joined Intel in 1984, working as a process engineer, and held progressive technical and management positions in logic process development.About Lam ResearchLam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX) is a global supplier of innovative wafer fabrication equipment and services to the semiconductor industry. Lam's equipment and services allow customers to build smaller and better performing devices. In fact, today, nearly every advanced chip is built with Lam technology. We combine superior systems engineering, technology leadership, and a strong values-based culture, with an unwavering commitment to our customers. Lam Research is a FORTUNE 500® company headquartered in Fremont, California, with operations around the globe. MILPITAS, Calif., Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC) today announced financial and operating results for its first quarter of fiscal year 2027, which ended on September 30, 2026, and reported GAAP net income of $1.55 billion and GAAP net income per diluted share of $1.18 on revenues of $4.14 billion.
"KLA's September quarter beat the midpoint of guidance across all key metrics, demonstrating the accelerated growth we expected for the second half of calendar 2026," said Rick Wallace, president and CEO of KLA Corporation. "Process control, and KLA in particular, continues to be critical to the AI ecosystem buildout and benefits from numerous ongoing inflections, including increases in leading-edge designs across foundry and logic, device size and value, memory complexity and performance requirements, and the importance of advanced packaging. In addition, KLA's process, PCB, and component inspection businesses are benefiting from the technology transitions and the rigorous performance requirements of high-performance computing, which further augments the company's growth profile. KLA's market-leading product portfolio and its associated services offerings remain well positioned to address these compelling opportunities as we approach the end of calendar 2026 and look forward to calendar 2027."

The non-GAAP and supplemental information provided in this press release is a supplement to, and not a substitute for, KLA's financial results presented in accordance with United States GAAP.
To supplement our Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements presented in accordance with GAAP, we provide certain non-GAAP financial information, which is adjusted from results based on GAAP to exclude certain gains, costs and expenses, as well as other supplemental information. The non-GAAP and supplemental information is provided to enhance the user's overall understanding of our operating performance and our prospects in the future. Specifically, we believe that the non-GAAP information, including non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income per diluted share, non-GAAP gross margin and free cash flow, provides useful measures to both management and investors regarding financial and business trends relating to our financial performance by excluding certain costs and expenses that we believe are not indicative of our core operating results to help investors compare our operating performances with our results in prior periods as well as with the performance of other companies. The non-GAAP information is among the budgeting and planning tools that management uses for future forecasting. However, because there are no standardized or generally accepted definitions for most non-GAAP financial metrics, definitions of non-GAAP financial metrics are inherently subject to significant discretion (for example, determining which costs and expenses to exclude when calculating such a metric). As a result, non-GAAP financial metrics may be defined very differently from company to company, or even from period to period within the same company, which can potentially limit the usefulness of such information to an investor. The presentation of non-GAAP and supplemental information is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for results prepared and presented in accordance with United States GAAP. The following are descriptions of the adjustments made to reconcile GAAP net income to non-GAAP net income:
a.
Acquisition-related charges primarily include amortization of intangible assets. Acquisition-related charges during the three months ended June 30, 2026 also include a discrete release of $11.6 million of interest on unrecognized tax positions recorded as part of purchase price accounting arising from acquisitions. Although we exclude the effect of amortization of all acquired intangible assets from these non-GAAP financial measures, management believes that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets were recorded as part of purchase price accounting arising from acquisitions, and such amortization of intangible assets related to past acquisitions will recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized. GM's winning portfolio continues getting stronger
		2026-10-01
        		News and events
				,
        		Financial
			Back
	GM continued to see strong demand for its portfolio in the U.S. market in Q3, extending its industry lead in segments like full-size pickups and full-size SUVs and fleet sales, along with record sales of affordable, small SUVs.
GM sales in Q3 totaled 670,974 vehicles, down 6% which reflected the much smaller EV market and discontinued vehicles. However, sales of GM’s highest volume vehicles were in line with the outstanding level of a year ago.
“Our business is performing very well, the launch of our next-generation full-size pickup trucks is on track, and we are making investments in new vehicles, innovative technologies, and our U.S. manufacturing footprint to drive our next phase of growth.” - Duncan Aldred, President of GM North America.
GM’s top five best-selling vehicles (Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra, Chevrolet Equinox, Chevrolet Traverse and Chevrolet Trax) continue to demonstrate multiple years of growth based on strong consumer demand.
GM also extended its lead in full-size pickups, and in Q4 the next-generation 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra are scheduled to begin arriving in dealerships.
GM’s portfolio strength extends beyond trucks. The family of affordable, small SUVs – led by the award-winning Chevrolet Trax and Buick Envista – had its best quarterly sales ever in Q3.
Key Q3 sales highlights:
GMC: Sierra is on track for its second-best calendar year, and the midsize Canyon pickup had its best quarter ever.
Chevrolet: Trax sales were up 16%, Trailblazer had its best Q3 sales ever since 2007 and Corvette sales were up 29%.
Buick: Total brand sales were up 8% in Q3 and the brand’s small SUVs (Envista and Encore GX) are on pace to have their second-best calendar year.
Cadillac: Expanded its lead of the luxury EV market, growing by 1.3 percentage points CYTD through August. It was also the best-ever Q3 for the CT5 Blackwing, keeping it on pace for its best year ever.
GM Fleet: Led the industry as number one in fleet sales, with a 10% year-over-year increase.
Read more about GM’s Q3 sales here.

documents.title: Johnson & Johnson’s Novel Shockwave Javelin Coronary IVL Catheter Delivers Positive Results in Pivotal FORWARD CAD IDE Study
documents.raw_text:
SAN DIEGO – November 1, 2026 – Today, Johnson & Johnson announced 30-day results from the FORWARD coronary artery disease (CAD) investigational device exemption (IDE) study evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Shockwave Javelin Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy (IVL) Catheter. The catheter, an investigational device in the U.S., is designed for the treatment of calcified, difficult-to-cross stenotic de novo coronary artery lesions prior to stenting. The results were presented as featured clinical research at the 2026 Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) congress in San Diego, California.In the 158-patient pivotal cohort, event rates for the primary safety and effectiveness endpoints exceeded pre-specified performance goals. Key findings from the study include:93.6% technical success rate (primary effectiveness endpoint, defined as successful Shockwave Javelin Coronary IVL-enabled lesion crossing without serious angiographic complications at final imaging).93.4% freedom from major adverse cardiovascular events (primary safety endpoint, defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction or target vessel revascularization) through 30 days.Additionally, the study demonstrated low complication rates in a highly complex lesion population. Among treated lesions, 96% were moderately or severely calcified, with a mean diameter stenosis of 81% and chronic total occlusions present in 20% of lesions. Despite this, serious angiographic complications at final imaging were observed in only 1.3% of patients.“Successfully treating heavily calcified lesions begins with being able to facilitate lesion crossing, an enduring challenge that can limit what physicians can achieve for patients,” said Robert Yeh, M.D., MBA, global co-principal investigator of the study and Section Chief, Interventional Cardiology, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.i “These findings represent an important step toward overcoming that barrier and creating a viable treatment path for patients whose disease may be beyond the reach of conventional balloon-based calcium modification approaches.”Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death globally, affecting an estimated 315 million people worldwide and approximately 1 in 20 adults over the age of 20 in the U.S.ii,iii,iv. In CAD, the buildup of cholesterol-rich deposits results in narrowing of the coronary arteries, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle. Among lesions that cannot be crossed with a balloon, more than 75% have moderate to severe calcification.v“The FORWARD CAD IDE study shows that difficult to cross lesions may be treated successfully without compromising safety,” said James Spratt, M.D., global co-principal investigator of the study and FRCP, St. George’s University NHS Trust.[vi] “This study suggests that Javelin could help physicians manage patients with limited treatment options.”About the FORWARD CAD StudyThe FORWARD CAD study is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study conducted in 28 sites in the U.S. and U.K. The study enrolled 158 patients with severely stenosed, de novo calcified coronary artery lesions with moderate to severe calcification defined by angiography and either over 90% stenosis with lesion length <40mm or a chronic total occlusion (CTO) and a J_CTO score of 1. The co-global principal investigators of the study are Robert Yeh, M.D., MBA, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and James Spratt, M.D., FRCP, St. George’s University NHS Trust, and the U.S. principal investigator is Robert Riley, M.D., FACC, Overlake Medical Center & Clinics.The investigational Shockwave Javelin Coronary IVL platform is designed with a single distal emitter that creates ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves, with a spherical energy field that extends beyond the tip of the catheter. This novel design enables lithotripsy delivery closer to highly stenosed calcified lesions than would be possible with balloon-based IVL platforms.Cardiovascular Solutions from Johnson & JohnsonAcross Johnson & Johnson, we are tackling the world’s most complex and pervasive health challenges. Through a cardiovascular portfolio that provides healthcare professionals with advanced mapping and navigation, miniaturized tech, and precise ablation, we are addressing conditions with significant unmet needs such as heart failure, coronary and peripheral artery disease, stroke, and atrial fibrillation. We are the global leaders in heart recovery, circulatory restoration and the treatment of heart rhythm disorders, as well as an emerging leader in neurovascular care, committed to taking on two of the leading causes of death worldwide in heart failure and stroke. For more information on circulatory restoration, visit our website. About Johnson & Johnson  At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more about our MedTech sector’s global scale and deep expertise in cardiovascular, orthopaedics, surgery and vision solutions at https://www.jnjmedtech.com/en-US/. Follow us at @JNJMedTech and on LinkedIn. Shockwave Medical, Inc. is a Johnson & Johnson company. documents.title: Data Show Positive Survival and Patient Outcomes with Best-Practice Impella Support in HRPCI, in Contrast to CHIP-BCIS3 Study Results
documents.raw_text:
SAN DIEGO – Nov. 1, 2026 – Johnson & Johnson announced results from three clinical analyses being presented during the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics annual scientific symposium (TCT 2026) that report positive survival and patient outcomes data when Impella™ heart pumps are used to support a patient’s heart during and after high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (HRPCI). Real-world and observational registry data from 1,379 HRPCI patients across hospitals in the U.S. and Europe show lower in-hospital cardiovascular mortality and lower 30- and 90-day mortality rates than those recently reported in CHIP-BCIS3. These contemporary findings from real-world U.S. and European experience with Impella-supported HRPCI provide important clinical context in contrast to the CHIP-BCIS3 study results.“Data from these high-impact presentations add to more than two decades of evidence supporting Impella use in complex HRPCI patients,” said Navin Kapur, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer, Heart Recovery, MedTech, Johnson & Johnson. “They also reinforce that outcomes depend not only on the device but how and when it is used, from selecting the right patients and procedural approach to post-procedural management and critical care.”The following data will be presented during TCT:TCT 197: Protected PCI with Microaxial-Flow Pump Support: Real-World Evidence from the TRI-GUARD-PCI Registry (Matthias Bossard, M.D., 11/1/26; 11 a.m. PST, station 4). This multicenter analysis of 279 patients undergoing elective protected PCI with Impella at hospitals in Germany, Switzerland and Austria showed lower 30-day (6.1%) and 180-day (7.9%) all-cause mortality rates than previously reported in the CHIP-BCIS3 trial Kaplan-Meier curve.“These real-world results provide important insights into outcomes following Impella-supported high-risk PCI in contemporary clinical practice,” said Matthias Bossard, M.D.1, an interventional cardiologist and researcher now at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, who conducted this research while at the Heart Center at Luzerner Kantonsspital in Lucerne, Switzerland, in collaboration with Mohamed Ayoub, MD, from Germany. “The findings may help inform patient selection and procedural planning for complex high-risk interventions.”TCT 888: Peri-procedural and Early Post-Procedural Cardiovascular Mortality Following HRPCI (Vasileios Panoulas, M.D., 11/2/26, 1 p.m. PST, station 2). Using a multicenter U.S. registry, this analysis of 522 patients who underwent Impella-supported HRPCI showed cardiovascular mortality of 3.4% at time of discharge compared with approximately 8% in the CHIP-BCIS3 study for patients treated with Impella on day 4 post-randomization. Kaplan-Meier curve estimates of cardiovascular mortality were 4.7% at 30 days and 6.5% at 90 days—both numerically lower than the corresponding rates reported in CHIP-BCIS3.“This analysis provides real-world perspective on the use of Impella during HRPCI and highlights differences from the CHIP-BCIS3 study protocol,” said Vasileios Panoulas, M.D.,2 physician at Royal Brompton and Harefield Hospitals in London and the abstract’s lead author. In the CHIP-BCIS3 treatment arm, the device was removed before patients left the catheterization lab whereas in the LOQI study, one in six patients were supported by Impella for more than three hours. “These observations suggest a potential relationship between duration of support, post-procedural management and patient outcomes,” adds Panoulas.TCT 1228: Clinical Characteristics and Early Mortality in a High-Risk PCI Cohort Similar to CHIP-BCIS3 Undergoing Impella Support: Insights from PROTECT III (Vasileios Panoulas, M.D., 11/3/26, 8:50 a.m. PST, station 10).This analysis identified patients enrolled in the PROTECT III study who would meet the study entry criteria for the CHIP-BCIS3 trial. The in-hospital all-cause mortality for those 578 Impella-supported patients was 4.7%, which is lower than the estimated ~8% mortality reported in CHIP-BCIS3.“In the high-risk PROTECT III cohort, Impella-supported HRPCI was performed in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction and complex coronary anatomy, including frequent left main and multivessel treatment, with lower mortality rates than reported in CHIP-BCIS3,” said Panoulas3, who is presenting this data at TCT. “Understanding mortality after HRPCI requires looking at patient risk at baseline, procedural complexity and the importance of post-procedure patient management.”Johnson & Johnson MedTech continues to study Impella across a range of coronary heart conditions, including the PROTECT IV randomized controlled trial, with results anticipated in 2027. This trial design builds on data demonstrating survival and patient outcomes and helps care teams further refine best practices for people with complex heart disease who need percutaneous coronary intervention. To learn more about PROTECT IV and our ongoing clinical research trials, visit https://www.heartrecovery.com/en-us/education/ongoing-studies/protect-iv.About Impella Heart PumpsImpella heart pumps are temporary mechanical circulatory support devices designed to unload the heart and provide hemodynamic support. Impella technology is used in appropriately selected patients with severe coronary artery disease or cardiogenic shock, consistent with applicable indications and labeling. Impella has been used to treat more than 450,000 patients globally.Cardiovascular Solutions from Johnson & Johnson MedTechAcross Johnson & Johnson, we are tackling the world’s most complex and pervasive health challenges. Through a cardiovascular portfolio that provides healthcare professionals with advanced mapping and navigation, miniaturized tech, and precise ablation we are addressing conditions with significant unmet needs such as heart failure, coronary and peripheral artery disease, stroke, and atrial fibrillation. We are the global leaders in heart recovery, circulatory restoration and the treatment of heart rhythm disorders, as well as an emerging leader in neurovascular care, committed to taking on two of the leading causes of death worldwide in heart failure and stroke. For more information about heart recovery, visit https://www.heartrecovery.com/en-us.About Johnson & JohnsonAt Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow and profoundly impact health for humanity. documents.title: Record 26 Abstracts at TCT 2026 Adds to More than 20 Years of Data Demonstrating the Safety, Efficacy and Cost Effectiveness of Impella Heart Pumps
documents.raw_text:
DANVERS, Mass. – Oct. 29, 2026 – Johnson & Johnson announces a record 26 presentations featuring the clinical science of Impella™ heart pumps will be presented at the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) 2026 conference, taking place Oct. 31–Nov. 3 in San Diego. The breadth of research reflects the company’s continued leadership in generating rigorous clinical evidence to advance the science of heart recovery and improve outcomes for patients facing complex and life-threatening cardiovascular conditions.Johnson & Johnson MedTech’s robust body of clinical evidence in heart recovery spans more than two decades, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective studies, registries and real-world clinical practice. More than 50,000 Impella patients have been studied, and more than 450,000 patients worldwide have been treated with Impella. This evidence base includes approximately 2,700 peer-reviewed publications and has contributed to the recognition of temporary mechanical circulatory support with Impella in 18 clinical guidelines and consensus statements.Impella clinical data being presented at TCT builds on that scientific foundation and includes new research from centers around the world across high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (HRPCI), cardiogenic shock, myocardial recovery, renal perfusion, physiologic risk and next-generation technology. Among the presentations are three analyses of contemporary U.S. and European experience with Impella-supported HRPCI that provide important clinical context in contrast to the CHIP-BCIS3 study results.“Scientific leadership requires sustained investment, rigorous evaluation of high-quality data, and a willingness to continually improve how we care for patients,” said Navin Kapur, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer, Heart Recovery, MedTech, Johnson & Johnson. “The record 26 Impella abstracts at TCT reflect our commitment to partnering with the clinical community to generate the evidence needed to advance understanding, inform best practices and help physicians deliver better outcomes for patients worldwide.”In addition, a novel health-economic model projecting lower lifetime healthcare costs and greater quality-adjusted survival with Impella compared with Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in heart failure patients undergoing HRPCI will be presented.TCT 391: HRPCI in Heart Failure: The Impact of Left Ventricular Unloading on Cost Effectiveness – a Markov Model. (M. Kodenchery, MD, Nov. 1, 2 p.m. PST, station 6)Impella Events at TCT 2026Johnson & Johnson MedTech will bring together the clinical community for two events designed to share best practices and promote scientific discussion about the 20 years of clinical evidence supporting the use of Impella across its multiple indications.Sunday, Nov. 1, from 6–7:30 p.m. PST. The evening program, featuring Devi Govender, worldwide president, and Navin Kapur, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer, Heart Recovery, MedTech, Johnson & Johnson, will bring together colleagues and leading investigators for an evening of scientific dialogue and discussion around the latest developments in Heart Recovery.Johnson & Johnson will also host the World Connect Symposium, Leading in Heart Recovery: Lessons Learned from the Clinical and Scientific Experience with Impella, on Monday, Nov. 2, from 7:45–8:45 a.m. PST at the World Connect Theater, upper level, San Diego Convention & Exhibition Center. The program will bring together leading experts on AMI cardiogenic shock and HRPCI to discuss emerging science and evidence and the future of heart recovery.Attendees can also visit Johnson & Johnson MedTech at Booth #4037 to explore Impella technology and connect with members of the heart recovery team.Innovation and Scientific Evidence At TCT, attendees will learn about the continued evolution of Impella technology, including prospective evidence from the Impella ECP pivotal trial and continuing access protocol evaluating lower-profile mechanical circulatory support during HRPCI. The scientific program will also feature emerging research intended to deepen understanding of myocardial recovery, renal perfusion and physiologic risk.Details on key Impella presentations are below:TCT 197: Protected PCI with Microaxial-Flow Pump Support: Real-World Evidence from the TRI-GUARD-PCI Registry (M. Bossard, Nov. 1, 11 a.m. PST, station 4)TCT 467: Site-Level Analysis of Infarct Size Reduction with LV Unloading in the STEMI-Door to Unload Trial (N. Mangner, Nov. 1, 3 p.m. PST, station 9) TCT 391: HRPCI in Heart Failure: The Impact of Left Ventricular Unloading on Cost Effectiveness: A Markov Model. (M. Kodenchery, Nov. 1, 2:50 p.m. PST | Station 6)TCT 888: Peri-procedural and Early Post-Procedural Mortality Following HRPCI (V. Panoulas, Nov. 2, 1 p.m. PST, station 2)TCT 1228: Clinical Characteristics and Early Mortality in a High-Risk PCI Cohort Similar to CHIP-BCIS3 Undergoing Impella Support: Insights from PROTECT III. (V. Panoulas, MD, Nov. 3, 8:50 a.m. PST, station 10)This work builds on a long-term commitment to evidence generation that has helped inform clinical practice and the evolution of care guidelines. Through ongoing and planned studies—including PROTECT IV RCT and other research across ischemic heart disease, heart failure, cardiac surgery and cardiogenic shock—Johnson & Johnson MedTech continues to partner with investigators and clinicians to advance the field and improve care for patients.About Impella Heart PumpsImpella heart pumps are temporary mechanical circulatory support devices designed to unload the heart and provide hemodynamic support. Impella technology is used in appropriately selected patients with severe coronary artery disease or cardiogenic shock, consistent with applicable indications and labeling.Cardiovascular Solutions from Johnson & Johnson MedTechAcross Johnson & Johnson, we are tackling the world’s most complex and pervasive health challenges. Through a cardiovascular portfolio that provides healthcare professionals with advanced mapping and navigation, miniaturized tech, and precise ablation we are addressing conditions with significant unmet needs such as heart failure, coronary and peripheral artery disease, stroke, and atrial fibrillation. We are the global leaders in heart recovery, circulatory restoration and the treatment of heart rhythm disorders, as well as an emerging leader in neurovascular care, committed to taking on two of the leading causes of death worldwide in heart failure and stroke. For more information about heart recovery, visit https://www.heartrecovery.com/en-us. About Johnson & JohnsonAt Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more about our MedTech sector’s global scale and deep expertise in surgery, orthopaedics, vision, and cardiovascular solutions at https://www.jnjmedtech.com/. Follow us at @jjmt_heartrecov and on LinkedIn.Cautions Concerning Forward-Looking StatementsThis press release contains “forward-looking statements” as defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 related to Impella heart pumps and the company’s research and innovation programs. October 22, 2026P&G Announces Fiscal Year 2027 First Quarter Results
Net Sales +4.0%; Organic Sales +4.0%
Diluted EPS $1.97, +1%; Core EPS $2.00, +1%
UPDATES NET SALES GUIDANCE FOR THORNE ACQUISITION
MAINTAINS FISCAL YEAR ORGANIC SALES, EPS GROWTH AND CASH RETURN GUIDANCECINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) reported first quarter fiscal year 2027 net sales of $23.3 billion, an increase of four percent versus the prior year. Organic sales, which excludes the impacts of foreign exchange and acquisitions and divestitures, also increased four percent versus the prior year. Diluted net earnings per share were $1.97, an increase of one percent versus prior year as the increase in net sales was partially offset by an increase in operating costs. Core earnings per share were $2.00, an increase of one percent versus the prior year.
Operating cash flow was $5.8 billion, and net earnings were $4.8 billion for the quarter. Free cash flow productivity was 93%. Free cash flow productivity is calculated as operating cash flow less capital spending, as a percentage of net earnings. The Company returned $3.9 billion of cash to shareowners via $2.6 billion of dividend payments and $1.3 billion of share repurchases.

Beauty segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Hair Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by innovation-based pricing in North America and Latin America, favorable product mix and an increase in unit volume. Personal Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume growth in Greater China and Europe and favorable product mix, partially offset by trade investments. Skin Care organic sales increased mid-single digits due to favorable premium product mix and a unit volume increase in North America.
Grooming segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago driven by innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America and IMETA, and favorable product mix.
Health Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Oral Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by premium product mix and innovation-based pricing, partially offset by a unit volume decline. Personal Health Care organic sales increased low single digits due to higher pricing, primarily in North America and Latin America, and favorable product mix, partially offset by a unit volume decline.
Fabric and Home Care segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Fabric Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable geographic mix. Home Care organic sales also increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable product mix.
Baby, Feminine and Family Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Baby Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by a unit volume increase, primarily in Greater China and North America, and favorable premium product mix, partially offset by lower pricing, primarily in North America. Feminine Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by favorable product mix and innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America, partially offset by a unit volume decline in Europe. Family Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by a unit volume increase, partially offset by merchandising investments.
Diluted net earnings per share increased by one percent to $1.97. Core earnings per share increased one percent to $2.00 and Currency-neutral Core EPS was unchanged versus the prior year.
Reported gross margin for the quarter decreased 160 basis points versus the prior year. Core gross margin and currency-neutral Core gross margin for the quarter decreased 150 basis points versus the prior year and excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decrease was driven by 140 basis points of higher costs from commodities, 140 basis points of product reinvestments, 50 basis points of unfavorable mix and 10 basis points of rounding and other items, partially offset by 120 basis points of gross productivity savings, 50 basis points of tariff impact from lower costs and recognized recoveries and 20 basis points of increased pricing.
Reported selling, general and administrative expense (SG&A) as a percentage of sales declined 90 basis points versus year ago. Core SG&A as a percentage of sales decreased 80 basis points versus year ago and decreased 70 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core SG&A excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decline was driven by 130 basis points of productivity savings and 100 basis points of net sales growth leverage, partially offset by 120 basis points of reinvestments and 40 basis points of rounding and other items.
Reported operating margin for the quarter decreased 70 basis points versus the prior year. Excluding the impact of non-core restructuring charges, core operating margin decreased 80 basis points versus the prior year and decreased 90 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core operating margin included gross productivity savings of 250 basis points.
Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance
P&G updated its guidance range for fiscal 2027 all-in sales growth to be in the range of two to four percent versus the prior year, reflecting the acquisition of Thorne as of October 1, 2026. The Company maintained its outlook for organic sales growth in the range of one to three percent versus the prior year. Included in the organic sales growth guidance is a headwind of 30 to 50 basis points from brand, product form and go-to-market discontinuations.
P&G maintained its fiscal 2027 diluted net earnings per share growth to be in the range of one to five percent versus fiscal 2026 diluted net EPS of $6.62. P&G also maintained its fiscal 2027 core earnings per share growth to be in the range of in-line to three percent versus fiscal 2026 core EPS of $6.89. This outlook equates to a range of $6.89 to $7.11 per share, with a mid-point estimate of $7.00, or an increase of approximately one and a half percent.
P&G now expects a commodity cost headwind of approximately $1.4 billion after tax driven by higher raw materials, energy and transportation costs, $300 million after-tax from higher net interest expense, $150 million after-tax from lower non-operating income and $50 million after-tax from unfavorable foreign exchange rates. Combined, these impacts equate to a headwind of $0.79 per share for fiscal 2027, or an eleven percent drag on core EPS growth.
The Company is not able to reconcile its forward-looking non-GAAP cash flow and tax rate measures without unreasonable efforts given the unpredictability of the timing and amounts of discrete items, such as acquisitions, divestitures, or impairments, which could significantly impact GAAP results.
P&G now expects a core effective tax rate to be in the range of 20% to 21% in fiscal 2027.
Capital spending is estimated to be in the range of four and a half to five and a half percent of fiscal 2027 net sales.
P&G continues to expect free cash flow productivity of 85% to 90% and expects to pay over $10 billion in dividends and to repurchase approximately $5 billion of common shares in fiscal 2027.

documents.raw_text:
October 15, 2026Head & Shoulders Launches All-New Scalp Care Collection to Prove Healthier Hair Starts at the Scalp
A skincare-powered innovation for clinically proven scalp care from the #1 US Dermatologist recommended anti-dandruff brandCINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Head & Shoulders today unveiled its new Scalp Care Collection, a line of skincare-inspired shampoos, conditioners and treatments built to care for the scalp while delivering the hair benefits people desire most. The collection features three personalized regimens designed for specific scalp needs that are clinically proven to remove visible flakes at the source and repair the scalp barrier for healthier-looking hair, bringing a new level of beauty to a brand best known for scalp care.
“This launch marks a bold new chapter for the brand, one that removes dandruff and moves beyond just managing flakes to transforming how hair looks and feels by taking a skincare-inspired approach to common scalp concerns,” said Matt Krehbiel, Vice President, Head & Shoulders. “We're showing people that exceptional hair starts at the scalp through educational content and partnerships with trusted experts and relatable voices in beauty.”
The collection targets the root causes of scalp damage in three ways: gently removing flakes, fighting oxidative scalp stress and restoring the scalp barrier. The formulas feature the brand's HydraSC+ Complex, built on either 1.8% salicylic acid, which exfoliates and lifts away flakes and buildup, or 1% zinc pyrithione, which targets Malassezia, the scalp microbe associated with dandruff. Consumers can select the regimen best suited to their scalp concerns:
Scalp Soothe with Niacinamide (for itchy* scalps): Instant cooling and dandruff itch relief from the first use, with shampoo delivering an added boost of hair shine. The regimen includes the Cooling Shampoo and Cooling Scalp Spray, which can be used up to 4 times daily for relief between washes.
Scalp Purify with Salicylic Acid (for oily scalps): Instantly removes up to 99% of flakes, oil and buildup for up to 5x more volume in one color-safe, non-stripping routine. The regimen includes the Clarifying Pre-Shampoo and Volumizing Shampoo.
Scalp Restore with Bio-Ceramides (for dry scalps): Delivers 72-moisture lock and restores the scalp barrier for hydrated hair. The sulfate-free regimen includes the Nourishing Shampoo, Nourishing Conditioner and Nourishing Leave-On Serum.
Shampoos and conditioners within the Head & Shoulders Scalp Care Collection are now available at Walmart with a suggested MSRP of $11.99. Treatments and expanded availability at Walmart and other retailers arrive this November. For more information, visit headandshoulders.com or follow Head & Shoulders on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.
About Head & Shoulders
With 65 years of trailblazing innovation in scalp care, Head & Shoulders is the world’s #1 anti-dandruff shampoo, #1 US dermatologist-recommended anti-dandruff brand, and the most-awarded scalp care brand** with a broad portfolio of products with cosmetic benefits and solutions for different hair types and scalp concerns. For more information, visit www.headandshoulders.com or follow Head & Shoulders on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

October 14, 2026Think Your Toilet Paper Is Good Enough? Charmin Thinks You and Your Butt Deserve Better.
Porsha Williams partners with Charmin to encourage consumers to raise their standards with Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest innovation in more than a decade.
Charmin introduces new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade.
Distinguished by its 3D durable weave texture, the new Charmin Ultra Strong now has wider sheets that clean better so you can use up to 50% less*.
Porsha Williams is teaming up with Charmin to help raise toilet paper standards, bringing the brand's wider-sheet innovation to life through social content and an immersive New York City experience where consumers can discover the difference for themselves.
CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Today, Charmin unveils the new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade. Designed to deliver a better clean, new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets replaces the existing Ultra Strong product line with a wider-sheet design that provides more coverage and helps consumers use up to 50% less* toilet paper. Built on the belief that better changes everything, the innovation is designed to challenge what consumers expect from their toilet paper by delivering an upgrade consumers didn’t know they needed.
For many shoppers, toilet paper has long been a category where people settle for what's familiar, but Charmin wants to challenge that notion. Featuring its signature 3D diamond weave texture, Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets aims to raise the bar for what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. By combining greater coverage with the strength and durability people already love, the innovation creates an upgraded experience that redefines what “good enough” should look and feel like in the bathroom. That’s what happens when you get the upgrade you didn’t know you needed - better changes everything.
"Consumers may not think to ask for a wider sheet, but they do know a better clean when they feel it. With Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, we've taken something people use every day and made it meaningfully better by delivering more coverage, a better clean, and helping consumers use less,” said Alex Perez, Charmin Brand Vice President, Procter & Gamble. “For years, Ultra Strong has provided consumers strength and durability. Now, Charmin is building on that legacy with an innovation designed to redefine what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. Charmin Ultra Strong truly delivers a differentiated clean that consumers can’t unfeel.”
To help raise these toilet paper standards, Charmin is partnering with media personality, entrepreneur and Charmin loyalist Porsha Williams. She will be involved in the brand’s social campaign and will serve as the host of Charmin’s Wider Sheet immersive NYC experience on October 20. Visitors can join in on the fun by snapping photos with a one-of-a-kind Charmin vehicle inspired by the brand's campaign, meet the beloved Charmin bears and get up close with the new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets to see the difference for themselves.
“Listen, I’m not someone who settles for basic, so why would I do it with my toilet paper?” said Porsha Williams. “When I tried Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, I was mad nobody told me sooner. More coverage, a better clean, AND using less? That’s the kind of upgrade I can get behind. And honestly? Your backside will thank you."
New Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is available now at major retailers nationwide and online. To learn more, visit Charmin.com and follow @Charmin on social media.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets?
Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is the newest innovation in the Charmin Ultra Strong portfolio and the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade. The new Charmin Ultra Strong now features wider sheets that clean better.
How does the wider-sheet design improve the cleaning experience?
The New Charmin Ultra Strong has wider sheets* that cleans better* with more durable weave texture per sheet*, and sheets that are 4X stronger so you can use 50% less
How does Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets help consumers use less toilet paper?
Charmin Ultra Strong now features wider sheets* that clean better, so consumers can use up to 50% less* toilet paper.
What makes Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets different from previous versions?
The introduction of Wider Sheets marks the first major innovation to Charmin Ultra Strong in more than a decade. The enhanced design builds on the product’s signature strength while introducing increased coverage that helps improve the overall cleaning experience.
Where can consumers purchase Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets?
Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is available at major retailers nationwide and online. Consumers can visit Charmin.com for additional product information and retailer availability.
Are Wider Sheets the new standard for Charmin Ultra Strong?
Yes, as Charmin's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade, Wider Sheets are designed to raise expectations for what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. By providing a better clean while using less, Wider Sheets challenge the idea that "good enough" is good enough and help establish a new standard for toilet paper.

October 13, 2026

P&G Shareholders Also Elect All 12 P&G Director Nominees at 2026 Annual Meeting

CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) announced at today’s Annual Meeting of Shareholders that the P&G Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of $1.0885 per share on the Common Stock and on the Series A and Series B ESOP Convertible Class A Preferred Stock of the Company, payable on or after November 16, 2026 to Common Stock shareholders of record at the close of business on October 23, 2026, and to Series A and Series B ESOP Convertible Class A Preferred Stock shareholders of record at the start of business on October 23, 2026.

P&G has been paying a dividend for 136 consecutive years since its incorporation in 1890 and has increased its dividend for 70 consecutive years. This reinforces our commitment to return cash to shareowners, many of whom rely on the steady, reliable income earned with their investment in P&G.

Also at today’s Annual Meeting, P&G shareholders elected all 12 P&G Director nominees, with each receiving strong support according to preliminary voting results. Company shareholders also voted in favor of two Board proposals: to ratify the appointment of P&G's independent registered public accounting firm and for an advisory vote on executive compensation. Additionally, Company shareholders voted against three shareholder proposals.

The results of the vote announced today are considered preliminary until final results are tabulated and certified by the independent Inspector of Elections. Final results will be reported on a Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

We expect these trends will continue to strengthen our performance into 2027 and beyond because we have multiple engines of margin expansion and growth while maintaining our capital discipline.
Our vehicle portfolio continues to get stronger, with the launch of the next-generation Chevrolet Silverado LD and GMC Sierra LD starting in December
Our software and services ecosystem is expanding
Our manufacturing and sourcing footprint is becoming more efficient, and we will be onshoring significant production to further reduce our tariff exposure
And growth businesses like GM Defense and GM Insurance are creating additional avenues for value creation
All of this supports our commitment to ongoing margin expansion. We know there’s more work ahead, but we are building from a position of strength with a proven track record of execution, and I’d like to thank you for your continued confidence in the General Motors team.

To our Shareholders:
General Motors delivered another solid quarter of earnings, driven by the appeal of our product portfolio, the agility of our team, and disciplined execution.
Our employees, our dealers and our suppliers are all making important contributions that continue to drive our success. Their commitment enables us to win in a dynamic market, and their efforts are leading us to raise our 2026 guidance for the second time.
The business continues to perform very well. Customer demand in North America remains strong driven by our very attractive lineup of pickups and SUVs. Pricing is consistent, and we delivered the best quarter and first half ever for new Super Cruise-equipped vehicles.
Our 8.6% EBIT-adjusted margin in North America was up 2.5 points from a year ago, and we continue to lower our warranty costs, reduce EV losses, and increase operating efficiency. In addition, GM International, inclusive of our China joint ventures, was profitable.
We expect these trends will continue to strengthen our performance into 2027 and beyond because we have multiple engines of margin expansion and growth while maintaining our capital discipline.
Our vehicle portfolio continues to get stronger, with the launch of the next-generation Chevrolet Silverado LD and GMC Sierra LD starting in December
Our software and services ecosystem is expanding
Our manufacturing and sourcing footprint is becoming more efficient, and we will be onshoring significant production to further reduce our tariff exposure
And growth businesses like GM Defense and GM Insurance are creating additional avenues for value creation
All of this supports our commitment to ongoing margin expansion. We know there’s more work ahead, but we are building from a position of strength with a proven track record of execution, and I’d like to thank you for your continued confidence in the General Motors team.
