1. Consolidated Financial Results for FY2027 First Half
Financial Results
Consolidated vehicle unit sales in Japan and overseas decreased by 25 thousand units, or 0.5%, to 4,758
thousand units in FY2027 first half (the first half ended September 30, 2026) compared with FY2026 first half
(the first half ended September 30, 2025). Vehicle unit sales in Japan increased by 54 thousand units, or 5.6%, to
1,024 thousand units in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. Meanwhile, overseas vehicle unit
sales decreased by 79 thousand units, or 2.1%, to 3,734 thousand units in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026
first half.
The results of operations for FY2027 first half were as follows:
Sales revenues 26,962.4 billion yen (an increase of 2,331.7 billion yen
or 9.5% compared with FY2026 first half)
Operating income 2,191.1 billion yen (an increase of 185.4 billion yen
or 9.2% compared with FY2026 first half)
Income before income taxes 2,954.4 billion yen (an increase of 476.2 billion yen
or 19.2% compared with FY2026 first half)
Net income attributable to
Toyota Motor Corporation 2,236.4 billion yen (an increase of 463.0 billion yen
or 26.1% compared with FY2026 first half)
The changes in operating income were as follows:
Marketing efforts an increase of 165.0 billion yen
Effects of changes in exchange rates an increase of 685.0 billion yen
Cost reduction efforts a decrease of 340.0 billion yen
Increase or decrease in expenses
and expense reduction efforts a decrease of 20.0 billion yen
Other a decrease of 304.6 billion yen

[[PAGE 6]]
TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION FY2027 Semi-Annual Financial Summary
Segment Operating Results
(1) Automotive:
Sales revenues for the automotive operations segment increased by 1,880.5 billion yen, or 8.5%, to
23,981.1 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased by
112.7 billion yen, or 7.6%, to 1,598.2 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The
increase in operating income was mainly due to the effects of changes in exchange rates.
(2) Financial services:
Sales revenues for the financial services operations segment increased by 431.7 billion yen, or 18.5%,
to 2,762.0 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased
by 21.9 billion yen, or 4.9%, to 472.3 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The
increase in operating income was mainly due to increase in loan balance.
(3) All other:
Sales revenues for all other businesses increased by 203.0 billion yen, or 27.6%, to 938.9 billion yen
in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased by 60.1 billion yen, or
87.3%, to 129.0 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half.
Geographic Information
(1) Japan:
Sales revenues in Japan increased by 1,239.2 billion yen, or 11.8%, to 11,752.5 billion yen in FY2027
first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased by 136.2 billion yen, or 12.2%, to
1,253.3 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The increase in operating income
was mainly due to the effects of changes in exchange rates.
(2) North America:
Sales revenues in North America increased by 1,453.6 billion yen, or 13.9%, to 11,922.1 billion yen in
FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased by 234.0 billion yen to
166.1 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The increase in operating income was
mainly due to the decrease in expenses and expense reduction efforts.
(3) Europe:
Sales revenues in Europe increased by 609.1 billion yen, or 19.4%, to 3,755.6 billion yen in FY2027
first half compared with FY2026 first half, and operating income increased by 18.4 billion yen, or 9.2%, to
219.2 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The increase in operating income was
mainly due to marketing efforts.
(4) Asia:
Sales revenues in Asia increased by 225.8 billion yen, or 5.1%, to 4,677.3 billion yen in FY2027 first
half compared with FY2026 first half. However, operating income decreased by 7.1 billion yen, or 1.6%, to
437.1 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The decrease in operating income was
mainly due to the increase in expenses and others.
(5) Other (Central and South America, Oceania, Africa and the Middle East):
Sales revenues in other regions increased by 331.0 billion yen, or 14.2%, to 2,658.2 billion yen in
FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. However, operating income decreased by 0.9 billion yen,
or 0.5%, to 200.9 billion yen in FY2027 first half compared with FY2026 first half. The decrease in operating
income was mainly due to the effects of marketing activities.

income of Hino Motors, Ltd. ("Hino") (automotive segment) and its consolidated subsidiaries were
reclassified as held for sale, and were presented as assets held for sale, liabilities directly associated with
assets held for sale, and other comprehensive income associated with assets held for sale. For the first half
ended September 30, 2026, Toyota lost control of Hino as a result of the business integration. The loss of
¥95,445 million associated with the loss of control is included in "Other finance costs" in the condensed
semi-annual consolidated statement of income.
(ⅱ) Review of capital relationship with Toyota Industries Corporation
At the end of the year ended March 31, 2026, Toyota reclassified its holdings of Toyota Industries
Corporation ("Toyota Industries") (automotive segment) shares and related other comprehensive income as
held for sale. Accordingly, investments accounted for using the equity method were included in assets held
for sale, and related other comprehensive income was included in other comprehensive income associated
with assets held for sale. For the first half ended September 30, 2026, Toyota completed the sale of its shares
in Toyota Industries.

Despite a challenging competitive environment, continued improvement efforts led to a YoY increase in
profit and an upward revision to the FY2027 forecast.
Operating income 2.2 trillion yen (+0.2 trillion yen YoY)
- Mitigated the impact on earnings through swift responses to changes in the external environment ,
including the situation in the Middle East.
- Supported by strong demand, vehicle sales remained resilient, led by HEVs
Operating income 3.9 trillion yen
(+0.5 trillion yen from the previous forecast, +0.1 trillion yen YoY)
- Mitigated the impact of rising materials prices and production disruptions caused by earthquakes
and floods through recovery efforts at production sites and optimized global supply, thereby
maintaining consolidated vehicle sales.
- In addition to reduced tariff-related costs, through the accumulation of improvement efforts, including
the expansion of value chain earnings, we expect year-on-year profit growth, and have revised our
forecast upward.
- We will maintain our policy to increase dividends in a stable manner to reward our long -term
shareholders.
Interim : 50 yen (+5 yen YoY) / Full-year (forecast) : 100 yen (+5 yen YoY)
- Share repurchase authorization : Increase by 300 billion yen (FY total：1.3 trillion yen)
- Share cancellation : Additional 1 billion shares of treasury stock (FY total：1.2 billion shares)
We have reduced the level of treasury stock holdings and will pursue capital policies focused on

documents.title: Healthcare and Life Sciences Leaders Build on NVIDIA to Advance Drug Discovery and Expand Patient Care
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design debut RFD4-Proteina, a new open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities, unlocking new frontiers in biology.

• Siemens Healthineers is advancing the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy, using NVIDIA intelligence to increase access to life-saving cancer care with agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and robotic control.

• Automata, Benchling, Biolevate, Boltz, Danaher, Hologen and Therna Biosciences are using the NVIDIA BioNeMo open platform to develop scientific agents that connect drug design, autonomous laboratories and biological discovery, helping researchers move from hypothesis to experiments faster.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced collaborations with leading global healthcare and research organizations to advance protein design — including through a newly released open model, RFD4-Proteina — accelerate drug discovery and bring greater precision to cancer care.

Life sciences researchers must search vast biological design spaces and aim to shorten the cycle between computational design and laboratory testing to discover new medicines. Cancer care teams face a different challenge: translating complex imaging and treatment data into precise plans for each patient.

NVIDIA open models, accelerated computing and physical intelligence can help experts evaluate more possibilities faster, from designing new proteins to planning adaptive radiotherapy.

“Agentic and physical AI are opening new possibilities across medicine, from designing proteins and powering autonomous laboratories to improving personalized cancer care,” said Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at NVIDIA. “Together with healthcare and life science leaders, we’re accelerating scientific discovery and advancing more precise, accessible care around the world.”

NVIDIA and the UW Institute for Protein Design Introduce RFD4-Proteina Proteins are molecular tools that perform many of life’s essential tasks, and designing new versions could open paths to new medicines, diagnostics and industrial applications. But finding a protein capable of performing a designed function requires searching an immense range of possible designs.

NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design are debuting RFD4-Proteina, a new NVIDIA BioNeMo™ open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities.

The model generates targeted protein designs, enabling scientists and agents to search and refine designs using molecular inputs, constraints and scoring objectives. Potential applications include designing proteins to interrupt disease processes or detect signs of disease in diagnostic tests.

In testing reported in the research draft, RFD4-Proteina achieved higher computational design success rates and generation throughput than the evaluated baselines across four benchmark suites: protein binding, small-molecule binding, enzyme scaffolding and DNA binding. The model helps researchers explore and prioritize candidates for laboratory testing, where experiments establish how a design performs under tested conditions.

“We are moving from an era of discovering the proteins nature has made to one in which we can design entirely new ones,” said David Baker, 2024 Nobel Laureate in chemistry and director of the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington. “RFD4-Proteina expands what scientists can create, from proteins that could advance drug discovery to enzymes that break down pesticides. Making the model open will allow researchers around the world to build on these capabilities and pursue solutions once beyond the reach.”

RFD4-Proteina is available today through partners including Amazon Bio Discovery, Anthropic’s Claude Science, Benchling, Databricks, Google Cloud, Hugging Face, Nebius, OpenAI and Tamarind Bio, enabling researchers and developers to integrate the open protein design model into agent, cloud and scientific computing workflows.

Siemens Healthineers Advances Cancer Care With NVIDIA Siemens Healthineers and NVIDIA are collaborating to develop the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy with agentic and robotic intelligence, combining imaging and oncology expertise with accelerated computing and simulation to simplify workflows and expand access to care.

By 2050, approximately 35 million people worldwide are projected to be diagnosed with cancer each year. Care teams face growing pressure to deliver precise, personalized treatment while managing limited specialist capacity. Greater efficiency can help expand access to care while maintaining the precision needed to deliver prescribed doses to tumors and protect surrounding healthy tissue.

Siemens Healthineers is working with NVIDIA to further develop adaptive radiotherapy through agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and real-time computing. NVIDIA Nemotron™ open foundation models are being explored to power agentic co-planning, with the aim of helping oncologists evaluate and refine personalized treatment strategies. The models could then be combined with NVIDIA CUDA®-accelerated dose calculation for rapid patient-specific simulation and the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to connect live sensor data with AI and simulation to support adaptive treatment.

“Adaptive radiotherapy is built on a single principle: treatment should adapt to the patient, not the other way around,” said Arthur Kaindl, head of Varian, the Siemens Healthineers cancer-care business. “We’ve made important advances in precision and adaptation — most recently, with the launch of the Accela system. Our collaboration with NVIDIA builds on that progress, exploring how AI and real-time computing could give clinicians greater speed and insight to make informed decisions, adapt treatment with greater confidence and deliver personalized care to more patients.”

Scientific Agents Advance Drug Discovery and Development Life sciences is one of the world’s most important scientific frontiers, with global scientific R&D reaching $3.8 trillion and annual pharmaceutical budgets approaching $300 billion.

Scientific agents and autonomous laboratories can help turn more of that investment into evidence, insight and, ultimately, new treatments by connecting design, experimentation and learning in a continuous cycle.

To accelerate discovery and free up scientists for work only they can do, research and laboratory technology companies are using NVIDIA BioNeMo — an open development platform that enables AI-driven biology and drug discovery — alongside Nemotron and other NVIDIA technologies to develop scientific agents and the specialized models and tools that connect drug design, scientific data and laboratory workflows:

• Benchling is grounding agents in experimental data, research context and connected scientific workflows.

• Biolevate is connecting biological data, specialized scientific tools and agentic reasoning across drug discovery and development.

• Boltz is developing specialized models and tools that scientific agents can use to predict molecular structures and design and evaluate candidates. It is also previewing a scientific agent to plan workflows, apply the right models and interpret results to guide the next experiment.

• Automata is connecting scientific agents with automated laboratory infrastructure so they can initiate experiments and capture structured, contextualized results through workflows.

• Genedata’s AI co-scientist will coordinate protein design and testing in the protein design foundry within Danaher’s autonomous lab. The workflow will incorporate RFD4-Proteina, helping scientists use experimental results to guide the next round of designs.

• Hologen is combining its large medicine models with NVIDIA Nemotron to build AI clinical scientists that help researchers turn imaging and clinical data into insights about patient outcomes to inform clinical trial design.

• Therna Biosciences is using large language model reasoning to connect experimental evidence and RNA medicine design, helping scientists turn biological insights into therapeutic candidates.

NVIDIA Open Models Streamline Hospital Operations, Expand Access to Specialized Care Healthcare systems across Europe are working to expand access to specialized care while reducing the administrative demands on already-stretched care teams.

Avelios, Corti, Dedalus, Dawn Health and Sword are also building on NVIDIA Nemotron, powering everything from AI scribes and AI-assisted clinical care to personalized patient support services.

PolyAI is building on NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to speed the path to care through its multilingual dialog deployment with medical software provider Corilus, which has a network spanning more than 70,000 healthcare professionals across Belgium and France.

Apian and VitVio are extending this into the physical world, using NVIDIA Cosmos™ world models and NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries to build digital twins that monitor and improve hospital operations.

documents.title: NVIDIA, Nokia and Leading Telecom Operators Turn Networks Into Distributed Intelligence Platforms
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:

• Leading global telecom operators are expanding NVIDIA-powered computing across their networks to deliver advanced services closer to people and businesses, improve wireless experience and automate network operations.

• T-Mobile completes the world’s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, while BT, Deutsche Telekom and Elisa announce AI-RAN pilots on live networks using Nokia’s CUDA-accelerated anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, and NVIDIA introduces new Aerial RAN Computer configurations for high-capacity sites.

• Nine EMEA telecom operators are building and expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure across centralized and distributed locations.

• Operators and software partners are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron open models to deliver agentic services and develop agents for autonomous network operations.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced that leading global telecom operators are turning their networks into distributed intelligence platforms, adding NVIDIA accelerated computing to centralized data centers, metro sites and cell sites so they can serve models and applications closer to the people, businesses and machines that use them.

T-Mobile has completed the world’s first AI-RAN call on a live network in Bellevue, Washington, with NVIDIA and Nokia. Deutsche Telekom is advancing physical AI for industries, and Orange is introducing new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Elisa has completed Europe’s first field trial of AI-RAN, running voice, mobile data and vision AI together on a single accelerated computing platform over 5G, and BT is preparing live AI-RAN trials in the U.K. Nokia is bringing its anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) for trials at BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange.

Nine operators across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, while Nokia and Cisco are incorporating NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into the software operators use to run autonomous networks.

“Telecom networks were built to carry the world’s conversations. Now, they will also carry the world’s intelligence,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Leading global operators are turning their land, power and connectivity into a distributed AI infrastructure — bringing intelligence closer to the industries, people and robots that use it. With Nokia, we’re extending accelerated computing into the radio network itself, creating the foundation for AI-native 5G.”

Intelligence is built in five layers: land, power and shell, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Telecom operators already own sovereign infrastructure at the first layer, with data centers, regional sites and cell sites that have power, fiber and spectrum.

By adding NVIDIA accelerated computing, open models and applications on top, operators are building the full intelligence stack into their networks. At distributed sites, a common converged platform based on the AI-RAN architecture can serve open models, power robotics, voice and agentic applications, and run intelligent 5G software.

Europe’s Leading Telcos Build Distributed Infrastructure Infrastructure sits at the foundation of telecom’s transition to distributed service platforms.

Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its NVIDIA-powered Industrial AI Cloud, which hosts open models — including NVIDIA Nemotron and Soofi — and serves robotics companies such as Agile Robots. At distributed sites, Deutsche Telekom is piloting AI-RAN trials with Nokia and NVIDIA, and demonstrating NVIDIA ARC to run inference between the device and the network edge.

A GTC Berlin demonstration with Agile Robots shows the approach: on-robot intelligence handles real-time perception and action, a model at the distributed edge supports fine-tuning and coordination across robots, and the central infrastructure provides capacity for larger training workloads.

Orange is hosting open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron, as a managed service on top of its Live Intelligence trusted AI platform, enabling new advanced services for enterprises. At distributed sites, Orange is deploying NVIDIA ARC for voice intelligence applications using Nemotron Speech, demonstrating new services to help emergency and field services teams translate across multiple languages in real time with low latency and reliability.

Elisa has deployed NVIDIA ARC at a distributed network location, running a voice intelligence application that serves as an enterprise assistant, and is using open models to build edge applications.

EMEA telcos are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure:

• New infrastructure: CRA in the Czech Republic, etisalat in the United Arab Emirates, Silknet in Georgia and TIM in Italy.

• Expansions: Cassava in Africa, Deutsche Telekom in Germany, Fastweb + Vodafone in Italy, Kazakhtelecom in Central Asia and Orion Telecom in Serbia.

AI-RAN Brings Accelerated Computing Into the Radio Network AI-RAN extends accelerated computing into the radio access network (RAN), turning it into an intelligence workload that runs on the same platform as advanced services, so operators can get more out of their spectrum while serving demand from sites close to users.

Globally, nearly 20 telecom operators have publicly announced AI-RAN collaborations using Nokia anyRAN software and NVIDIA ARC.

• T-Mobile recently marked the world’s first AI-RAN call on its commercial network in Bellevue, Washington, running on commercial ARC servers, Nokia’s NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated RAN software and massive multiple-input multiple-output radios, and connected to an existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone.

• BT is planning live AI-RAN trials in Birmingham, England, with Nokia and NVIDIA in 2027.

• Deutsche Telekom has validated Nokia and NVIDIA’s commercial AI-RAN platform in Bonn and Oulu labs, including AI-enhanced uplink channel estimation to improve uplink user throughput, with plans to move to field trials in 2027.

• Elisa simultaneously ran voice, mobile data and video analytics on the NVIDIA ARC platform, marking a European first in Elisa’s over-the-air field environment using 5G spectrum. The trial clears the way for distributed deployment and commercial AI-RAN services in 2027.

• Orange is testing Nokia 5G software on NVIDIA ARC, focusing on AI-RAN spectral efficiency improvements and support for edge services in live networks.

NVIDIA is introducing two ARC configurations — MGX 2U and MGX 4U — designed for dense, high-capacity intelligence and radio workloads, typically deployed at centralized RAN sites. Powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO™ 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, the configurations will offer x86 and NVIDIA Vera CPU options. Dell Technologies, Quanta Cloud Technology and Supermicro will offer ARC-ready servers.

Open Models Power Autonomous Network Operations Leading telcos are using open models and agents to speed progress toward fully autonomous network operations. NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software are now integrated into leading partners’ commercial software, powering specialized agents built for telecom network workflows.

Nokia is integrating NVIDIA Nemotron into its Autonomous Networks Suite and using NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software to build and deploy trusted agents that manage operations across fixed, radio, core and transport networks.

Cisco has fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron models and integrated them into Crosswork AI, creating a common agentic layer across its Crosswork Network Automation software to manage IP and optical transport networks. The company is also using NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to help telcos operate agents safely.

TCS is working with telcos to fine-tune NVIDIA Nemotron models and use NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to build specialized agents that validate radio-site builds, detect, diagnose and auto-remediate network issues, and deliver multilingual voice experiences. BT is adopting Nemotron to build agents that inspect field-installation photos, detect problems and help reduce repeat site visits.

NTT DATA is extending its NextGenOSS platform with fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to build agents that detect early network degradation, identify likely root causes and recommend next actions.

• Eaton Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Results

• Third quarter sales increased 28%, with organic sales growth of 19%, above the high end of guidance

• Twelve-month rolling average organic orders increased 39% in Electrical Americas, 51% in Electrical Global and 20% in Aerospace, with order dollars reaching record levels in all three segments, driven by broad end-market strength

• Strong year-over-year total backlog growth of 46% in Electrical and 33% in Aerospace

• Record segment margins of 25.3%, above the high end of guidance, with Electrical Americas margins improving 230 basis points sequentially

• Announced agreement to acquire COL Group, expanding manufacturing capacity and power distribution capabilities for data center and utility markets in Europe

• Full year 2026 earnings per share expected to be between $10.39 and $10.49; adjusted earnings per share expected to be between $13.70 and $13.80​

DUBLIN – Intelligent power management company Eaton Corporation plc (NYSE:ETN) today reported strong third quarter 2026 results, including earnings per share of $2.77. Adjusted earnings per share were a record of $3.68, excluding charges of $0.62 per share related to intangible amortization, $0.30 per share related to acquisitions and divestitures, and income of $0.01 per share related to a multi-year restructuring program.

Sales in the quarter were a record $8.9 billion, up 28% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 19% growth in organic sales, 8% growth from acquisitions, and 1% growth from foreign exchange.

Segment margins were a record 25.3%, 30 basis points above both the high end of the guidance range and the third quarter of 2025, driven by higher sales and improved performance amid continued capacity investments to support growth.

The Company continued to generate solid cash flow, supporting investment in growth initiatives while maintaining financial flexibility. Operating cash flow was $1.31 billion, and free cash flow was $1.03 billion.

Paulo Ruiz, Eaton chief executive officer, said, “Our strong third quarter performance reflects the focus and discipline our teams have demonstrated all year as we expand capacity, strengthen execution and position the business to meet accelerating customer demand. We delivered organic growth and segment margins above the high end of our guidance, driven by strong demand across our markets and continued momentum across our Electrical businesses. Record orders grew sequentially, backlog continued to expand, and we remain well-positioned to help customers deliver on their critical power infrastructure investments. These results reinforce our confidence in the remainder of the year.”

In the quarter, the company also announced an agreement to acquire COL Group, a leader in medium-voltage electrical distribution solutions, expanding the company’s European power distribution capabilities and manufacturing footprint and enhancing its ability to support growing customer demand across data center and utility markets.

Guidance

For the full year 2026, the company anticipates:

• Organic growth of 13-15%

• Segment margins of 24.1-24.5%

• Earnings per share between $10.39 and $10.49

• Adjusted earnings per share between $13.70 and $13.80

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the company anticipates:

• Organic growth of 13-15%

• Segment margins of 25.4-25.8%

• Earnings per share between $3.28 and $3.38

• Adjusted earnings per share between $4.05 and $4.15

Business Segment Results

Demand remained robust across key end markets, as sales for the Electrical Americas segment were a record $4.2 billion, up 22% organically from the third quarter of 2025. Operating profits were a record $1.2 billion, up 20% over the third quarter of 2025, and operating margins in the quarter were 29.8%, up 230 basis points sequentially.

The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 39% organically. Total backlog at the end of September remained strong and was up 33% over September 2025.

Sales for the Electrical Global segment were a record $2.7 billion, up 58% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 27% growth in organic sales and 31% contribution from Boyd Thermal in its second full quarter post-acquisition. Operating profits were a record $576 million, up 75% over the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins in the quarter were 21.1%, up 200 basis points over the third quarter of 2025.

The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 51% organically. Total backlog at the end of September was up 121% over September 2025.

On a rolling twelve-month basis, the book-to-bill ratio for the Electrical businesses remained strong at 1.2.

Aerospace segment sales were a third quarter record $1.2 billion, up 11% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 6% growth in organic sales and 5% growth from the Ultra PCS acquisition. Operating profits were a third quarter record $298 million, up 6% over the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins of 24.9% were down 100 basis points over the third quarter of 2025.

The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 20% organically. Total backlog at the end of September was up 33% over September 2025. On a rolling twelve-month basis, the book-to-bill ratio for the Aerospace segment remained strong at 1.2.

The Mobility segment posted sales of $852 million. Organic sales increased 9%. Operating profits were $146 million, up 39% from the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins in the quarter of 17.2% were up 370 basis points from the third quarter of 2025.

Eaton is an intelligent power management company dedicated to protecting the environment and improving the quality of life for people everywhere. We make products for the data center, utility, industrial, commercial and institutional, machine building, residential, aerospace and mobility markets. We are guided by our commitment to do business right, to operate sustainably and to help our customers manage power ─ today and well into the future. By capitalizing on the global growth trends of electrification and digitalization, we’re helping to solve the world’s most urgent power management challenges and building a more sustainable society for people today and generations to come.

Founded in 1911, Eaton has continuously evolved to meet the changing and expanding needs of our stakeholders. With revenues of $27.4 billion in 2025, the company serves customers in 180 countries. For more information, visit www.eaton.com. Follow us on LinkedIn.

Notice of conference call: Eaton’s conference call to discuss its third quarter results is available to all interested parties today as a live audio webcast at 11 a.m. United States Eastern time at Eaton.com/investor under “Presentations.” This news release can also be accessed on that page. Also available on the website before the call will be a presentation on third quarter results, which will be covered during the call.

Forward-Looking Statements

This news release contains forward-looking statements concerning fourth quarter and full year 2026 earnings per share, adjusted earnings per share, organic growth and segment margins; impact of acquisitions and portfolio changes on near- and long-term financial results; anticipated multi-year restructuring program charges and savings; the anticipated separation and divestiture of the Mobility business; and the anticipated acquisition of COL Group. These statements should be used with caution and are subject to various risks and uncertainties, many of which are outside the company’s control. AMD Builds the Classical Foundation for Quantum’s Future
documents.raw_text:
The future of quantum computing will depend on bringing quantum and classical computing together at unprecedented scale. Leadership-class classical computing is essential to managing quantum systems, accelerating complex simulations, correcting errors and integrating quantum processors with HPC clusters at scale. With leadership technologies spanning CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs and open software, AMD is uniquely positioned to build that foundation.

Today, AMD is applying its classical computing leadership to that challenge through a new codesign platform for quantum error correction established by IBM and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The collaboration provides a shared environment to evaluate the architectures, software and workflows that future hybrid quantum systems will require.

The new codesign platform will draw on the experiences of all three partners. IBM brings quantum computing technology, ORNL brings its scientific research and computing environment, and AMD brings the classical computing technologies and open software to connect quantum processing with scientific workloads.

The first deployment brings together IBM quantum computers, including the 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and the Umbra HPC system, powered by AMD EPYC™ CPUs and AMD Instinct™ GPUs, in a colocated environment.

Your browser doesn't support embedded video. Download the file instead.

“Building useful quantum systems requires the quantum and classical computing communities to solve system design challenges together," Ralph Wittig, Corporate Fellow, Head of Research & Advanced Development, AMD. "AMD brings expertise across CPUs, GPUs and FPGAs, from real-time control to leadership-class supercomputing. With IBM, Oak Ridge and our ecosystem partners, we are applying that experience to develop and test how quantum processors, classical computing and software can work together at scale.”

This work builds on AMD’s experience powering leadership-class supercomputers and an ongoing collaboration with IBM across GPU-accelerated scientific calculations and FPGA-based error decoding.

Designing the Classical Foundation

Integrating quantum and classical computing requires matching different processing requirements within one system. Control and feedback demand precise timing and rapid responses. Scientific calculations require substantial parallel processing. And orchestration coordinates work across all these resources.

AMD works together with the ecosystem and its partners through deep codesign to utilize its broad high-performance portfolio to address the classical computing requirements of quantum systems from real-time control through leadership-scale scientific computing. AMD brings expertise across these requirements:

• AMD EPYC™ CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate complex hybrid classical-quantum systems.

AMD EPYC™ CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate complex hybrid classical-quantum systems.

• AMD Instinct™ GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads.

AMD Instinct™ GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads.

• AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities required near the quantum processor.

AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities required near the quantum processor.

• AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem helps developers connect HPC and AI applications and this hardware into increasingly integrated quantum-classical environments.

AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem helps developers connect HPC and AI applications and this hardware into increasingly integrated quantum-classical environments.

Together, these technologies give quantum developers, system builders and research institutions a scalable classical foundation they can design around today.

AMD and Its Role in Quantum's Future

Error correction is what stands between the quantum computers we have today and the ones that can perform real science. Solving for that takes work on both quantum and classical computing, with a large part of it being on the classical side. Error correction requires quantum researchers to understand processors and classical computing as the two systems work side by side. The new codesign platform gives AMD, IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory a shared environment to investigate those requirements together as they continue support for the Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis Mission and its progress toward a scientifically relevant quantum computer by 2028.

Plans call for connecting the platform with the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), which also houses, ORNL’s new Lux SI (Super Intelligence) + HPC supercomputer, powered by AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Instinct GPUs. Those connections will extend the research environment to the full-scale system necessary to explore how integrated quantum, AI and scientific computing can accelerate scientific discoveries and national security.

For AMD, the work reflects a foundational principle: Advances in quantum computing depend on progress in classical computing. By working with IBM and ORNL to investigate those requirements now, AMD shapes the computing foundation that future quantum computers will need. AMD is codesigning a holistic system with quantum companies, research institutions and technology providers.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 3, 2026 ― AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue was $13.4 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.8 billion, net income was $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.46. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 56%, operating income was $3.9 billion, net income was $3.5 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.09.

“We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year,” said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. “Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and ‘Venice’ production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years.”

“Third quarter revenue grew 45% year-over-year to a record $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 74%, demonstrating the significant operating leverage in our business model as our Data Center business drives scale,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our Data Center portfolio.”

Segment Summary

• Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs.

Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs.

• Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors. Gaming business revenue was $773 million, down 40% year-over-year, due to lower semi-custom and graphics revenue.

Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors. • Embedded segment revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29% year-over-year, led by growth in aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets.

Embedded segment revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29% year-over-year, led by growth in aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets.

Recent Highlights

• AMD solutions and software are powering superintelligence infrastructure at scale: Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running models and workloads on the first AMD Helios™ rackscale solutions, powered by AMD Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. HPE announced that Vultr will deploy the first AMD Helios by HPE systems. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure announced its OCI Compute E7 cloud compute instances will be powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs, supporting enterprise applications and the CPU services surrounding models. AMD introduced the AMD Helion reference architecture, an open, flexible blueprint for building rack-scale agentic systems that lets customers configure the mix of CPUs and GPUs based on their workloads. AMD ROCm™ 10 was released, bringing AI-native developer experiences to AMD platforms with ROCm.AI, along with performance improvements and updated libraries, compilers, frameworks, tools and model support. The EuroHPC JU selected AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors to power the LUMI-AI supercomputer. Google Cloud and Microsoft announced general availability of storage-optimized cloud instances powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs.

Current Outlook

AMD’s outlook statements are based on current expectations. The following statements are forward-looking and actual results could differ materially depending on market conditions and the factors set forth under “Cautionary Statement” below.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, AMD expects revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The mid-point of the revenue range represents year-over-year growth of approximately 66% and a sequential increase of approximately 27%. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be approximately 55%.

AMD Teleconference

AMD will hold a conference call at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) today to discuss its third quarter 2026 financial results. AMD will provide a real-time audio broadcast of the teleconference on the Investor Relations page of its website at www.amd.com.

documents.title: What Is the Intel 14A PDK 0.9, and Why Does It Matter to Foundry...
documents.raw_text:
The Intel 14A process design kit (PDK) 0.9 gives foundry customers a more mature, silicon-validated environment for designing products on the Intel 14A process node. This milestone is an important step toward the Intel 14A PDK 1.0 and high-volume manufacturing readiness.

• Print

• Email

• Copy Link

Silicon process technologies provide a range of transistors, interconnects and specialized features that chip designers leverage to build their products. For a foundry customer to use these features, they need a way to incorporate them into their designs.

This is where the process design kit (PDK) comes in. A PDK serves as the interface between the process technology and the design tools engineers use to turn their ideas into silicon. If you think of a chip as a microscopic but vast city, a PDK is the digital building codes, approved building materials, and helpful resources that allow a designer to create a successful product.

Intel Foundry recently announced the general availability of the PDK 0.9 for the Intel 14A process node, an important milestone that allows customers to use the technology in an environment closer to full scale production. We asked Ben Sell, who leads Intel 14A and advanced nodes development, and Ali Farhang, who oversees PDKs and design enablement, to talk about the importance of this release, PDKs in general, and what’s next for the Intel 14A node.

Let’s start with the basics. What exactly is a PDK, and why is it important when you develop a new process technology?

Ali: A Process Design Kit, or PDK, is essentially the ultimate reference guide for a chip designer to create a product on a specific manufacturing process. It brings together the models, design rules, and other supporting materials that electronic design automation (EDA) tools use to help a customer bring their product from concept to mass production.

Just as importantly, the PDK release lifecycle serves as the clock that orchestrates technology development. Each revision represents a milestone of technology maturity, synchronizing our internal research and development, EDA and IP ecosystem partners, and customer design teams on a single, shared schedule.

Can you tell us what it means for Intel Foundry to announce general availability of the Intel 14A PDK 0.9?

Ben: From a customer perspective, the PDK 0.9 gives customers the confidence to design products on Intel 14A, as the technology is reaching the industry-standard performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, supported by silicon-backed validation.

Process technologies take time to mature for production, but customers want early access to begin design evaluation to enable time-to-market. With PDK 0.9, customers can create designs that go into the fab for production around the time a process node is certified. As we approach PDK 1.0, it says that we are confident that this process technology is on track for high volume manufacturing.

Ali: In the foundry business, trust is paramount. For fabless customers, selecting a foundry is one of the most consequential decisions they make. If a foundry does not deliver, the impact on a customer’s business can be profound. The general availability of Intel 14A PDK 0.9 is a critical milestone demonstrating that Intel Foundry can execute on its commitments.

How are things going so far with Intel 14A, and how does that translate into your confidence in the PDK releases?

Ben: We are pleased with the pace of progress on Intel 14A and encouraged by the feedback we are receiving from customers. That progress reflects both a strong technology foundation and the growing maturity of how we develop and deliver a foundry process.

Intel 14A builds on proven backside power delivery architecture with PowerDirect and gate-all-around transistor technology with RibbonFET 2, and with Turbo Cells added to give designers greater flexibility on optimizing performance and efficiency depending on their needs. The node incorporates extensive learning and manufacturing knowledge from Intel 18A, increased investment in inline detection, modeling and simulation to identify issues earlier, and several strategic initiatives to accelerate the pace of development.

Together, these capabilities are helping us improve Intel 14A performance, yield, variability and cycle time while staying aligned to our committed schedule that customers depend on to build their products.

That execution discipline is what gives us confidence in the PDK releases. Each release is grounded in silicon, so customers receive a progressively more accurate and complete representation of the technology. The PDK 0.9 is an important proof point that many customers use as a gate to start a design.

How is Intel Foundry working with the ecosystem around Intel 14A development?

Ali: Intel is partnering closely with leading EDA providers, including Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens, and Keysight, along with a broad ecosystem of IP partners, to deliver a comprehensive design platform for our foundry customers.

Earlier this year, Cadence, Keysight, Siemens and Synopsys announced design-tool certifications; in addition, Cadence and Intel launched a DTCO (Design Technology Co-Optimization) collaboration focused on optimizing Intel 14A for next-generation AI-driven design tools and IP.

As we advance toward future PDK releases, we continue to deepen engagement with ecosystem partners to validate and optimize design tools, IP, and flows, ensuring readiness at every stage of technology development. This ongoing collaboration provides customers with a predictable path to adoption, supported by a trusted ecosystem of certified solutions that accelerates design productivity and time-to-market.

Ben: From a technology development perspective, we are bringing in the broader ecosystem to help us achieve our results. This has required evolving our collaboration model with equipment and material suppliers, and earlier engagement from our process experts with suppliers to drive improvements in process and equipment capabilities. We hold regular executive summits and engineering review meetings to accelerate progress against critical deliverables.

What are you looking forward to next?

Ben: I am excited to translate the progress we are making on Intel 14A to customer success. Our immediate focus is to continue to improve performance, yield, variability and cycle time as we move toward the PDK 1.0 and volume production ready milestones. I am also looking forward to seeing customer designs advancing on Intel technologies and giving them the confidence they need to build their products with Intel Foundry as a trusted partner.

Ali: I’m looking forward to sustaining this level of quality across future releases and continuing to earn our customers’ trust by delivering on our commitments with a customer-first mindset. Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027.

I’m equally excited about the roadmap of node enhancements and performance scaling steps that will follow as Intel 14A matures. Our goal is to provide a highly stable, continuously optimized platform so our customers have the long-term capabilities they need to create differentiated, successful products for the AI era.

Meet The Experts

Ben Sell is a corporate vice president and general manager leading the front-end technology development for Intel Foundry. Ben joined Intel in 2002 and has been involved in the development of multiple advanced process nodes dating back to 65nm including 32nm, 22nm, 14nm, Intel 4 and Intel 18A. He started his career at Infineon Technologies working in DRAM capacitor pathfinding.

Ali Farhang is Corporate Vice President and General Manager of the Foundry Design Technology Platform (DTP) organization at Intel Foundry. With over 35 years of semiconductor leadership, Ali oversees the co-optimization of technology and design (DTCO), PDK development, foundational IP, reference flows, and strategic ecosystem enablement. He spent 25 years at Intel in lead product and technology enablement leadership roles before rejoining the company in 2025, following executive tenures as Corporate VP of Central Engineering at Micron and in the IP startup ecosystem.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a process design kit?

A process design kit, or PDK, is the reference guide chip designers use to create products on a specific manufacturing process. It brings together models, design rules and supporting materials used by electronic design automation tools.

What does the Intel 14A PDK 0.9 enable?

The Intel 14A PDK 0.9 gives customers a more mature, silicon-backed representation of the process technology for product design and production planning. It is an important milestone on the path toward the PDK 1.0 and high-volume manufacturing readiness.

What technologies are included in Intel 14A?

Intel 14A builds on the technologies in Intel 18A with RibbonFET 2 gate-all-around transistors, PowerDirect backside power delivery, and Turbo Cells, while incorporating manufacturing and development learning from Intel 18A.

What role does the ecosystem play in supporting Intel 14A development?

In addition to their use by customers, PDKs are also leveraged by electronic design automation (EDA) and IP providers to validate and certify their design tools and reusable IPs. Intel is working with a variety of ecosystem members to support the Intel 14A design platform.

What is the next Intel 14A PDK milestone?

The next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027.

Visit Intel.com to learn more about Intel Foundry’s process technologies.

documents.title: From Task to Fulfillment – Intel and SAP Demonstrate Physical AI and...
documents.raw_text:
• Print

• Email

• Copy Link

What New: Intel announced a collaboration with SAP to bridge business IT systems and the operational technology that controls physical equipment and processes through Physical AI. This initiative establishes a model in which business intent can drive physical action while status, outcomes and exceptions flow back into enterprise systems – a closed loop in action.

SAP and Intel demonstrated this through a proof of concept (PoC) showing how Physical AI can automate warehouse material handling by connecting the SAP Extended Warehouse Management’s (SAP EWM) business context and workflow orchestration with Intel-powered edge AI and robotics hardware and software, turning enterprise requests into autonomous robot tasks.

Requests are initiated in SAP EWM and are dispatched to autonomous robots with Intel’s edge AI hardware and software. The robots transport materials and report task status and completion back to SAP EWM, creating a closed loop between enterprise workflows and physical execution. The PoC demonstrated operational improvements, including a reduction in transport distance and less repetitive manual handling.

Why it Matters: Unlike standalone robot automation, the approach closes the IT/OT loop. SAP supplies the business context, governed workflows and process rules, while Intel provides an open, real-time edge AI foundation that enables robots to perceive, navigate and act locally. Status and exceptions are returned to enterprise systems, creating a reusable blueprint for a business-aware physical workforce that can scale across sites, robot vendors and use cases.

“Organizations want to connect AI directly to physical operations. By combining SAP’s enterprise context and orchestration with Intel’s edge AI and robotics technologies, we can help customers move Physical AI from business decision to real-world execution.” said John Healy, Vice President and General Manager, Industrial and Robotics, Intel.

“Physical AI can reshape operations by connecting enterprise systems with operational technology. SAP and Intel are creating solutions to help customers integrate AI-driven automation into core processes while preserving flexibility across robotics platforms, deployment models and ecosystem partners across both hardware and software.” said Dr. Lukasz Ostrowski, Head of Physical AI and Robotics, SAP Research and Innovation, SAP SE.

Intel’s Ricky Watts joins SAP President and Chief Product Officer of Autonomous Suites, Manoj Swaminathan on stage to discuss how Intel and SAP are working together to connect enterprise intelligence with Physical AI in the real world.

Intel and SAP showcase Physical AI in action with a live robotics demo at SAP TechEd.

From Proof of Concept to Enterprise Physical AI

The collaboration is designed to translate critical business decisions made in SAP systems into efficient, precise and responsive physical execution through SAP’s physical AI solutions and Intel’s foundational physical AI hardware and software capabilities.

Intel brings an edge AI and robotics foundation designed to operationalize and scale multimodal AI, including scalable heterogeneous compute (CPU, GPU and NPU working together) for local perception, inference, navigation, inspection and real-time control. Intel’s physical AI approach combines heterogeneous compute, industrial-ready silicon, real-time capabilities, and open software, including OpenVINO Physical AI, Physical AI Studio and Robotics AI Suite. Intel’s common hardware and software foundation can help consolidate mixed workloads, reduce integration fragmentation, preserve ecosystem choice and support progression from proof of concept to repeatable deployment.

Open and Agnostic Architecture

The open, robot-agnostic architecture is designed to preserve customer choice across robot vendors, operating systems, AI models, and cloud or on-premises deployment approaches. It is also designed to support scaling across platforms, sites and use cases without vendor lock-in.

Together, SAP and Intel aim to turn this proof of concept into a repeatable blueprint for enterprise Physical AI—helping customers scale intelligent automation across sites, robot platforms and operational use cases while preserving choice and flexibility.

About Intel

Intel (Nasdaq: INTC) designs and manufactures advanced semiconductors that connect and power the modern world. Every day, our engineers create new technologies that enhance and shape the future of computing to enable new possibilities for every customer we serve. Learn more at intel.com.

documents.title: Beyond the Medal: Samsung Helps Young Athletes Explore What Comes Next at Dakar 2026 - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
The Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 are under way in Senegal from October 31 to November 13, bringing together some 2,700 young athletes across 25 sports for the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent.

As a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, Samsung Electronics is supporting the Games with Galaxy technology — from Victory Selfie and broadcast integrations to the Samsung Open Station, an experience space inside the Youth Olympic Village. Having supported the Youth Olympic Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010, Samsung is going beyond technology at Dakar 2026 to support young athletes’ personal growth as well.

For the athletes competing at Dakar 2026, reaching the Olympic stage is the result of years of dedication. But some of the most lasting lessons come from what happens along the way — overcoming setbacks, building resilience, discovering what matters beyond results.

That is why, on November 3, Samsung hosted “Beyond the Medal: Your Journey Shapes What Comes Next,” a mentoring session at the Samsung Open Station inside the Youth Olympic Village. By bringing in athletes who have walked the Olympic path before them, the session aimed to inspire pride and motivation in the next generation — and to share the spirit of openness at the heart of Samsung’s Olympic partnership.

Two IOC Athlete Role Models1 — Senegalese canoe slalom Olympian Jean-Pierre Bourhis (31) and Ugandan swimmer Jamila Lunkuse (29) — joined New Zealand tennis bronze medalist Marcus Daniell (36) for a conversation with young athletes.

Moderated by Lefa Makgato, CSR Manager at Samsung Electronics Africa, the session brought the three mentors together with 28 young athletes from 12 countries to share the journeys that shaped them — and offer a guide for exploring where life beyond sport might lead.

Open the Way: Finding Your Own Path

Makgato opened by asking each mentor where their Olympic journey began.

For Bourhis, who represented Senegal at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 and is featured in Samsung’s “Voices of Galaxy: Paddling for the Future,” the dream took shape in 2008, when Togo’s Benjamin Boukpeti won a bronze medal in kayaking at Beijing 2008.

“As a kid, I realized an African paddler could reach the podium,” he said. “Rio 2016 showed me the way could be opened. Now my job is to keep it open for others.”

Lunkuse, who made her Olympic Games debut at 15, recalled that swimming began with friendship rather than ambition. “I wasn’t thinking about medals or the Olympics,” she said. “I just enjoyed being part of something with my friends, and that’s what built my love for the sport.”

Daniell, who ended New Zealand’s 109-year wait for an Olympic tennis medal at Tokyo 2020, pointed to choosing tennis over football at 14. “Because I’d given up a sport I loved, I knew I had to fully commit,” he said.

Break Your Boundaries: Learning Through Challenges

The conversation then turned to the biggest challenges each mentor faced.

With almost no whitewater facilities in Senegal, Bourhis had to build his training base in France — while holding down a full-time job as an engineer in electric vehicle repair. “As an engineer, I see a limit as a problem to solve, not a wall,” he said. “I train before work, during lunch, or late at night. What keeps me going is purpose.”

Lunkuse spoke openly about the anxiety she faced ahead of Rio 2016. “I became so focused on qualifying times that I no longer enjoyed it,” she said. “It was only when I took time away that I could see what I was going through and what help I needed — and that’s what got me to Rio 2016.”

Daniell described a knee injury in 2022 that kept him out for nearly two years. “What got me through was having something bigger than tennis,” he said. “Everyone fails. Those who last are the ones who learn to pick themselves up when they fall.”

Beyond the Game: Turning Experience Into Opportunity

Finally, Makgato asked how the lessons of sport carried into what came next.

Through nonprofit work, Bourhis is building a canoeing ecosystem in Senegal. “We’re building it step by step — and building canoes locally makes the sport more affordable, creates local jobs, and leaves a lasting legacy,” he said. “I want to give the next generation the tools to build their own way.”

Lunkuse, a youth coach and World Aquatics Athletes’ Committee member, urges young athletes to look beyond results. “Results do not define your value,” she said.

Similarly, Daniell — an IOC Athletes’ Commission member and founder of High Impact Athletes, a nonprofit connecting athletes with charities — advised: “Look for a goal beyond personal success. For me, that was what kept pushing me forward.”

Opening Possibilities for the Next Generation

Makgato closed the session with a story of her own. Growing up in a small township in South Africa, she first encountered a computer at 18 — at one of Samsung’s Solar Powered Internet Schools. She later joined Samsung Electronics Africa, where she now leads CSR programs across the continent, including Solve for Tomorrow, giving the next generation the kind of opportunity she once received. Having seen firsthand how a single opportunity can change a life, she had good reason to stand before the young athletes that day.

“I know firsthand how access to technology and education opens doors you may never have imagined. Where you are today doesn’t determine where you’re going,” she said. “We wanted to encourage young athletes to stay open to new ideas and recognize the potential they have to shape their own futures.”

• IOC Athlete Role Models (ARMs) have been part of the Youth Olympic Games since Singapore 2010. Selected by International Federations for each sport, these experienced Olympians stay on site to speak with young athletes and lead workshops on topics such as career management and injury prevention, helping shape the athletes of tomorrow. ↩︎

documents.title: Upgraded Sleep Apnea Feature Now Available on Galaxy Ring Following Regulatory Approvals From US FDA and Korea MFDS - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
Samsung Electronics today announced that its updated Sleep Apnea feature1 is now available on Galaxy Watch and Ring.2 Following United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance in July, the updated feature has also received approval from Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS). With this update, Samsung becomes the first company in the world to bring sleep apnea risk detection on a smart ring.

The updated Sleep Apnea feature, available through the Samsung Health Monitor app, marks a significant leap forward from its predecessor. The enhanced algorithm analyzes a user’s vitals during sleep in greater depth and now provides insight into the level of breathing disruptions detected — going beyond the previous sleep apnea risk assessment to deliver more comprehensive, meaningful information that helps users better understand their condition, which can lead to productive conversations with healthcare professionals.

Most notably, Samsung is extending sleep apnea risk detection to a smart ring for the first time. Galaxy Ring’s comfortable, lightweight design makes it easy to wear through the night and convenient for sleep measurement, encouraging nightly wear. With the feature’s low data requirement, users can gain meaningful insight into their sleep health from as little as two nights of monitoring within a 10-day period. By offering the feature on both Galaxy Watch and Galaxy Ring, Samsung lets users monitor their sleep health in the way that best fits their lifestyle.

Samsung’s original Sleep Apnea feature previously received groundbreaking U.S. FDA De Novo authorization in February, 2024 — the first of its kind for a wearable device designed to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea. Building on that clinically validated reliability, the updated feature has now also been approved by Korea’s MFDS last October. Samsung will continue to expand the feature’s availability so more people around the world can detect possible signs of sleep apnea and take proactive steps toward better sleep health. This underscores Samsung’s dedication to accessible preventive care, with sleep health serving as a fundamental pillar.

“Samsung has long worked to make sleep health a simple and seamless part of everyday life,” said Jongmin Choi, Head of Health R&D Group, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business, Samsung Electronics. “This approval from Korea’s MFDS, along with our introduction of the world’s first support for a smart ring, reflects our commitment to accessible innovation. We are giving people the tools to help spot possible early signs of sleep apnea and take charge of their wellbeing.”

• The Sleep Apnea feature is an over-the-counter (OTC) software-only, mobile medical application operating on a compatible Samsung Galaxy Wearable and Phone. This feature is intended to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea in the form of significant breathing disruptions in users 18 years and older, over a two-night monitoring period. It is intended for on-demand use and requires two nights of valid data within a 10-day period. This feature is not intended for users who have previously been diagnosed with sleep apnea. Users should not use this feature to replace traditional methods of diagnosis and treatment by a qualified clinician. ↩︎

• Available on Galaxy Watch 9 running Wear OS 7.0 or higher. Support for Galaxy Watch 7/8 will expand through future software updates. ↩︎

documents.title: SK hynix Announces 3Q26 Financial Results | SK hynix Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
Seoul, October 28, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today that it has recorded 104.6155 trillion won in revenues, 83.3338 trillion won in operating profit (with an operating margin of 80%), and 39.7756 trillion won in net profit (with a net margin of 38%) in the third quarter.

During the earnings presentation, CEO Kwak Noh-Jung explained the background of the company’s decisions regarding the Solidigm IPO and its principle to share the returns from strategic investment with shareholders.

“The IPO was intended to raise external capital for the expansion of Solidigm’s production facilities, and thereby to lighten our own investment burden and broaden our capacity for shareholder returns,” CEO Kwak said. “However, after carefully considering recent financial market conditions and other factors, we concluded that proceeding at this time would not be the best way to achieve the originally anticipated outcome. We have therefore discontinued our review.”

“Our principle has been to share the majority of the gains from successful strategic investments with our shareholders. These gains help replenish our capacity for shareholder returns, which may temporarily decline as we prepare for the future, allowing us to continue investing boldly in sustainable growth while protecting shareholder interests,” he continued. “In line with this principle, we have decided to return the gains realized from our investment in Kioxia this year to shareholders through a special dividend and we will remain committed to upholding this principle so that our shareholders can directly benefit from the returns from our strategic investments.”

Record quarterly results in both revenue and operating profit and revenue surpasses 100 trillion won for the first time

In a market environment in which prices of key products have risen on the back of growing demand for AI memory, the company once again posted all-time-high quarterly results in both revenue and operating profit, underpinned by the competitiveness of its high-value-added products. In particular, revenue exceeded 100 trillion won for the first time in the company’s history. Revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, from the previous quarter, respectively.

* Q2 2026: Revenue of 79.3187 trillion won, Operating Profit of 60.5426 trillion won

By product, DRAM results were driven by a significant increase in sales of server DDR5 while HBM4 shipments began in earnest. In NAND, sales of 321-layer TLC eSSD expanded, and high-value-added products for data centers continued to grow across the board.

The company’s financial structure has also become significantly concrete. At the end of the third quarter, cash and cash equivalents stood at 114.5 trillion won, up 26.5 trillion won from the end of the previous quarter, while borrowings decreased by 2.8 trillion won to 15.8 trillion won. As a result, net cash increased to 98.7 trillion won.

Memory supply shortage to persist through 2030

SK hynix analyzed that a virtuous cycle has taken hold in which AI-driven productivity gains and new revenue generation in areas such as software development, customer service, and search lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure. It also projected that, as the drivers of AI investment move beyond the early stage, when a small number of companies accounted for most of it, and broaden to include general enterprises and nation-level initiatives, the global AI data center infrastructure market will continue to grow steadily.

The company likewise expects the memory market to sustain its growth, led in the short term by enterprise and personal AI and, over the mid-to-long term, by physical AI such as autonomous driving and robotics.

The company assessed that supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.

Expanding production capacity and strengthening product competitiveness to achieve a further step up in growth next year

Building on these favorable conditions, the company plans to accelerate the expansion of production capacity and the strengthening of product competitiveness in order to sustain the current growth momentum, and to scale up revenue and profit one step further next year.

First, the company plans to rapidly increase the portion of its 10nm-class 6th generation (1c) process technology and expand sales of DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM for AI servers, thereby further strengthening its DRAM portfolio centered on high-value-added products.

To respond to surging HBM demand, the company will ramp up M15X to maximum capacity by the end of the year to increase HBM4 production. Accordingly, the company expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter and to establish itself as a mainstream product.

In NAND, the company will raise the ratio of its 321-layer process to more than half of its domestic production capacity in the fourth quarter, and thereby increase the supply of high-performance, high-capacity eSSD. Over the mid-to-long term, the company intends to develop NAND into a core solution that enhances the throughput and economic efficiency of AI services, based on HBF and system optimization technologies.

Long-term agreements secured for more than 50% of 2027~2028 production capacity and the company to drastically expand investment next year

To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility and solidify its growth foundation, SK hynix is expanding long-term agreements (LTAs) with customers. The company has currently signed LTAs with 14 major customers, including leading global cloud service providers (CSPs), and is also proactively discussing with a number of customers the possibility of extending the contract terms, which are typically five years.

The LTA volume secured to date corresponds to more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. In particular, by introducing a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers, the company has established a structure that secures stable profitability while allowing flexible responses to market changes.

Backed by the demand visibility, the company is also moving to expand its production capabilities. Next year, with the Yongin Phase 1 entering full-scale operation and domestic and overseas infrastructure investment gaining momentum, investment is expected to increase significantly. The company nevertheless plans to adjust the scale and timing of its investment flexibly, after carefully weighing customer demand, product competitiveness, profitability and investment efficiency.

Most of the gains from the Kioxia investment to be shared with shareholders, with approximately 100 trillion won in shareholder returns to be executed this year

As previously indicated in August, SK hynix announced its additional shareholder return plan. For fiscal year 2026, the company will pursue shareholder returns totaling approximately 100 trillion won, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won or more and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won or more in total, including the 40 trillion won announced in August. Through this, the company intends to fulfill its commitment to return 50% or more of free cash flow (FCF). Of this, the 40 trillion won share repurchase announced in August was completed last week, and the shares will be cancelled shortly.

The company also set out its principles: the dividend amount will be determined on the basis of operating results; if significant investment gains arise, they will be returned additionally through special dividends; and share repurchases will continue every quarter.

At today’s meeting, the Board of Directors resolved on a third-quarter cash dividend of 14 trillion won and a share repurchase of 20 trillion won. Of the shares to be repurchased, 10 trillion won, earmarked for shareholder returns, will be cancelled in full, while the remaining approximately 10 trillion won will be used for employee compensation and is not included in the shareholder return total.

The third-quarter dividend is 20,000 won per share, consisting of a 10,000-won dividend reflecting improved earnings and a 10,000 won special dividend that shares the gains from the Kioxia investment. The company has decided to return to shareholders most of the gains realized from its Kioxia investment this year.

“The customer trust built through our technological competitiveness is leading to long-term contracts, and our business structure is transforming into one with earnings stability and mid-to-long term demand visibility,” CEO Kwak emphasized. “We will carry our HBM competitiveness over to next-generation products, and we will also increase the rewards we share with our shareholders as our business outcome and investment result grow.”
