Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work - The Official Microsoft Blog
documents.raw_text:
If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model. And if you want to take advantage of everything that different AI models have to offer, you need a great harness. But building one that works seamlessly across multiple models and surfaces is incredibly hard. You need to solve for performance, quality, and cost. And then you have to maintain it, which is even harder.

Luckily, the GitHub engineering team built a best-in-class, truly multi-model harness, which we’ve adopted company-wide. The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. And today, we’re making that harness available through Microsoft Foundry. That gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. You get the right model for the job without switching the harness or the rest of your tech stack. That frees up your time, energy, and resources to focus on your bottom line.

What’s a harness, and why is it hard?

If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model. It’s the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment, and controls to accomplish meaningful work. And a harness worth its salt has support for open standards like MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins.

This is a fast-moving space. A frontier model today might fall behind tomorrow. And building your own harness or model router to keep up can be painful and slow. Now, you can build on the same harness Microsoft and GitHub ship in our own products, and you don’t have to maintain it.

We invest in science and engineering work to continually improve and evolve the harness and ensure high-quality, efficient, and low-cost performance across a range of models and workloads. The benefits compound for us and our customers who use the harness to build and run their own agents. Improve the harness, and every surface it touches benefits.

Born in GitHub, battle-tested at enterprise scale

The Copilot harness was built by the same GitHub engineers behind new technologies like our multi-model orchestration. And those technologies are only possible because we built our own harness. Designed to be fast, token-efficient, and predictable, it was our original, high-quality harness. And it had the highest satisfaction among our most demanding audience: developers. That’s why we’re standardizing all of our Copilot experiences on the strongest foundation possible.

The harness is built to perform across model families, with 20+ frontier models plus bring your own key, so you can use the right model for the right job. Instead of doing the work to keep up with and eval new models, lean on us to intelligently route work to the right model or models based on the task.

Our harness is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service. We recently ported the harness runtime to Rust, which has resulted in industry-leading performance and reductions in both session overhead and time-to-first token. And because the Copilot harness powers surfaces across Microsoft, it’s battle-tested and proven performant at the scale of millions of users and hundreds of real-world use cases.

A unified harness lets us ship faster, learn faster, and improve Copilot over time. And because the agents you build in Foundry can run on the same harness we’ve adopted across Microsoft, our continuous harness improvements will benefit your agents, too.

Try it yourself

The SDK is available to download, or you can run the harness in the cloud, all managed by Foundry. Our platforms remain open and interoperable, so you can continue to bring in any harness and framework you want, too.

With the Copilot harness, Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance and optimization built in from day one. You bring the instructions, skills, tools, and model choice.

This is an important step towards our vision of a stronger system around the model that preserves choice. It represents the best of GitHub, brought to the Microsoft platform and beyond.

We’ll keep pushing the harness forward, so you can focus on what only you can build.

Tags: GitHub, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry

documents.title: The platform approach to becoming Frontier - The Official Microsoft Blog
documents.raw_text:
Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry.

Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver.

Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites.

Empowering human ambition with Copilot

Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work. Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition.

Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000. Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually, while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers.

KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work. Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily.

At Krafton, Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated. By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions.

To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses.

To transform frontline work, Williams, a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting, while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous. Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier.

Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption, and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows.

Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden. Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations. These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care.

Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence

BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average. Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone.

Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context. This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production, while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected.

To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company, Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x, helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours. By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes.

Kinaxis, a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains. With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change.

Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis. This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions.

To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud, an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights. Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets.

Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees. The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months.

With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring. After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide, TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on.

Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production, the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence.

Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack

To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale. With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities. With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation.

Insight Enterprises, a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale. As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries.

KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI. Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same.

Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization. Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity. That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats.

—

Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination.

Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally.

Text of this article

November 3, 2026

UPDATE

Redesigned Health app expands language support

Today, Apple’s redesigned Health app will expand language support to global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese, bringing powerful, personalized health insights to millions of people worldwide.1 Built with Apple Intelligence at its core, the Health app dynamically adapts to an individual’s health metrics across iPhone and iPad, offering insight into how to optimize their day and a comprehensive view of long-term wellbeing.2, 3 The Health app has been built to securely and privately protect a user’s data at every step.

The updated experience includes a new Insights tab that surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.

To help users better understand their health trajectory, a new Longevity tab analyzes longitudinal metrics across heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement, metabolic health, hearing, and nutrition. Central to this tab is Health Age, a feature that translates data from Apple Watch — including VO2 max, resting heart rate, sleep, and heart rate variability — into a metric that reflects how a user’s body is tracking relative to their chronological age. Users can also incorporate clinical laboratory data, such as A1c and LDL cholesterol, to enrich their long-term health picture.

Additionally, the update introduces at-home movement evaluations, which make physical assessments accessible without requiring specialized equipment. Using an iPhone camera and Apple Watch, users can measure their flexibility, strength, balance, movement mechanics, and VO2 max with real-time audio and visual feedback. Powered by on-device vision-based AI models and developed with clinical experts, the experience runs entirely on device; no video is ever recorded, stored, or shared.

The redesigned Health app is available in the iOS 27.3 developer beta today and will roll out to users as a free software update later this year. Apple will continue to expand support for the redesigned Health app in new languages.

documents.title: Advancing New Entertainment Experiences through Onchain Technology
documents.raw_text:
Tokyo, Japan — Sony Group Corporation ("Sony") today announced the launch of the Sony Onchain Entertainment Incubation Program, a global incubation program for startups and creators, beginning October 29, 2026. Through the program, Sony aims to foster the growth of "onchain entertainment" which leverages blockchain technology to enable more direct connections between creators and fans, as well as new forms of value creation and community building.

Recent advances in blockchain technology are opening new possibilities not only for the ownership and use of content and digital assets, but also for how creators engage with fans and build communities. As a company with diverse entertainment businesses, Sony is working to create next-generation entertainment experiences by leveraging these technologies.

The program will invite creators from around the world that use Soneium, a blockchain, to create new entertainment experiences and business models by bringing together content, communities and digital assets. These may include initiatives that build new relationships between creators and fans, deliver new forms of value through community participation, or explore new revenue opportunities leveraging digital content, among other efforts to explore the potential of onchain technology in entertainment.

Selected projects will receive support toward commercialization, including access to Soneium's technology infrastructure, opportunities for co-creation with Sony Group companies, business development and marketing support, opportunities for community engagement, and access to fundraising opportunities. Through these forms of support, the program aims to help projects move beyond technical validation toward services and experiences that deliver tangible value to users.

Since 2024, Sony has been advancing initiatives in the onchain space centered on Soneium. Through two previous incubation programs, Sony has selected and supported a total of 43 projects from around the world.

Building on the knowledge and networks developed through these initiatives, the new program will focus specifically on onchain entertainment. Through co-creation with creators, startups and communities, Sony aims to foster new entertainment experiences in which people can discover and engage with content, support creators and communities, and share in the value they help create.

Sony Group will continue to explore the possibilities enabled by onchain technology and, through co-creation with innovators around the world, contribute to the future of entertainment by creating value for both creators and fans.

Program Overview

• Program Name Sony Onchain Entertainment Incubation Program

• Organizer Sony Group Corporation

• Program Period Application Period: October 29-December 2026 Selection and Screening: November 2026-March 2027 The schedule is subject to change depending on the number of applications received and the progress of the selection process.

• Support for Selected Projects Selected projects will receive support toward commercialization, including access to Soneium's technology infrastructure, opportunities for co-creation with Sony Group companies, business development and marketing support, opportunities to engage with communities, and access to fundraising opportunities. The specific support provided will be determined in consultation with each selected project based on its individual needs and circumstances.

• Key Areas of Focus Projects developing or planning to develop entertainment-related products or services, including applications and infrastructure.

• Eligibility and Evaluation Criteria Eligibility • Projects developing entertainment-related products or services • Projects that have launched, or plan to launch, on Soneium Evaluation Criteria • Originality of the entertainment experience; use of IP; community building; business scalability; track record; market and competitive landscape; and other relevant factors

Projects with a willingness to integrate or utilize the Soneium blockchain. For more information, please visit the official Sony Onchain Entertainment Incubation Program website.

Broadcom Fixes 89 New Open Source Vulnerabilities in TrueSource Spring Enterprise, Reaching 408 Total in 2026

PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO), a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, today shipped fixes for 89 novel vulnerabilities in TrueSource Spring Enterprise to its critical infrastructure customers and others who qualify for early access, ahead of public disclosure. This brings the total number of vulnerabilities fixed across TrueSource offerings to 408.

Patches only secure an environment once deployed. To close that gap, Spring Enterprise adds TrueSource Hub to help enterprises assess application exposure, prioritize critical fixes, and track status. Additionally, build plugins for Application Advisor automate patching within existing Maven or Gradle workflows, generating update pull requests to streamline merging approved fixes.

A sustained investment in open source security

Building on its June 2026 open source commitment, Broadcom uses Frontier AI scanning and advanced research to find and fix vulnerabilities. TrueSource Spring Enterprise delivers simultaneous fixes across all supported versions, giving legacy releases immediate access, while providing security-only patches for current versions to speed deployment. Detailed vulnerability information will be published when fixes reach the community and CVEs are issued.

Scale & Impact: Reaching a massive footprint of downloads of Spring and Reactor libraries in 2026, Broadcom engineers fixed 406 new vulnerabilities, delivered over 1,090 fixes (including 798 backports), reviewed 2,600+ reports, and filtered out 3,000+ false alarms.

Key High/Critical Broadcom Fixes Earlier This Year:

• Spring (June): Fixed a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-41855, CVSS 8.1) across four supported lines simultaneously.

• Netty Dependency (June): Discovered a DNS redirection vulnerability (CVE-2026-47691, CVSS 10.0) and addressed with the community maintainers and fixed for all supported Spring versions.

• RabbitMQ (July): Fixed a credential forgery vulnerability (CVE-2026-67404, CVSS 9.2) across four supported lines at once.

“Security isn’t a one-time initiative; it’s an ongoing commitment. In June, we pledged to identify and resolve Spring vulnerabilities faster than ever, and today’s release demonstrates our continued momentum,” said Purnima Padmanabhan, general manager, Tanzu Division, Broadcom. “Our customers receive critical fixes early in a deployable format, with complete visibility into where patches belong and confirmation when they land. Crucially, fixes are contributed back to the open source community—because open source remains resilient only when businesses actively invest in ecosystem health.”

See it, prioritize it, fix it, prove it

Most enterprises know they run open source. Few can say exactly which applications run which versions, which are out of support, and which need a fix published this morning. TrueSource Spring Enterprise closes that gap with four capabilities that work together:

• Assess every repository. TrueSource Hub connects to an organization’s code repositories and shows the security state of the open source components every application depends on, across Java, Python, and JavaScript libraries, container images, and data services, along with its patch status, in a live view rather than a one-time audit.

• Prioritize the fixes that matter. When Broadcom publishes a fix, Hub shows which applications need it and how exposed they are, so security and engineering leaders can direct effort to the applications that carry the most risk. TrueSource works with the vulnerability scanners that teams already use. Snyk, for example, is actively partnering with Broadcom so that customers can recognize Broadcom-patched Spring versions as fixed, with the goal of reducing unnecessary alerts and keeping teams from chasing alerts for already-resolved vulnerabilities.

• Apply patches in the build. For Spring applications, Spring Application Advisor plugins integrate directly into existing Maven and Gradle builds. Fixes and version upgrades arrive as reviewable pull requests built on deterministic recipes verified by TrueSource engineers. Additionally, the new integration with JFrog Zero-Touch Remediation delivers instant protection. By automatically delivering verified, backward-compatible TrueSource fixes to builds, security teams can stop waiting on manual pull requests and dependency overrides - keeping software secure with zero friction.

• Prove it through pipeline audits. Every build records its source and the libraries it contains and reports that to TrueSource, so security leaders can show their boards and leadership exactly which libraries shipped and where each fix was applied.

The TrueSource portfolio

TrueSource by Broadcom is Broadcom’s portfolio of enterprise open source software, verified by engineers and delivered from one trusted source. It has three offerings:

• TrueSource Spring Enterprise for the Spring framework Broadcom maintains, with CVE-only patches, the security fix and nothing else, delivered for every supported version at the same time so teams can apply them without an upgrade, plus the tooling announced today.

• TrueSource Trusted Artifacts for verified open source libraries in Java, Python, and JavaScript, and the Secure Images catalog of container images, covering the middleware, runtimes, and backing services applications depend on.

• TrueSource Data Services for the data engines applications rely on: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Valkey, and RabbitMQ, with self-service provisioning, fleet management across environments, and enterprise support for the engines themselves, including prescribed high availability and disaster recovery.

Availability

TrueSource Spring Enterprise, featuring TrueSource Hub and build plugins, is generally available today. Its 87 fixes are accessible immediately to early-access and critical infrastructure customers, with public CVE release to follow. TrueSource Spring Enterprise, Trusted Artifacts, and Data Services are offered via tiered site licensing. Learn more at https://www.broadcom.com/products/software/truesource.

NEW YORK and CHARLOTTE, N.C. and PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) (the "Lead Financial Partners") today announced a $63 billion transaction to enable the deployment of AI compute capacity, leveraging Broadcom Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AVGO) technology, for Anthropic. This transaction is part of the strategic compute capacity agreement previously announced by Broadcom, with expected deliveries starting in calendar 2027.

The transaction will be executed through a newly formed special purpose vehicle ("SPV") with committed financing from the Lead Financial Partners to support the purchase of Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic. The first lien portion of the financing is being arranged by Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, with Blackstone as the sole provider of the committed portion of the second lien financing. Broadcom is providing residual value support to the SPV for the amount equivalent to the first lien portion of the financing. This transaction highlights the deep collaboration across the AI technology and financial ecosystems.

Jon Gray, President and COO, Blackstone, said, "The rapidly growing demand for AI is creating an enormous opportunity to finance compute capacity at scale. We're proud to help advance this buildout with Broadcom."

Dan Simkowitz, Co-President of Morgan Stanley, said, "This transaction represents an important milestone in enabling the next buildout of AI compute capacity. Morgan Stanley has been at the forefront of innovation in designing scalable capital solutions for AI infrastructure, and we are proud to continue to advance new financing structures through this transaction."

Vis Raghavan, Head of Banking and Executive Vice Chair at Citi, said, "Financing AI demands capital solutions at unprecedented scale. Citi is proud to pioneer innovative structures and leverage our global capital markets structuring and distribution expertise to help accelerate the buildout of critical AI infrastructure that will power the future of technology for years to come."

Jim DeMare, Co-President of Bank of America, said, "Advancing AI responsibly requires turning ambitious technology plans into tangible compute infrastructure. Bank of America's infrastructure financing expertise, advisory capabilities and broad capital solutions platform enable us to deliver innovative structures and mobilize institutional capital at scale. This transaction brings together Broadcom's leading technology and significant bank capital to accelerate the buildout of compute capacity that will power the next wave of AI innovation."

Hock Tan, President and CEO of Broadcom Inc., said, "Today's transaction underscores the power of our advanced technology and our strong conviction in the AI ecosystem. Fundamentally, the need for AI compute continues to grow at an extraordinary pace. This validates that there is capital available to finance such growth and that Broadcom is uniquely positioned to enable it."

Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel to Blackstone. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley. Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel to Broadcom, with Evercore serving as financial advisor.

Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) today announced it is increasing its investment in BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) (Euronext Amsterdam: BESI), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, to approximately 20 percent of Besi’s outstanding shares. The share purchase would add to Applied Materials’ current investment in Besi, which Applied initially made in April 2025.

The companies have a longstanding strategic collaboration, which began in 2020 and was recently expanded with Besi joining Applied Materials’ EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The expanded partnership extends the companies’ co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry’s AI-driven scaling roadmap. Areas of collaboration include next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.

“Applied Materials is adding to its investment in Besi as hybrid bonding technology and next-generation interconnect architectures become increasingly critical enablers of energy-efficient AI compute performance,” said Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We also look forward to furthering our strategic collaboration with Besi and delivering the innovative products and technologies our customers need to scale AI systems.”

Applied Materials has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement for the Besi shares, and the delivery of the shares is subject to the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the HSR Act).

Applied Materials views its investment in Besi as long term. Applied currently has no intention to increase its investment in Besi beyond approximately 20 percent, and Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi.

documents.title: Design the Muse App, Just for You
documents.raw_text:
Today, we’re introducing spaces, an interactive way to build a more personalized Muse. A space is a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, like a holiday gift tracker, a daily word game, or a planning board for your next DIY project. It’s shaped around your routines, goals, and interests, and can be as practical or entertaining as you want. Every space you create becomes part of Muse, so you can keep it where you want and come back to it any time.

From An Idea to Something Real

Have an idea you’ve been meaning to try? Tell Muse about it, and it builds it for you. Your initial idea is just the starting point. As you use your space, you can keep adjusting it with Muse, whether that’s adding what’s missing, trying a new look, or changing how it works.

You can also choose where your spaces live in Muse. Add them to your sidebar, move them into your main tabs, hide the ones you don’t need right now, and schedule when they appear. For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday.

What You Can Build

Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home. Here are a few ideas:

• A shopping hub that brings holiday and birthday gift ideas, wishlists from Instagram saves, and your Marketplace listings and buyer messages into one view

• A school dashboard that finds the events relevant to your kids in school emails and adds them to your calendar

• A music tracker for the artists you love, with new releases and upcoming shows

• A wedding planner with your RSVP list, vendor invoices, and to-dos

• A trivia game that quizzes you on your favorite movies, music, or sports team

• A podcast studio to keep your episode ideas, research, and scripts together

• An order tracker for your small business, with new orders, customer messages and what needs to ship today

• A client hub for your freelance work, with projects, deadlines, and invoices

• A trip planner with your flights, hotel, reservations and a day-by-day itinerary.

Got a half-finished idea sitting in your notes app, a spreadsheet you keep meaning to clean up, or a hobby you want to dive into? Chances are you can turn it into a space.

A Space That Keeps Up With You

Your spaces are personal from the start. Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask. You can check things off, add notes, and make edits right in your space, and everything will be there when you return.

Looking Ahead

Starting today, spaces are available everywhere Muse is available. We’re also exploring ways for you to share your spaces with others to build a more collaborative experience in Muse.

We’re also rolling out specialized versions of our models to Muse, trained with learnings from Muse Wonder, to make your overall experience even better.

documents.title: Give Your Muse a Voice
documents.raw_text:
At Connect 2026, we previewed real-time conversations with your Muse. Now we’re rolling it out in the Muse app on mobile, web and on Mac — just tap the phone icon in the top-right corner to start talking.

Talk It Through With Muse

Sometimes it’s easier to think out loud. With voice, you can talk through an idea with your Muse and let it take shape without worrying about the exact prompt.

Planning a trip? Start with the half-baked idea: the city you’ve always wanted to see, the kind of place you’d want to wake up in, the one meal you’d plan the rest of the trip around. Your Muse picks up the thread and works while you talk — on a walk, making dinner, or wherever you are.

Some things are better rehearsed out loud. Prepare for a job interview, run through a presentation, or talk through a pitch — hearing a response and answering in the moment makes it feel more like the real thing.

See Muse Respond in Real Time

As your Muse speaks, the avatar uses subtle expressions and gestures that match the tone of the conversation. It reacts while you talk, so you can tell it’s following along. And you choose how present you want it to be: voice only, the avatar alongside your conversation, or full screen when you want to talk face to face.

Give your Muse a voice with some personality. Want the energy of a New Yorker or the flair of a pirate? With hundreds of voices to choose from, you can pick a style that feels right for your mood and change it whenever you want.

Our Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology lets you have fluid conversations in real time. Speak to your Muse, as you do with real people. Hear responses right away. You can even interrupt if you need to. Wherever the conversation goes, Muse keeps up with you.

What’s Next

Voice and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the Muse app in the US to start. Voice conversations with your Muse are coming soon to AI Glasses and Muse Charm.

documents.title: Arista Networks, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results - Arista

Arista Networks, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

• Delivered total revenues in Q3 2026 of approximately $3.66 billion, exceeding guidance of $3.3 billion while growing 58.5%, the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO.

• In partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, Arista launched open standards-based rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI networks.

• In September 2026, Arista was added to the S&P 100, an index comprised of 100 major blue-chip companies across multiple industry groups.

SANTA CLARA, Calif.- November 3, 2026 -- Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

“Arista registered another momentous quarter with the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO and record profitability, surpassing even my high expectations,” stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. “This strong momentum across customer sectors highlights our increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era.“

Third Quarter Financial Highlights

• Revenue of $3.66 billion, an increase of 20.5% compared to the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of 58.5% from the third quarter of 2025.

• GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.9% and 49.1%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 42.4% and 48.6% in the third quarter of 2025.

• GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.22 and $1.20, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.67 and $0.77 in the third quarter of 2025.

A reconciliation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.

Commenting on the company's financial performance, Chantelle Breithaupt, CFO, said, "This quarter brought a true trifecta for our company, setting new record highs in revenue growth, net income, and EPS. I’m incredibly proud of the Arista team for their hard work in driving such outstanding performance for our shareholders."

Company Highlights

• Arista announced open Ethernet rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics – The new liquid-cooled portfolio leverages Ethernet for Scale-Up Networks (ESUN) and introduces the Etherlink™ SU-144 architecture, supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack in a single hop and scaling up to 1,024 XPUs via cross-rack topologies.

• Arista detailed its scale-across networking strategy for distributed AI fabrics – Highlighting the flagship Arista 7800 AI Spine and unified Arista EOS®, the company outlined how Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) multiplane forwarding, deterministic routing, and real-time congestion signaling enable lossless, high-radix AI fabrics across geographically distributed data centers up to one million XPUs.

• Arista expanded AI-driven software security across its development lifecycle – Collaborating with the likes of Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, Arista embedded domain-specific AI harnesses that accelerate proactive vulnerability discovery, building on the company’s track record of low CVEs and no-downtime upgrades.

Financial Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect:

• Revenue of $3.9 - $4.0 billion;

• Non-GAAP operating margin of 48 - 49%; and

• Non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.26 - $1.30.

Guidance for non-GAAP financial measures excludes certain items, including stock-based compensation expense, intangible asset amortization, tax benefits on stock-based awards, the income tax effect on non-GAAP exclusions, and potential non-recurring charges or benefits. A reconciliation of non-GAAP guidance measures to corresponding GAAP measures is not available on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort because these exclusions can be uncertain or difficult to predict, including stock-based compensation expense and tax benefits on stock-based awards, which are impacted by the timing of employee stock transactions, and the future fair market value of the company’s common stock. The actual amount of these exclusions will have a significant impact on the company's GAAP gross margin, operating margin and diluted net income per share.

Prepared Materials and Conference Call Information

Arista's executives will discuss the third quarter 2026 financial results on a conference call today at 1:30 PM Pacific Time. To listen to the call via telephone, dial (888) 330-2502 in the United States or +1 (240) 789-2713 from international locations. The Conference ID is 5655862.

The financial results conference call will also be available via live webcast on Arista's investor relations website at https://investors.arista.com/. Shortly after the conference call concludes, a replay of the audio webcast will be available on Arista’s investor relations website.

documents.title: Honda Celebrates 50 Years of Motorcycle Production in Brazil and Announces R$ 3.3 Billion Investment | Honda Global Corporate Website
documents.raw_text:
• News Release

Announcement was made in the presence of global and local leadership and reinforces Honda’s confidence in the potential of the Brazilian market

MANAUS, Brazil, November 5, 2026 – Honda today held a ceremony in Manaus, Amazonas state, marking 50 years of motorcycle production in Brazil.

As part of the celebrations for this historic milestone and reaffirming its confidence in the growth potential of the Brazilian market, the company announced a new investment cycle for its motorcycle manufacturing operation in Brazil.

The company will invest BRL 3.3 billion from 2026 to 2030 and expand its annual production capacity to 2.3 million motorcycles by 2029, strengthening the competitiveness of its operations and meeting the growing demand of the Brazilian market. This amount is in addition to the BRL 1.6 billion investment announced last year.

The announcement was made in the presence of Toshihiro Mibe, President, CEO & Representative Director of Honda Motor Co., Ltd.; Keisuke Tsuruzono, President of Honda South America; members of Honda’s global and local leadership teams; and company associates.

The investment comes amid an expanding motorcycle market in Brazil, driven by consumers’ increasing demand for agile, affordable, and efficient mobility solutions. Present in the daily lives of millions of people, Honda motorcycles contribute to income generation, strengthen mobility in both urban and rural areas, expand access to opportunities, and represent independence, leisure, and freedom.

This initiative reinforces Honda’s commitment to the sustainable development of its business and to creating value for customers and business partners.

The Manaus factory, responsible for all Honda motorcycle production in Brazil, plays a central role in the company’s growth story in the country. Over its 50 years of operation, the plant has produced more than 33 million motorcycles, consolidating Honda’s leadership in the segment and its contribution to the development of Brazil’s manufacturing industry.

Expansion of Production Capacity

The investment will enable the construction of two new plants within the manufacturing complex. Each of these new plants will have its own assembly line as well as supporting manufacturing processes. Currently, Honda’s Manaus factory operates four assembly lines distributed across two production plants.

With these investments, installed annual production capacity will reach 2.3 million motorcycles by 2029.

The expansion will also contribute to the region’s economic and social development through the creation of 2,000 new jobs to support increased production.

Honda Motorcycle Operations in Brazil

Under Honda’s global strategy of “producing where there is demand,” the company began manufacturing operations in Brazil in 1976.

Today, the Manaus plant is the most vertically integrated* motorcycle production facility within the Honda Group worldwide, producing approximately 7,200 motorcycles per day.

The facility manufactures 20 models, ranging from 110cc to 1,100cc.

In addition to serving the Brazilian market, the operation exports motorcycles to 19 countries, including the United States, Australia, and Mexico.

Honda employs 9,200 associates directly at the Manaus plant and maintains a state-of-the-art Development and Technology Center responsible for product, process, and manufacturing engineering activities.

The company’s activities also generate positive impacts throughout its value chain. With more than 1,200 dealerships nationwide and over 120 direct suppliers, Honda contributes to economic and social development across different regions of Brazil.

In addition, the company maintains initiatives focused on environmental sustainability, community development, and road safety through investments in industrial eco-efficiency, safety technologies for its products, and rider education programs delivered through Honda Traffic Education Centers (CETH).

Since the beginning of its manufacturing activities in Brazil, Honda has contributed to the sustainable development of the Amazon region. By establishing its factory in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, the company helped drive local industrialization, create qualified jobs, and develop a skilled workforce.

Over the past five decades, Honda has continuously invested in technology, innovation, and professional development, establishing an operation that is recognized globally within the Honda Group.

* A vertically integrated facility is one in which most components of the final product are manufactured in-house. At the Manaus plant, this includes items such as frames, wheels, seats, and engines, ensuring not only vehicle assembly but also the internal production of key components.

Comment from Toshihiro Mibe, President, CEO & Representative Director, Honda Motor Co., Ltd.

“The Manaus factory is one of the core facilities within Honda’s global motorcycle operations, distinguished by its high levels of productivity, quality, and manufacturing efficiency. Reaching this 50-year milestone has only been possible thanks to the tremendous support of our customers and business partners, as well as the dedication and commitment of our associates, to whom I express my sincere gratitude. Honda will continue investing in Brazil’s future, contributing to mobility and economic development in local communities. Building on this strong business foundation and the passion that drives this operation, we will continue advancing Honda’s growth over the next 50 years.”

Comment from Keisuke Tsuruzono, President of Moto Honda da Amazônia Ltda.

“As we celebrate 50 years of motorcycle production in Brazil, I would like to express my gratitude to all those who made this journey possible. The Brazilian market continues to offer significant growth potential. This investment, aimed at expanding the production capacity of the Manaus factory and strengthening its competitiveness, demonstrates our unwavering confidence in the future of Brazil, the Amazon region, and Honda’s business. We will continue striving to provide products and services that exceed our customers’ expectations.”

documents.title: ＜EICMA 2026＞Honda Unveils Its First High-End Electric-Assist Mountain Bike, the Honda RN0 in World Premiere | Honda Global Corporate Website
documents.raw_text:
• News Release

- Combining Honda’s motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technology to deliver a new riding experience -

MILAN, Italy, November 3, 2026 - Honda unveiled its first high-end electric-assist mountain bike (e-MTB), the Honda RN0, at EICMA 2026 (Milan Motorcycle Show; Press days: November 3–4; Public days: November 5–8) in Milan, Italy.

Developed jointly with ROTWILD, a German manufacturer of high-end e-MTBs, the Honda RN0 combines Honda’s extensive motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technologies, which continue to evolve, particularly in Europe.

Weighing approximately 24kg, the lightweight Honda RN0 features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. By combining a highly stable frame with an electronically controlled electric-assist drive unit, the Honda RN0 delivers the fun of riding expected of a next-generation e-MTB. It also combines high pedaling efficiency with excellent terrain-following performance, delivering outstanding riding performance across a wide range of conditions, from technical trails to long-distance rides.

Key features of the Honda RN0

Grand concept

The concept behind the Honda RN0 is “New Terrain, Same Dream.”

“New Terrain” *1 represents Honda’s first venture into the premium e-MTB market and its entry into a new field.

“Same Dream” expresses Honda’s enduring commitment to expanding people’s possibilities and delivering the joy of riding, the spirit of exploration, and the excitement of taking on new challenges, regardless of changes in product categories or the environments in which its products are used.

Naming concept

Honda began researching and developing mountain bikes in the 2000s, and in 2005, its RN01 won the overall series championship in the UCI*2 Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup.

Although Honda did not subsequently introduce another mountain bike to the market, the passion for mountain biking, which was developed through its research and development activities, has been passed down. The Honda RN0 carries this legacy forward into a new model. Its name embodies two ideas: “Ride Natural,” expressing a sense of connection with nature, and “Reach New Peaks,” representing the pursuit of new heights.

Motorcycle-derived chassis construction

The Honda RN0’s most distinctive features are its proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. An efficient structural layout extending from the head tube to the rear axle delivers high rigidity and excellent feedback from the riding surface. This allows riders to intuitively understand terrain conditions and enjoy outstanding stability and control across a variety of surfaces.

The combination of the carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm provides the high rigidity characteristic of motorcycle chassis design, delivering exceptional straight-line stability. At the same time, carefully engineered flexibility allows the frame to deform slightly, improving tire contact with the ground during cornering.

Geometry optimized for all-mountain riding

The Honda RN0 is available in three frame sizes—S, M, and L—to accommodate riders of different builds. The geometry of each size incorporates ROTWILD’s extensive mountain bike development expertise and is optimized for the wide range of riding conditions encountered in all-mountain riding, from steep climbs to descents.

The rear suspension uses a single-pivot swingarm with a linkage system. This configuration minimizes unwanted suspension movement during pedaling while allowing the suspension to respond smoothly to impacts from the terrain, achieving an effective balance between pedaling efficiency and shock absorption.

Color scheme

The frame features a two-tone color scheme combining Pearl Moon Ash Gray and Mat Ballistic Black Metallic. The premium finish gives the Honda RN0 a distinctive presence, even against the backdrop of natural outdoor environments.

Premium chassis package

The Honda RN0 is equipped with industry-leading components.

The front suspension features a FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima fork with 160mm of travel, while the rear suspension uses a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima shock.

The front and rear wheels are DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE units designed specifically for e-MTBs. A mullet configuration*3, combining a 29-inch front wheel with a 27.5-inch rear wheel, delivers an outstanding balance of stability and agility.

Schwalbe Albert EVO Trail tires and SHIMANO DEORE XT four-piston disc brakes provide excellent grip and braking performance across a wide range of terrain conditions.

Next-generation SHIMANO drive system

The Honda RN0 features a new SHIMANO drive unit. Despite weighing just 2.3kg, the lightweight unit delivers a maximum torque of 100Nm and maximum output of 750W, supported by a 720Wh battery. It provides powerful assistance across a broad range of riding conditions, from steep climbs to high-speed trails.

The AUTO ASSIST function automatically adjusts the level of assistance according to the gradient of the terrain and the rider’s pedaling effort.

The AUTO SHIFT function automatically changes gears to maintain an optimal cadence,*4 allowing riders to concentrate on the trail ahead.

In addition, the Assist Carryover function smoothly maintains drive power for a short period after the rider stops pedaling, helping the motorcycle maintain momentum when negotiating obstacles and other challenging terrain.

User interface

A 2.2-inch full-color display is integrated into the top tube, providing clear information on speed, remaining range, assist mode, and other riding data. The system also supports device charging through a USB-C port. Integration with the SHIMANO app allows riders to customize the SHIMANO drive unit’s settings and lock or unlock the bike’s electronic systems.

Since its founding, Honda has supported people’s mobility and their pursuit of new challenges through a wide range of products and technologies, including the Honda A-Type, which combined a bicycle with an auxiliary engine, the Honda Racoon series of electric-assist bicycles, and the RN01 mountain bike developed exclusively for downhill racing.

The Honda RN0 represents a new challenge that builds on this history.

Honda aims to achieve carbon neutrality across all products and corporate activities in which it is involved by 2050 and is advancing electrification in its motorcycle business. Going forward, Honda will continue to deliver the joy and freedom of mobility to more people through products that meet increasingly diverse customer needs, while contributing to the realization of a carbon-neutral society.

*1 “Terrain” refers to a field or area of activity.

*2 UCI: Union Cycliste Internationale (International Cycling Union).

*3 A bicycle configuration that uses different wheel sizes at the front and rear.

*4 The number of pedal revolutions per minute.

Boeing and Avolon today announced the lessor finalized its purchase of 140 737-10 airplanes, a record 737 MAX order by a lessor that increases Avolon’s backlog to more than 240 unfilled orders.

• Record single-aisle purchase by a lessor raises Avolon's 737 MAX backlog to more than 240 airplanes

• Large single-aisle jets like the 737-10 are the fastest-growing segment of commercial aviation

SEATTLE, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boeing [NYSE: BA] and Avolon today announced the lessor finalized its purchase of 140 737-10 airplanes, a record 737 MAX order by a lessor that increases Avolon's backlog to more than 240 unfilled orders.

Lessors have placed firm orders for more than 230 737-10 airplanes in 2026, five times more than the lessor backlog for the largest 737 MAX variant at the end of 2025.

With the 737-10, Avolon can meet strong market demand for larger single-aisle jets and leverage the versatility of the 737 family.

"We continue to see strong demand for new technology aircraft, and this order further strengthens our long-term delivery pipeline. The 737-10 combines outstanding economics with the capacity airlines increasingly require, making it one of the most attractive aircraft in its class," said Avolon CEO Andy Cronin. "This agreement enhances our ability to support airline growth and fleet renewal well into the next decade, while further strengthening our long-standing partnership with Boeing."

The 737, with a large customer base and low operating costs, is a cornerstone of most lessors' portfolios, representing approximately 30% of all financed airplanes.

"Avolon's growing and diverse 737 MAX portfolio enables its airline customers to modernize fleets with aircraft that reduce emissions and operating costs, improve route economics and support long-term sustainability goals," said Brad McMullen, Boeing senior vice president of Commercial Sales and Marketing. "As long-term travel demand is expected to remain strong, we stand ready to support lessors expanding their single-aisle portfolios with fuel-efficient jets that can operate across diverse route networks."

The 737-10 offers the best per-seat economics of any single-aisle airplane. It can seat up to 230 passengers and has a range of 3,100 nautical miles (5,740 kilometers).

Projected 4% annual passenger traffic growth over the next 20 years is driving lessors to broaden single‑aisle offerings. Lessors have ordered more than 1,450 737 MAX airplanes, about 20% of Boeing's backlog.

documents.title: Boeing: Travel Demand Propels Middle East Fleet to Double by 2045
documents.raw_text:
• Middle East commercial fleet will double to more than 3,500 airplanes to support air traffic growth

• Widebody jets comprise almost half of the nearly 3,000 projected new airplane deliveries for fleet growth and renewal

• Fleet growth will drive $475 billion investment in commercial aviation services

DOHA, Qatar, November 3, 2026 — Passenger traffic in the Middle East is forecast to grow 4.3% annually despite current industry headwinds, supporting trade, tourism and commerce across the region over the next 20 years, according to Boeing’s [NYSE: BA] 2026 Commercial Market Outlook. The region’s airplane fleet is projected to double to more than 3,500 airplanes to support twice the travel demand, underscoring the aviation sector’s continued resilience.

Airlines in the Middle East are expected to take delivery of nearly 3,000 new airplanes over the next two decades to support fleet expansion and replace older airplanes. Around 85% of the Middle East fleet in 2045 will consist of modern, fuel-efficient airplanes delivered over the next 20 years.

“The Middle East has long established itself as one of the world’s most important aviation crossroads, connecting people and economies throughout Asia, Africa and Europe,” said Shahab Matin, Boeing managing director of Commercial Marketing, Middle East and Africa. “The region’s airlines have proven to be resilient and continue to adapt as conditions evolve. Carriers have ambitious long-term growth plans supported by strong demand fundamentals, modern fleets and continued investment in aviation infrastructure.”

The Middle East’s share of global passenger traffic is double the region’s share of the world’s population, reflecting the scale of Middle East carriers’ long-haul networks. The Middle East region is forecast to see nearly 6% growth on major Asia routes over the next two decades and triple the 2025 volumes by 2045.

Widebody airplanes remain central to region’s growth Boeing forecasts demand for 1,370 new widebody airplanes in the Middle East, representing nearly half of the region’s new airplane deliveries through 2045. This share of widebody jet deliveries is the highest of any region and more than double the global average.

The region will also require 1,505 single-aisle airplanes to support short- and medium-haul network growth. Single-aisle airplanes will continue to support year-round point-to-point service and strengthen domestic and intra-regional connectivity. As Middle East economies diversify and tourism grows, demand for more frequent and flexible travel options is expected to support continued growth for low-cost carriers and single-aisle operators.

Air cargo growth supports regional trade and logistics Middle East carriers transport roughly 15% of international cargo. Over the next two decades, carriers in the region are forecast to double their share of the global large widebody freighter fleet from less than 10% to nearly 20%, requiring 120 new widebody freighter deliveries to support diversifying global supply chains and growing e-commerce demand.​

Commercial aviation services: A $475 billion opportunity Over the next 20 years, airlines in the Middle East will invest $475 billion in digital services improvements, airplane maintenance and personnel training to improve productivity and capability. The region’s aviation services market is projected to grow at approximately 4% annually, reinforcing the need for continued investment in maintenance capacity, aftermarket infrastructure, digital technologies and operational support.

Building talent pipelines to support Middle East aviation Boeing projects the Middle East aviation sector will require 236,000 new aviation professionals through 2045, including:

• 67,000 pilots

• 65,000 technicians

• 104,000 cabin crew

Developing a growing workforce will require continued collaboration among airlines, training providers, universities, governments and the wider aerospace industry to expand training capacity and create pathways into aviation careers.

Boeing’s Commercial Market Outlook is an annual forecast published since 1961 that provides 20-year demand projections for airplanes and services worldwide. The 2026 Commercial Market Outlook projects demand for nearly 44,000 new airplanes, with the worldwide commercial fleet expected to grow by nearly 80% to exceed 50,000 airplanes by 2045.

STRATFORD, Conn., Nov. 6, 2026 – Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company (NYSE: LMT), has been selected to deliver the S-92A+™ helicopter, the next-generation variant of its S-92® helicopter, to the Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) for its Presidential Helicopter II program.

Lockheed Martin and Sikorsky's partnership with the Republic of Korea spans more than 70 years, including Black Hawk, Seahawk and S-92 helicopter programs. Since taking delivery of three S-92 helicopters in 2007, the ROKAF has relied on the platform for nearly two decades of safe and reliable presidential transport. S-92 helicopters have also supported Korea Coast Guard search and rescue operations, along with firefighting and other lifesaving missions for South Korea's National 119 Rescue Headquarters, part of the country's National Fire Agency.

For the new presidential fleet, Korea Aviation Engineering & Maintenance Service (KAEMS), a subsidiary of Korea Aerospace Industries, will perform in-country mission equipment completion for the S-92A+ helicopters. The contract also includes additional special mission equipment and sustainment support, including critical spare parts and field service representation.

“We are deeply honored that the S-92A+ has been selected as the Republic of Korea’s presidential helicopter. Building on the Republic of Korea Air Force’s long-term experience operating the S-92A, we are confident the S-92A+ will continue supporting this critical mission with the highest standards of safety and reliability,” said Wonik Lee, South Korea country executive for Lockheed Martin. “The S-92 platform’s shared heritage in presidential transport across the Republic of Korea, the United States and other nations makes this selection especially meaningful. Together with Korean aerospace partner KAEMS’ participation in the program, this milestone reflects Lockheed Martin’s longstanding commitment to the ROK-U.S. alliance, national defense and defense industry cooperation.”

S-92A+ Advances Proven Aircraft

For head-of-state and VIP transport, the S-92 combines best-in-class safety and reliability with long-range, all-weather capability and a spacious, quiet cabin tailored for executive travel. The S-92A+ builds on these proven strengths with upgraded engines, a new Phase IV main gearbox and increased payload or fuel capacity to enhance performance and mission flexibility.

With more than 2.6 million fleet flight hours, an average lifetime availability rate of over 90% and more than 300 aircraft delivered across 28 countries, the S-92 supports head-of-state and VIP transport, offshore energy and search and rescue missions. The platform also serves as the foundation for the U.S. Marine Corps' VH-92A Patriot® presidential helicopter, continuing Sikorsky's legacy of transporting every U.S. president since 1957.

Sikorsky is ramping up S-92A+ production at its facilities in Stratford, Connecticut, and Owego, New York, with capacity to produce up to 12 aircraft annually. These efforts reflect Sikorsky's continued commitment to modernizing the S-92 platform and supporting its global customer fleet today and into the future.

For more information about the S-92 helicopter, visit http://www.lockheedmartin.com/S-92

BETHESDA, Md., Oct. 30, 2026 – Lockheed Martin (NYSE: LMT) today announced new and expanded partnerships with organizations across the country as part of 25Forward, the company’s five-year, $25 million initiative commemorating the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks.

Through partnerships with 11 organizations, 25Forward will safeguard stories and lessons of Sept. 11, as well as military service; serve survivors, first responders, veterans and military families; and sustain a spirit of service and preparedness by expanding opportunities for education, volunteerism and disaster readiness.

“These new partnerships mark an important next step for 25Forward and our commitment to those who serve and strengthen communities across the country,” said Stuart Holliday, Lockheed Martin senior vice president and chief public affairs officer. “By investing in these organizations, we are extending their reach and lasting impact.”

Through 25Forward, Lockheed Martin is partnering with the following organizations:

• 9/11 Day turns the anniversary of Sept. 11 into a nationwide day of service, honoring those lost by uniting people together to help others.

• Air Commando Heritage Foundation will preserve and share Air Force Special Operations history to educate visitors and honor those who served.

• Conservation Legacy creates conservation service and career opportunities, including pathways for veterans through its Veteran Fire Corps.

• FDNY Foundation supports New York City firefighters, EMS members and their families while advancing fire-safety education and programs that strengthen the FDNY.

• Friends of Flight 93 National Memorial supports preservation of the memorial and shares the stories of Flight 93’s passengers and crew.

• Gary Sinise Foundation supports military service members, veterans, first responders and their families by building custom homes for our nation’s most severely wounded heroes, providing first responder equipment, serving appreciation meals, supporting the families of our fallen and more.

• National Cold War Center will interpret and share the history and legacy of the Cold War through an immersive educational experience.

• Pentagon Memorial Fund preserves the memory of those lost at the Pentagon on Sept. 11 and will help educate future generations through the planned Visitor Education Center.

• Scholarship America provides postsecondary scholarships to eligible dependents of people killed or permanently disabled as a result of the Sept. 11 attacks through its Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund.

• Soldiers’ Angels provides aid, comfort and resources to service members, veterans and military families.

• Team Rubicon brings veterans and volunteers together to help communities prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters.

Lockheed Martin launched 25Forward in September with a $10 million contribution to the Pentagon Memorial Visitor Education Center. Over the next five years, the initiative will preserve history, support those impacted by Sept. 11 and advance a lasting legacy of service.
