documents.title: Schneider Electric launches Energy Tech Accelerator to build AI-ready talent for the energy transitionSchneider Electric launches Energy Tech Accelerator to build AI-ready talent for the energy transition
documents.raw_text:
Rueil-Malmaison, France

02/11/2026

• New flagship global early-career program combines engineering, AI and real-world energy challenges

• Inaugural cohort of 50 will complete two six-month rotations, supported by learning, mentoring and customer exposure

• Applications open November 2

Schneider Electric, a global energy technology leader, today launched Energy Tech Accelerator, a 12-month global early-career program that will recruit an inaugural cohort of 50 participants across five global hubs, Boston, Paris and Grenoble, Dubai, Bangalore, and Shanghai, to work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, engineering and sustainable energy. Participants will work on meaningful business and customer challenges while gaining dedicated learning, mentoring, customer exposure and opportunities to build a connected global community.

“At Schneider, our goal is to Advance Energy Tech to the next level to deliver greater business outcomes for our customers. By leveraging Data & AI, we connect the physical and digital worlds to deliver Energy & Industrial Intelligence to our Customers,” said Olivier Blum, chief executive officer of Schneider Electric. “Turning that intelligence into solutions that help our customers operate more efficiently and sustainably requires people who can combine deep knowledge of energy and industrial processes with AI. That is why we are launching Energy Tech Accelerator: to attract and develop people who understand AI, are passionate about the energy transition and want to make a tangible contribution to a more sustainable future.”

Energy Tech Accelerator is part of Schneider Electric’s investment in the workforce capabilities needed as energy systems become more digital and connected. The program gives emerging talent responsibility and practical experience from the start.

“Advancing energy technology is ultimately about people,” said Charise Le, chief human resources officer of Schneider Electric. “Early-career talent should not have to wait years to make a meaningful contribution. Through Energy Tech Accelerator, participants will learn across the business, take on real challenges and build the capabilities and confidence to help shape a more sustainable energy future.”

The program is designed for curious, analytical and globally minded early-career engineers who are excited by AI, digital technology and sustainable transformation. Applications open Nov. 2. Candidates can learn more and apply at Energy Tech Accelerator Graduate Program.

documents.title: Schneider Electric, Nscale and Start Campus Bring the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint into a Live AI Factory EnvironmentSchneider Electric, Nscale and Start Campus Bring the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint into a Live AI Factory Environment | Schneider Electric
documents.raw_text:
Berlin, Germany

22/10/2026

• Built using the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, the Immersive Twin pilot connects Schneider Electric, AVEVA, and ETAP technology in one digital platform

• Digital twin connects AI workload requirements with power, cooling, electrical, and operational models to accelerate AI Factory deployment and improve token efficiency

• Pilot at Start Campus’ Sines data center campus is expected to optimize operations for Nscale

Global energy technology leader Schneider Electric, industrial software leader AVEVA, full-stack AI cloud platform Nscale, and data center developer and operator Start Campus, today announced the successful pilot of an end-to-end digital twin developed using the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, part of NVIDIA DSX Sim.

The Immersive Twin pilot marks a significant step toward bringing Schneider Electric’s digital twin technology, powered by AVEVA software, into real-world AI infrastructure, allowing Nscale to accelerate token production and optimize token efficiency.

The deployment is focused on Nscale’s operations within the SIN01 data center on the 1.2 GW SINES Data Campus in Portugal, developed by Start Campus. As one of Europe’s largest and most sustainable AI factories, the SINES Data Campus is designed to support successive generations of AI infrastructure. It will soon become home to more than 66,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, representing one of the largest AI deployments in the region. By combining engineering and operational data with advanced power and cooling simulations and workload requirements, the new Schneider Electric and AVEVA Immersive Twin provides a unified view of data center performance to help identify opportunities to optimize infrastructure before changes are implemented on-site.

Using the digital twin, Nscale expects to achieve faster time to token, greater token efficiency, enhanced operations, increased flexibility, and reduced risk when updating or modifying its technology stack.

"Working with Start Campus, Schneider Electric and NVIDIA, we’re using digital twins to model how AI data centers operate in the real world — from power and cooling to token delivery,” said David Power, Chief Technology Officer at Nscale. “This gives us a clearer view of where full-stack optimizations can be realized before changes are made on the ground. It’s about using intelligence and simulation to build and operate AI infrastructure more efficiently, and sustainably at scale.”

Complete End-to-End Experience and Collaboration

The successful pilot reflects the strength of a collaborative, end-to-end approach, bringing together complementary expertise from across the AI ecosystem, including energy management, engineering, simulation and AI infrastructure operations to create a more complete view of data center performance.

The Immersive Twin pilot supports the full lifecycle of AI factories—from design through operations—by building an OpenUSD-based digital twin that connects Schneider Electric, ETAP, AVEVA, and third-party technologies. It enables rapid “what-if” scenario testing across power, cooling, and process behavior to validate design decisions, assess upgrade impacts, reduce procurement risk, and continuously optimize performance by linking IT and OT data. In parallel, it advances interoperability through simulation-ready asset files, accelerating seamless integration into digital twins.

Start Campus provides the real-world infrastructure, engineering expertise and operational environment to demonstrate how digital twin technology can transform the design, development and operation of AI data centers. Bringing this data, technology and expertise together enables Nscale to use the digital twin to model and test “what-if scenarios” for new configurations or technologies before implementation, speeding up deployment times while significantly reducing risk.

“Building a credible, end-to-end digital twin requires collaboration across the AI ecosystem,” said Pankaj Sharma, Executive Vice President, Software & Service with Schneider Electric. “By advancing energy tech, and connecting Nscale’s workload and IT infrastructure requirements with Start Campus’s physical facility and infrastructure data, while pairing it with Schneider’s digital twin technology, we’re bringing together critical perspectives needed to model AI factories more holistically and identify opportunities to optimize performance, efficiency and token production.”

"AI infrastructure needs to evolve as quickly as the technology it supports,” added Robert Dunn, Chief Executive Officer at Start Campus. “Our collaboration with Schneider Electric, Nscale and NVIDIA has taught us that operators and customers design, develop and operate data centers best when they work from the same model. By using digital twin technology to simulate how a jump in rack density moves through the power train and the liquid cooling loop before it becomes a physical reality, we can test new hardware generations, agree the configuration with our customer and build it once. That accelerates deployment, improves efficiency and maximizes the value of every megawatt. This is an important step towards delivering resilient AI infrastructure at scale."

Building on Existing Collaboration

This latest pilot expands Schneider Electric, AVEVA and ETAP’s work with NVIDIA. Last year, the three companies joined the Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD) to accelerate digital twin and AI factory development through the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint.

Additionally, the companies continue to collaborate on reference architectures, integrated infrastructure and software solutions that will power and cool the next generation of AI factories, and use NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate and improve energy efficiency in real-world environments.

###

He believes that the next wave of innovation will not be defined by better AI models alone, but by how effectively we connect AI, software and services to the way energy is managed. With responsible AI governance as a foundation, this is where intelligence becomes impact, turning operational data into measurable improvements in energy efficiency, resilience and sustainability. Building on a legacy of AI-ready infrastructure Prior to his current role, Pankaj led Schneider's Global Secure Power & Data Centers and Services businesses. Under his leadership, the Secure Power & Data Center business more than doubled in scale, strengthening Schneider’s position in efficient, resilient, AI-ready digital infrastructure. He also transformed the Global Services business, helping customers unlock greater value across the lifecycle of their operations through predictive and prescriptive analytics and remote expertise. This experience continues to shape Pankaj's work on energy intelligence today: Schneider recently collaborated with NVIDIA, Nscale, and Start Campus to develop an industry-first immersive twin for AI factories. documents.title: GE Vernova to support India’s energy transition with 6 GW HVDC transmission project
documents.raw_text:
• Project will facilitate the transmission of 6 GW of clean power from the renewable energy zone in Barmer, Rajasthan, to support national energy demand.

Project will facilitate the transmission of 6 GW of clean power from the renewable energy zone in Barmer, Rajasthan, to support national energy demand.

• The project was booked in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The project was booked in the fourth quarter of 2026.

• Reinforces GE Vernova’s commitment to modernizing India’s power system, ensuring greater stability and efficiency for the national grid.

Reinforces GE Vernova’s commitment to modernizing India’s power system, ensuring greater stability and efficiency for the national grid.

NEW DELHI (6 November 2026) – GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) today announced it has been officially chosen by PowerGrid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) to deliver a critical 6 GW High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission corridor. The project was booked in the fourth quarter of 2026.

This project will serve as a vital energy highway, enabling the efficient transport of 6 GW of power from the renewable energy-rich region of Barmer, Rajasthan, to the load center in South Kalamb.

By connecting remote renewable energy zones to the national network, this 800 kV project aims to provide the infrastructure needed to stabilize power flow for millions of homes and businesses. As India’s electricity demand continues to grow, this high-capacity link is essential to ensuring that the country’s grid remains reliable and resilient while supporting its decarbonization goals.

“India is at the forefront of the global energy transition, characterized by an unprecedented scale of renewable integration and rapidly evolving grid requirements,” said Philippe Piron, President and CEO of GE Vernova’s Electrification Segment. “This project represents more than just transmission capacity; it is an investment in the reliability and future-proofing of India’s power system. We are proud to work with PGCIL to deploy the advanced technology required to bridge the gap between renewable energy production and national consumption, ensuring long-term system performance.”

"As India accelerates its renewable energy journey, the development of robust, high-capacity transmission infrastructure is paramount,” said Sandeep Zanzaria, CEO & Managing Director at GE Vernova, T&D India. “The Barmer–South Kalamb HVDC corridor is a strategic project for PGCIL, designed to efficiently integrate large-scale renewable capacity from Rajasthan into the national grid. By leveraging advanced transmission technologies, we are strengthening the backbone of India’s power system, ensuring reliable, high-quality electricity reaches consumers across the country while supporting our national commitment to a sustainable and resilient energy future."

GE Vernova will deliver the complete design for the ±800 kV, 6,000 MW (2x3000 MW) bipolar HVDC link between Barmer II and South Kalamb. The project scope encompasses the creation of new converter stations, the supply of all major equipment, and the full management of site erection, testing, and commissioning. By overseeing the end-to-end delivery of this link, GE Vernova ensures a synchronized approach that prioritizes grid stability and system efficiency, suitable for large scale renewable energy links such as Barmer.

The project will feature GE Vernova’s most advanced LCC (Line Commutated Converter) valve, which will be manufactured at the Pallavaram factory in India. It will also include the eLumina™ control system which provides the digital intelligence required to manage complex power flows, enabling the grid to respond dynamically to changing conditions.

This collaboration further strengthens GE Vernova’s long-standing relationship with PGCIL, reinforcing a shared vision of a modernized, resilient, and decarbonized power grid for the future.

documents.raw_text:
• Event marks the start of a three-year initiative to inspire the next generation of energy leaders in the Upstate

Event marks the start of a three-year initiative to inspire the next generation of energy leaders in the Upstate

GREENVILLE, S.C. – November 2, 2026 – The GE Vernova Foundation today celebrated the official launch of Engineers of Change in Greenville, with the first students beginning programming this fall. The launch event brought together GE Vernova leadership, local government officials, Clemson University partners, and community leaders to highlight the program’s role in creating a pipeline for future innovators who will build a more sustainable energy future.

First announced in April 2026, Engineers of Change is a three-year, $4.5 million initiative in two locations – Greenville, South Carolina and Staffordshire, UK. In Greenville alone, the program aims to reach 3,000 students. By bringing engineering to life through hands-on learning, real-world design challenges, and direct mentorship from industry professionals, the program aims to ignite curiosity and confidence in students ages 13–18.

“Meeting the world’s growing energy needs will require not only breakthrough technology, but people — bold thinkers, problem-solvers, and next-generation leaders,” said Kristin Carvell, President, GE Vernova Foundation and Chief Communications Officer, GE Vernova. “Our goal with Engineers of Change is to teach young people in Greenville more about this exciting career path and the purpose and impact that comes along with it and inspire them to pursue a career in engineering.”

The launch event at the Advanced Manufacturing Works (AMW) facility featured a panel discussion with industry experts and educators, as well as live engineering demonstrations.

The program focuses on two core components:

• Engineering Spark: Introduces students ages 13–14 to foundational engineering concepts through dynamic, hands-on learning.

• Engineering Catalyst: An immersive, two-year program for students ages 15–18 featuring design challenges and career readiness workshops designed to equip students with the skills to pursue engineering.

“The GE Vernova Foundation has been a dedicated partner in expanding opportunity and connecting education to the workforce needs of our communities,” said Ben Ayers, President of Clemson University. “Engineers of Change puts that partnership into action by giving young people in the Upstate hands-on experiences, mentorship and a clear view of the opportunities available to them in engineering and energy. We are grateful for the GE Vernova Foundation’s continued investment and, as the program’s first university partner in the United States, proud that Clemson is helping prepare the next generation of innovators and problem-solvers.”

Engineers of Change is delivered in collaboration with Clemson University’s PEER program and the global nonprofit FHI 360, ensuring that programming is aligned with local workforce needs. Through this collaboration, the GE Vernova Foundation continues to put its purpose, The Energy to Change the World, into practice.

“We are proud to see Engineers of Change take root here in Greenville,” said Mayor Knox White. “This partnership creates a unique pathway for our students, providing them with the practical skills and encouragement to pursue engineering as a mission-driven career that can change the world.”

GE Vernova and the GE Vernova Foundation continue to invest heavily in the future of Greenville, driving impact through both education and community-building. Since 2021, the company and the Foundation have together granted nearly 300 scholarships—including the John Lammas Annual Scholarship for engineering students and GE Vernova STAR Scholarships supporting employees' children—while also funding skilled trades and technical programs, such as granting $100,000 for Future of Energy Skills scholarships in Greenville.

Additionally, the 2026 opening of the GE Vernova Park in Greenville marked a major milestone in creating vibrant, connected communities. Serving as the home pitch for Greenville Triumph SC and Greenville Liberty SC, the venue welcomed over 45,000 fans in its inaugural season while doubling as a year-round hub for soccer clinics, yoga, and World Cup watch parties. Through shared volunteer efforts like Hands On Greenville Day and programs like the Triumph's "Read to Score" initiative—which rewarded 2,703 students for literacy—GE Vernova is proud to invest in the social, physical, and educational well-being of the Upstate region.

Learn more about Engineers of Change.

About GE Vernova Foundation

The GE Vernova Foundation, an independent charitable organization funded by GE Vernova, puts the company’s purpose – The Energy to Change the World – into practice across the global communities where employees live and work. Building on the 100+ year legacy of the GE Foundation, the GE Vernova Foundation is prioritizing employees through programs such as Matching Gifts and STAR Awards. The Foundation’s resources are also channeled into initiatives focused on championing the global workforce needed for the energy transition as well as building stronger and more resilient communities.

About GE Vernova

GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE: GEV) is a purpose-built global energy company that includes Power, Electrification and Wind segments and is supported by its accelerator businesses. Building on over 130 years of experience tackling the world’s challenges, GE Vernova is uniquely positioned to help lead the energy transition by continuing to electrify the world while simultaneously working to decarbonize it. GE Vernova helps customers power economies and deliver electricity that is vital to health, safety, security, and improved quality of life. GE Vernova is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, U.S., with approximately 85,000 employees across approximately 100 countries around the world. Supported by the Company’s purpose, The Energy to Change the World, GE Vernova technology helps deliver a more affordable, reliable, sustainable, and secure energy future.

About FHI 360

FHI360 is a global organization that mobilizes research, resources and relationships so people everywhere have access to the opportunities they need to lead full and healthy lives. With collaborations in over 60 countries, we work directly with local leaders to improve health and well-being, respond to humanitarian crises and strengthen community resilience. We share data-driven insights and scalable tools so communities can effectively address complex challenges and achieve thriving futures.

About Clemson University

Clemson University is a public, land-grant-ranked research university located in Upstate South Carolina. Established in 1889, Clemson is dedicated to teaching, research and public service—serving as a catalyst for economic growth, scientific discovery, and

student development. The university comprises nine colleges offering a wide array of undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs within a vibrant campus community.
